tasks.label: Replace or refurbish upholstery of items, using tacks, adhesives, softeners, solvents, stains, or polish.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a furniture repair/refinishing shop: refurbishing existing leather or vinyl upholstery on a chair or sofa — cleaning with solvents, applying softener/conditioner, filling and blending re-dye/stain on worn bolsters and scuffs, then buffing and polishing to match surrounding original color and sheen.

In the shop: replacing the cover on drop-in/slip seats of dining or side chairs — prying out old tacks and staples, removing the worn fabric, cutting new material to the seat pattern, stretching it over the pad, tacking/stapling the edges and trimming the excess.

In the shop: partial or full reupholstery of a used or antique armchair/settee — stripping to the frame, replacing webbing and padding, cutting and fitting cover pieces to a one-off frame, tacking, and gluing gimp/trim with adhesive before final finish touch-up.

On site at a customer's home, office or showroom: touch-up refurbishment of upholstery on a delivered or in-service piece — regluing loose trim or a lifted panel, spot-dyeing a scuff on leather, applying softener and polish, working around household furnishings without a shop setup.

In a furniture manufacturing plant: covering new components on a production run — stretching fabric/lining over seat panels or pads, stapling or tacking the edges, trimming excess, and gluing fabric or trim in place, repeated across identical parts to a plant quality standard.

tasks.label: Design, create, and decorate entire pieces or specific parts of furniture, such as draws for cabinets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Custom/restoration shop: make a replacement or new specific part for an existing piece — most often a drawer box (also a door, panel or molding). Worker takes dimensions off the case, mills stock, cuts joinery (dovetails/dados/grooves), assembles and glues the box, fits it to the opening, then sands and finishes it. Shop with standard machinery, bench and spray booth.

Finishing room/spray booth: decorate a whole piece or a set of parts with a specified sprayed decorative finish — sealer, stain/dye, shading and toning, colored lacquer or paint, topcoat — matched to a customer sample or company standard, then rubbed out and inspected.

Furniture/cabinet plant: create and decorate standardized parts in runs — drawer fronts, doors and panels sanded, edge-treated, printed/embossed or roller/spray coated with a decorative wood-grain or color decor to a specified surface standard, on a line with conveyors and staging carts.

One-off hand decoration on an assembled piece: gold or metal leaf, hand-painted motifs and striping, faux bois graining and marbling, hand-wiped glaze/antiquing into carvings and corners, marquetry/inlay banding or hand-carved detail — judged by eye against an original or a designer's sample.

Bespoke design-and-build from a customer brief: discuss the piece, sketch and dimension it, choose species/veneer/hardware and finish, build the case and its drawers, fit hardware, finish and deliver, with revisions after the customer sees a sample or the piece in progress.

On-site at a client's home, office or historic interior: create or decorate a part in place — fit a made-to-measure drawer or shelf to an installed built-in, replace a broken element, or blend decorative graining/color into an installed piece, working around furnishings, floors and occupants.

tasks.label: Spread graining ink over metal portions of furniture to simulate wood-grain finish.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Furniture plant finishing department: a finisher grains the metal portions of new production furniture (steel office furniture panels, tubular chair/table frames, metal bed rails) — wiping/brushing graining ink over a base-coated metal surface and drawing a grain pattern with combs/rollers to match the wood components, in batches of standard parts inside a spray/finishing room.

Custom or contract furniture shop: a small batch of metal parts (e.g., a set of tubular chair frames or metal bed frames) is grained by hand at a bench or in a booth to a standard species look (oak, walnut, maple) so the metal harmonizes with the wood elements; parts are removable and handled individually.

Restoration/antique shop: a one-off metal component (bed rail, metal trim, painted-steel case part) is grained to reproduce a period wood-grain appearance on the piece, requiring base-color toning plus a plausible grain figure; component is removed and worked on a bench.

Spot repair/touch-up: chipped, scratched or worn graining on the metal parts of an already-assembled and finished piece is repaired in place on the bench — the finisher feathers new graining ink into surviving grain and blends color and sheen so the repair is invisible.

On-site work at a customer's premises (office suite, hotel, private residence): the finisher re-grains metal portions of installed furniture in place — masking surroundings, working around fixed furnishings and variable light/ventilation, applying graining ink by hand.

sources.system: Decoral System sublimation wood-grain metal decoration line (Decoral / Decoral America)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing a simulated wood-grain finish on metal furniture parts by machine transfer of grain-patterned ink instead of hand-spread graining ink. Same substrate (metal furniture components), same accepted output (convincing wood-grain appearance), performed in a purpose-built line.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring wood-grain ink patterns onto fixtured metal parts. The dipped part receives a full wood-grain ink film over its metal surface, the same accepted output as hand graining, on comparable objects (metal furniture components) in a purpose-built dipping cell.

tasks.label: Brush bleaching agents on wood surfaces to restore natural color.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repair/refinishing shop bench: a stripped tabletop or dresser top has dark water rings and iron stains; the finisher brushes oxalic acid solution over the affected zone (usually the whole top for evenness), lets it dwell, checks color, reapplies, then neutralizes, rinses, dries and de-nibs the raised grain.

Shop: a whole stripped case piece or chair frame gets two-part A/B bleach brushed over every surface (top, sides, drawer fronts, turned legs, aprons) to lighten it overall to a specified color, applied wet and even without runs or streaks, then neutralized, dried and sanded before finishing.

Selective blend bleaching: spot-bleaching a sun-faded panel, a dark glue/water stain, a new veneer patch or a carved detail so it matches surrounding wood — repeated small applications, feathering edges, judging color match against adjacent areas, and avoiding lifting veneer or opening glue joints.

Finishing department of a high-grade furniture/millwork plant: a batch of white oak panels, doors or parts receives a bleach or bleaching stain as the first step of a specified finish schedule, applied uniformly to identical parts, then neutralized, dried, sanded and moved to the stain/topcoat stations.

On-site at a customer's home or historic building: bleaching a built-in cabinet, stair rail, mantel or a piece too large to move — masking and protecting surroundings, ventilating, brushing bleach in place, neutralizing and drying with limited working room.

sources.claim: Cefla's iBotic cartesian spraying robot scans wood workpieces of varying shape and ... on a conveyor and sprays them, applying coatings, stains and adhesives to furniture parts, doors and panels in an enclosed finishing line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of liquid finishing chemicals (stain, coating, glue) to wood furniture parts. Same substrate and same physical act as brushing bleach on wood — wetting the surface with a reactive liquid at uniform coverage — with the workpiece conveyed and scanned in a purpose-built booth.

sources.system: CMA Robotics wood painting robots (3D-vision auto program generation)

roles.title: Model Makers, Wood
roles.description: Construct full-size and scale wooden precision models of products. Includes wood jig builders and loft workers.

tasks.label: Read blueprints, drawings, or written specifications, and consult with designers to determine sizes and shapes of patterns and required machine setups.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Fit, fasten, and assemble wood parts together to form patterns, models, or sections, using glue, nails, dowels, bolts, screws, and other fasteners.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pattern shop of a foundry or jobbing patternmaker: fitting and joining a segmented wooden casting pattern — gluing and doweling cope and drag halves, adding core prints and loose pieces, screwing pattern halves to a match plate — one-off bespoke geometry with draft and shrink allowances, fits held to a few tenths of a millimetre, work done on benches with clamps while glue cures.

Jig, fixture, template and tooling build in a manufacturer's or shipyard's wood shop: assembling plywood and hardwood frames, gussets, spacers and locating blocks into large jigs and drill templates using screws, bolts, dowel pins and glue, squared and shimmed to layout lines, moderate-to-high precision over several metres.

Architectural, display or museum scale model in a model shop: gluing and pinning dozens to hundreds of small, fragile basswood, plywood and veneer parts (thin strips, sills, mullions, terrain layers) into a presentation model, held by hand or light clamps while adhesive sets, cosmetic joint quality required.

Full-size mockup, buck or loft-derived section: erecting curved frames and stringers over a lofted form and fitting battens or planking to them, trimming and fairing each piece to fit before fastening with screws, nails and glue; large, awkward, one-off assemblies built on the shop floor.

Batch or repeat work: producing a set of identical model sections, pattern blanks, core boxes or standardized jig frames — squaring boxes and frames, stacking and gluing laminations, driving screws and nails to a fixed drawing, several near-identical units in a run.

sources.claim: The TIM robotic timber platform robotically prefabricated the BUGA Wood Pavilion's bespoke hollow wood segments, each built from about eight custom timber elements, with the robots placing beams and plates, preparing glue joints and fixing elements with beech nails inside a purpose-built robotic cell with part input bays and a glue press.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic prefabrication of bespoke timber cassettes. It is the same operation as the rated task — fitting and fastening custom-cut wood parts into a section using glue and nails — on comparable wooden members and at tighter tolerance than typical pattern work, executed from a CAD model in a robotic cell.

sources.system: TIM robotic manufacturing platform (BUGA Wood Pavilion)
sources.title: BUGA Wood Pavilion — Cluster of Excellence IntCDC, University of Stuttgart
sources.claim: The same platform performed automated assembly and milling of 376 bespoke hollow wood segments so that they fit together with sub-millimetre precision, and the workflow chained gripping, vacuum clamping, nailing, gluing, planing, drilling and milling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of one-off wood sections. Establishes that bespoke, non-repeating wood parts can be joined by robots to sub-millimetre fit, the precision class demanded of wood patterns and jigs.

tasks.label: Verify dimensions and contours of models during hand-forming processes, using templates and measuring devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench-scale hand-shaped wood model or foundry pattern (up to ~1 m) in a pattern/model shop: after each round of bandsawing, rasping, carving and sanding the maker checks critical dimensions and profiles with calipers, height gauge, radius gauges and sheet-metal profile templates against the drawing/CAD, then marks where stock must still come off.

Full-size model, plug, buck or mockup (car body buck, boat hull plug, aerospace mockup) too large to move, being faired by hand on stands in the shop: station/sweep templates, battens, straightedges, plumb lines and portable measuring gear used in place to check contour and overall dimensions between shaping passes.

Wood jig, assembly fixture or contour board under construction: as parts are hand-fitted and trimmed, the builder verifies hole locations, flatness, squareness, spacing of locators and contour surfaces against the drawing/CAD, working on the shop floor with tape, square, level, indicators and templates.

Complex compound-curved or sculptural piece (propeller/impeller pattern, furniture or product prototype, decorative carving) where fairness and surface feel matter: verified with contour gauges, sweeps, section templates and hand/eye checks, sometimes against drawings only rather than a CAD nominal.

Field verification away from the shop: a jig, mockup or full-size model assembled or installed at a customer plant, boatyard, exhibit hall or job site is checked for dimensions and contour under as-found conditions with tape, templates, level and portable measuring gear.

sources.system: ZEISS ScanCobot (ATOS Q + collaborative robot)
sources.title: ZEISS ScanCobot: Mobile measuring station | Collaborative robot
sources.claim: ZEISS ScanCobot is a commercially sold mobile measuring station combining a collaborative robot arm, an ATOS optical 3D scanner and a motorized rotary table; it is wheeled onto the shop floor next to the work, scans a small/medium part automatically, and its software produces nominal/actual comparisons and reports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional inspection of prototype and pre-production parts. Transfer holds because the verified act is identical (compare a formed surface to nominal geometry and report deviation), matte wood scans at least as well as plastic or cast iron, and wood-model tolerances are far coarser than the sensor's.

sources.system: ATT Collaborative Scanning System (FANUC CRX-10iA + Creaform MetraSCAN-R BLACK|Elite)
sources.title: Factory Ready Automated Inspection Systems - ATT Metrology Solutions
sources.claim: ATT sells a factory-floor robotic scanning system built on a FANUC CRX collaborative robot and Creaform MetraSCAN-R optical scanner on a rolling base, explicitly unfenced, whose listed applications include tooling verification and jig inspection from small components up to large tooling assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tooling and jig inspection in aerospace shops. Same verification act on the same class of object (assembly jigs and fixtures checked against CAD), performed in an ordinary human-occupied shop rather than a fenced cell.

sources.system: Nikon APDIS MV4x0 / MV5X Laser Radar
sources.title: APDIS MV4x0 - Nikon Metrology, LLC
sources.claim: Nikon's APDIS Laser Radar is a motorised non-contact measuring machine, deployable on a stand or robot, that runs automated measurement programs on large structures such as car bodies and aircraft assemblies in place on the factory floor, at 20 um + 5 um/m accuracy and with no targets or surface preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-situ dimensional inspection of large assemblies and tooling. A full-size wood buck, plug or mockup poses the same measurement problem (metres-scale contoured surface measured where it stands) with looser tolerances than aerospace tooling.

sources.system: ZEISS ATOS ScanBox (Series 4 RC / 6 / 7 / 8)

sources.claim: ZEISS ScanBox automated 3D scanning cells are enclosed measuring machines with robot-manipulated optical sensors that program, digitize, inspect and report ...; the Series 7 handles parts up to ten metres and Series 8 digitizes entire car bodies, with robot part loading through a motorized door.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated full-field inspection of large formed parts and try-out tooling. Same verification output (surface-to-nominal deviation map and report) on objects of the same size class as full-size wood models and bucks, with the work brought into the cell.

sources.system: Creaform R-Series (MetraSCAN 3D-R, CUBE-R, VXscan-R Automation)

sources.claim: Creaform's R-Series pairs robot-mounted MetraSCAN 3D-R optical CMM scanners with industrial or collaborative robots for shop-floor automated inspection, including automatic generation of the robot scanning path from the digital twin, which removes most per-part programming for one-off geometries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mounted optical CMM inspection of complex-surface parts. Automatic path planning from CAD matters because model shops build one-offs; the scan-and-report verification step transfers directly to hand-formed wood models and patterns.

sources.system: TARUS Claymill (5-axis milling/scanning machine)

sources.claim: TARUS Claymill full-size vehicle model machines, the standard in automotive design studios, combine milling and scanning so that a model altered by hand is then measured and scanned on the machine and compared or fed back to CAD.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine verification of a full-size design model after hand sculpting. This is the same in-process check a wood model maker performs with sweeps and templates, on comparable full-size contoured models mounted on the machine.

tasks.label: Trim, smooth, and shape surfaces, and plane, shave, file, scrape, and sand models to attain specified shapes, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench work in a pattern/model shop: shaping and smoothing small-to-medium wooden pattern parts (hardwood, MDF, laminated blanks) with block plane, rasp, file, scraper and hand/orbital sander to reach a specified profile and surface within pattern tolerances; part is held in a vise or on the bench, worker rotates it and works by eye and feel.

Shaping compound-curved full-size work: a boat hull plug, a body buck, a wind-tunnel or display mockup built up from laminated wood/MDF/tooling board. Worker walks around a large piece on stands, uses spokeshave, drawknife, long fairing boards and belt/orbital sanders to fair the surface to templates/battens.

Final finish sanding of an assembled wooden model or pattern before sealing/painting: progressive grit sequence over convex and concave surfaces, filleted corners, edges that must stay crisp, and blended glue joints; inspection by raking light and hand feel.

Corrective, iterative fit-trimming during assembly: scraping and shaving mating surfaces of pattern halves, core boxes, loose pieces and jig blocks so trial assemblies seat with no gap, dressing draft angles, squaring machine-cut joint corners, removing a few thousandths where a trial fit binds.

Dressing and trimming large wooden jigs, fixtures, and loft templates on the shop/loft floor: sawing and planing plywood/MDF contours to the lofted line, filing and sanding edges of templates and jig faces, fitting the jig against the part or floor layout.

sources.system: Cohesive Robotics Smart Finishing Robotic Workcell — Woodworker Edition (Argus OS)
sources.title: Robotic Sanding & Finishing for Woodworking | Cohesive Robotics
sources.claim: Cohesive Robotics sells a commercially available 'Woodworker Edition' Smart Finishing robotic sanding workcell that processes woods and MDF with force-controlled sanding, uses in-cell pneumatic fixturing and 3D scanning to generate paths without CAD or teaching, and is marketed for cabinets, doors, furniture and musical instruments.

sources.system: FANUC robotic sanding cells with Integrated Force Sensing; FANUC CRX-10iA cobot sanding wood doors
sources.title: Woodworking Solution | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC documents robotic sanding cells for woodworking in which force-sensing robots perform controlled material removal on wooden chairs and doors to achieve consistent surface finishes, plus robot routers that route and sand parts.

tasks.label: Plan, lay out, and draw outlines of units, sectional patterns, or full-scale mock-ups of products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench layout in the model shop: from a print or CAD file, select board/sheet stock (plywood, MDF, basswood, hardwood), decide part placement around grain, knots and defects, and mark part outlines, centerlines, station/reference lines and joinery locations with pencil, knife, square, dividers and trammel points before cutting.

Expanding a scaled drawing to full size: drawing full-scale sectional patterns / templates (frames, ribs, bulkheads, jig profiles) on sheet stock, template hardboard or mylar in the shop, fairing curves with splines and battens, then cutting the template.

Planning and drafting: interpreting blueprints, engineering data or customer specifications, computing scale and offsets, deciding materials, joint and jig construction, and producing the shop drawings/sketches or CAD layout that will govern the model, pattern or mock-up.

Laying out onto an already-assembled three-dimensional workpiece in the shop bay: transferring station lines, waterlines, buttock lines, trim lines, hole and fixture locations onto the curved or built-up surfaces of a partially finished mock-up, plug or jig standing on horses or a build table.

Full-scale layout on the loft floor / shop or hangar floor: snapping and drawing full-size outlines, grid and reference lines for a full-size mock-up footprint or large jig, working over tens of feet with control points established from a datum.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pattern shop: build a three-dimensional foundry pattern and matching core box from CAD/drawings — glue up a laminated hardwood or tooling-board blank, shape contours with draft, fillets and shrink allowance to a few tenths of a millimeter, bench-sand, seal and color-code paint, mount on a match plate.

Shop bench/CNC area: make flat templates, layout boards, router/drill jigs, check fixtures and full-size lofted templates from plywood, MDF or hardboard — 2-D profiles, pockets, locating holes, labeling, edges eased, verified against the drawing or lofted lines.
Model/milling room: contoured full-scale mock-up or styling buck — laminated wood and tooling-foam blocks carved to a CAD surface, faired, sanded and finished for appearance and fit review.

Shop floor (occasionally at the customer's plant): framed-and-skinned full-scale mock-up such as an aircraft cabin section, machine enclosure or appliance mock-up — build a wooden frame, cut and fit plywood skins, hinged doors, brackets and hardware, then hand-fit and modify iteratively during fit checks.

Tooling shop: wooden/composite plug or mold for composite layup or vacuum forming (boat hull plug, layup tool) — laminate a large blank, machine the surface, fill and fair, sand to a high finish, seal and wax.
Model shop bench: detailed scale display or engineering model — many small wooden parts cut and fitted, glued into subassemblies with clamps, hand-detailed, sanded and painted.

tasks.label: Select wooden stock, determine layouts, and mark layouts of parts on stock, using precision equipment such as scribers, squares, and protractors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Solid-stock cut layout in a model/pattern shop: worker pulls boards of a given species and thickness from the lumber rack, sights them for warp, knots and checks, decides which parts come out of which board, and marks crosscut/rip lines with a framing square, straightedge and pencil or scriber. Bench and floor space, other workers moving about.

Precision layout on a prepared hardwood blank for a small scale-model or pattern component: centerlines, joint shoulders, angled faces and hole centers laid out to roughly 0.5 mm with combination square, protractor/bevel, marking gauge and scriber, working from a print or CAD dimension set on a bench.

Sheet-goods layout for a jig, mold or full-size mock-up: select MDF/plywood/particleboard sheets of the right grade and thickness, nest the part outlines on the sheet for yield, and mark outlines, reference lines and hole locations with straightedge, square and trammel.

Loft-style full-size layout: transfer full-scale drawing geometry (station lines, curves, contours, bevels) onto large stock or template sheets laid on the loft floor or a large table, using battens, trammel points, straightedge and protractor, checking the marked geometry against the drawing.

Appearance-critical stock selection and grain-oriented layout for the exposed surfaces of a presentation/display model: match color and figure between adjacent parts, orient the layout to grain direction and figure, avoid blemishes on show faces, then mark the parts out.

tasks.label: Mark identifying information on patterns, parts, and templates to indicate assembly methods and details.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Foundry/industrial pattern shop: after a wooden pattern half or core box is machined, the model maker marks part number, job number, cope/drag, parting-line arrows, core-print IDs and match callouts on the curved 3D wooden surfaces with pencil, marker or stamp at the bench.

Jig and fixture shop: stamping, stenciling or writing tool numbers, station callouts, orientation arrows and 'this side up' notes on wooden jig components and hardboard/ply templates before they go to the assembly floor.
Loft work, sheet templates: marking frame/station numbers, bevel notations, centerlines and up-arrows on full-size plywood or hardboard templates cut from sheet stock.
Loft work, floor layout: marking full-size lofted lines on the loft floor and annotating them with station numbers, frame identifiers and sequencing notes.
Mid-fabrication marking: as parts are cut and fitted, the worker writes match marks on mating surfaces, keep-side/waste marks, and assembly sequence numbers on varied small parts held on the bench.
Applying printed labels or stamped tags to finished patterns, core boxes and templates for storage and retrieval (pattern number, customer, rack location, revision).

tasks.label: Set up, operate, and adjust a variety of woodworking machines such as bandsaws and planers to cut and shape sections, parts, and patterns, according to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pattern/model shop floor: worker pulls rough hardwood boards and glued-up blanks from the rack, sets fences/stops on the table saw, miter saw and bandsaw, and rips/crosscuts stock to rough sizes from a cut list for a foundry pattern, jig or scale model — working around knots, checks and warp, leaving material oversize for later dimensioning.

Dimensioning stock: worker sets/adjusts jointer knives and infeed depth and planer thickness, flattens and squares stock, then thicknesses laminated blanks and pattern boards to drawing dimensions within roughly 0.01 in, taking trial passes, checking with caliper and square, and adjusting to eliminate snipe and tearout.

Curved/contour cutting on the bandsaw: worker installs and tensions the right blade, sets guides and table tilt, then cuts curved pattern segments, templates and core-box halves along scribed layout lines, and resaws blanks — compensating for blade drift and leaving finish allowance.

Shaping and profiling: worker sets up a shaper, router table or CNC router (cutters, spindle height, fence, hold-downs, or program, workholding and tool offsets), makes trial cuts, and machines molded edges, draft angles, fillets and 3D contoured surfaces on pattern/model parts to the print, adjusting to hold tolerance.

Full-size loft and jig work: laying out and cutting full-size templates, jig components and large/long members (4x8+ MDF and plywood, long laminated members) on the panel saw, large bandsaw or gantry router in the shop, with heavy handling and dimensions taken from a full-scale layout or lofted lines.

tasks.label: Build jigs that can be used as guides for assembling oversized or special types of box shooks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the box/crate shop, build a new nailing-and-squaring form for an oversized rectangular crate from a dimensioned drawing: cut 2x4s and plywood to length on shop saws, lay out and fasten perimeter rails, corner blocks and stops onto a base, check diagonals/square before release.

Build a jig for a special-shaped box (tapered, angled-end, hexagonal or heavily cleated shook) from a drawing: compound-angle cuts, angled fences, hold-downs and spacers set to non-rectangular geometry, verified against the drawing.

Build the jig by working from physical reference rather than full dimensions: assemble a sample/first-article shook, scribe stop positions off the actual parts, fasten stops, then trial-fit and shave/shim until the shook seats and nails square.
Rework an existing jig: strip and reposition worn or damaged stops and cleats for a changed box size or after production wear, replace broken members, re-square and re-verify the jig with a test box.

Build a one-off cradle/jig in a customer's crating bay or field site around an actual oversized machine or item: take measurements in situ from the object, use lumber on hand, build the frame around and under the load amid other operations.

tasks.label: Issue patterns to designated machine operators.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-shop handoff: the model maker carries a just-finished plywood/MDF template or router jig (2-30 lb, up to ~4 ft) from his bench across the pattern shop to the bandsaw, shaper or CNC operator's station, points out the reference edge and registration marks, and leaves it at the machine.

Archive pull: per a work order, the model maker locates a previously made pattern on the shop's storage racks/shelves, checks the part number and revision stamp against the traveler, signs it out in the pattern log, and walks it across the floor to the designated CNC router or molding operator.

Heavy or multi-piece set: a foundry cope-and-drag pattern with core boxes, or a matched jig set, is loaded on a cart or lifted with a hoist, kept together as a matched set, and issued to the molding-machine or panel-saw operator, who mounts it in the machine.

Oversized rigid template: a large plywood/MDF full-size layout template or loft board (up to 8-12 ft, heavy but rigid) is moved, usually two-handed or on a panel cart, to the mill or router operator without racking or damaging the edges.

Floppy loft work: long thin battens or full-size mylar/paper loft templates from a mold loft are rolled, carried and unrolled at the mill operator's station, kept flat and unstretched, with fairing marks aligned.

Mid-run reissue: a corrected, repaired or superseding pattern is brought out to an operator at a running machine, exchanged for the one in the setup, and the superseded pattern is taken back and logged.

instances.label: Flat 2D template/pattern: in the model shop, the maker takes a shape from a drawing, CAD file or an existing part and cuts it from plywood, MDF, hardboard or acrylic (bandsaw/router or CNC), then sands the edge to the line so it can be used for tracing and pattern-routing model parts.

Full-size loft template / station template or spline for a large model, plug or mold: shape laid out at full scale from lines drawings or CAD on the loft floor, cut from large sheet stock, often several mating station templates that must agree with one another.

Wooden jig or fixture built as a work aid: several machined wood pieces (base, fences, stops, bushings) glued and screwed into a drilling, routing or glue-up jig sized to a specific model part, holding parts to close tolerance in the shop.

Profiled scraper or shaped scraping/forming aid: a steel scraper blade, profile knife or profile gauge shaped (filed/ground) to match a molding or fillet profile on the model, then sharpened so it cuts cleanly.
3D contoured aid: a curved sanding block, caul, cradle or support form shaped to fit a compound-curved surface of the model in progress, made from wood or tooling board in the shop.

tasks.label: Finish patterns or models with protective or decorative coatings such as shellac, lacquer, or wax.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the model/pattern shop's spray booth, seal and topcoat a wooden foundry pattern or core box (roughly 1-3 ft, three-dimensional, with draft, fillets and core prints): spray sanding sealer, scuff-sand, apply two or three lacquer coats, hang or set the piece on a turntable, achieve a smooth, hard, dimensionally faithful film for repeated molding.

At the bench, seal small one-off pattern components, loose pieces, match-plate details and end grain with brushed or wiped shellac/sealer: several thin coats, light scuff-sanding between, pieces varying in shape and size from job to job, done between other shop operations.

Coat a large full-size wooden item - a styling/product mockup, hull plug, loft template or production jig, 6-20 ft long - that will not fit a small booth; sprayed or rolled while set up on stands or sawhorses in the shop, sealer plus topcoats, with sanding between coats.

Rub out and wax a finished presentation or display model: level the cured lacquer with fine abrasives, apply paste wax or polish, and buff to an even decorative sheen acceptable to a client viewing the model up close.

Color-code a finished foundry pattern to shop/AFS convention: mask off regions and apply different colored coatings to cast surfaces, core prints, loose pieces and machined-stock areas, plus stenciled part-number markings.

roles.description: Plan, lay out, and construct wooden unit or sectional patterns used in forming sand molds for castings.

tasks.label: Read blueprints, drawings, or written specifications to determine sizes and shapes of patterns and required machine setups.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Fit, fasten, and assemble wood parts together to form patterns, models, or sections, using glue, nails, dowels, bolts, and screws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pattern-shop bench glue-up/lamination: gluing and clamping kiln-dried boards or blocks (sugar pine, mahogany, MDF/laminate) into a built-up pattern blank or box-like core-box body; joints held with clamps, brads or a few dowels/screws until cured; prismatic geometry, tight glue lines, stock indexed off flat reference faces.

Fitting and attaching shaped secondary components onto a pattern body - core prints, bosses, ribs, lugs, wood fillets, loose pieces - onto curved/tapered surfaces: trial fit, hand-pare/rasp/sand until the mating surface seats flush, then glue and brad/screw in place and clamp; iterative fit-by-eye-and-feel bench work.

Split (cope/drag) pattern halves: fit the two halves so parting faces mate flat, lay out and bore dowel-pin and bushing holes, drive or press pins, then verify the halves register within a few thousandths and separate cleanly with draft intact.

Mounting pattern halves plus gating, runners and risers on match plates or wood follow/mounting boards: laying out positions, drilling and countersinking, and fastening with bolts and wood screws so both faces stay in register.

Large sectional/segmented patterns for big castings (staved cylinders, large housings): heavy timber sections handled with hoist or crane on the shop or foundry floor, dry-fitted, shimmed and faired, then bolted, screwed and glue-blocked together with fits checked and adjusted by hand.

tasks.label: Lay out patterns on wood stock and draw outlines of units, sectional patterns, or full-scale mock-ups of products, based on blueprint specifications and sketches, and using marking and measuring devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pattern shop bench: laying out a simple unit pattern's parts on planed board stock — transferring blueprint dimensions with a shrink rule, square, dividers and pencil/scribe; drawing part outlines, centerlines and parting-line references on each board before sawing.

Laying out curved or irregular sectional-pattern parts and core-box blocks on glued-up blanks: transferring templates, striking arcs with trammels, marking segment joints, draft references, dowel and core-print locations.
Nesting several pattern parts and mounting/match-plate boards on sheet stock (plywood, MDF) for yield: drawing all part outlines and identification marks on the sheet before cutting.

Working from rough-sawn or reclaimed random-width lumber on a bench or sawhorses: sighting grain, knots, checks and wane, then laying out and marking part outlines to avoid defects and orient grain correctly.

Full-scale mock-up lofting: drawing full-size outlines/profiles of the product on large plywood sheets or a layout board on the shop floor from blueprints and sketches, for a wooden mock-up or a large sectional pattern.

tasks.label: Trim, smooth, and shape surfaces, and plane, shave, file, scrape, and sand models to attain specified shapes, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Final smoothing/sanding of a completed wooden pattern (bench-scale, e.g., a pump-housing cope or drag half) in the pattern shop: progressive grits over flat and simple curved faces and edges, hand block and orbital sander, no dips or burn-through, draft edges preserved, ready for filler/sealer.

Planing, shaving and rasping built-up stock on a medium-to-large pattern to bring faces and contours to layout lines and specified draft angles, checked with straightedge, bevel gauge and templates in the shop.

Shaping and blending compound-curved surfaces on 3D pattern sections (blade, elbow, volute forms): files, rasps, cabinet scrapers and sanding to sweeps/section templates until the surface fairs smoothly and matches the specified form.

Trimming and fitting at assembly: chisel-shaving, scraping and filing mating faces of joints, loose pieces, dowel seats and core-box halves, with repeated trial fits of the assembled parts until seating, alignment and parting-line match are correct.

Fine detail work on small pattern parts: carved or trimmed lettering and logos, thin feather edges, small chamfers and delicate ornament cleaned up with small files, knives and chisels without breaking fragile stock.

Touch-up/alteration of an existing pattern returned from the molding floor: rasping, scraping and sanding a glued repair, added boss or reworked area to blend into the surrounding surface, often done quickly at the foundry beside the molding line.

tasks.label: Divide patterns into sections according to shapes of castings to facilitate removal of patterns from molds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small/medium two-part split pattern with a planar parting line for a symmetric casting (pipe fitting, valve body, pulley, bracket) made new from a print or 3D model in a pattern shop: patternmaker sets the parting plane per the casting shape, produces cope and drag halves with matching contours and draft, and registers them with dowel pins/bushings so the halves draw cleanly from the sand.

Moderately complex pattern with core prints and an irregular/curved parting surface, produced in the pattern shop from a 3D model (wood, MDF or tooling board): the parting is laid out over compound surfaces, the pattern is divided into cope and drag sections plus core-print sections, and the sections are located to one another (dowels, or mounted on cope-and-drag boards / a match plate).

Pattern with undercuts and re-entrant shapes requiring loose pieces and draw-backs: the patternmaker judges which portions must be separated so the main body can be rapped and drawn, then hand-fits loose pieces with wedges, keys, sliding dowels or pins so they stay in the sand and are withdrawn afterwards, checking and adjusting fit against trial molding with the foundry.

Large pattern for a heavy casting (machine base, pump/turbine housing, large ring or propeller), built up from glued-up staves/segments and skeleton framing: divided into multiple sections for handling, flask depth and drawing, with keyed, bolted or doweled joints; pieces are several feet in size and moved with hoists in the shop.

Alteration or repair of an existing legacy pattern with no CAD model: an old solid or damaged wood pattern is re-sectioned (sawn on a new parting line, sections added or re-doweled) to suit a different flask, molding machine or repeat order; work is done at the bench with hand and shop tools on a one-off artifact.

tasks.label: Verify dimensions of completed patterns, using templates, straightedges, calipers, or protractors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Final dimensional check of a small-to-medium loose wood pattern (up to ~500 mm) at the bench in a jobbing pattern shop: the patternmaker checks overall lengths, boss diameters, core-print sizes and draft against shrink-rule dimensions on a model-derived drawing using calipers, steel/shrink rule, square and straightedge, then signs off or marks rework.

Verification of a finished core box: internal cavity depths, widths, radii, draft angles and print seats checked with inside calipers, depth gauge, protractor/bevel and profile templates, plus checking that the two halves close and register on dowels; a CAD model of the tooling exists.

Verification of a large pattern, match plate or mounted cope/drag section (roughly 1-3.5 m, heavy, moved by hoist) on a layout table or shop floor: overall dimensions, squareness, flatness/twist, parting-line alignment and plate hole locations checked with long straightedges, squares, height gauge, tape and templates.

Verification of a complex contoured pattern (impeller, volute, propeller blade, turbine section) whose freeform surfaces are checked against sectional profile templates/loft boards and layout lines, with angles checked by protractor and key sections by caliper; 3D model available.

Verification of a repaired, altered or duplicated legacy pattern where the reference is a physical sample casting, an old worn pattern or a 2D paper print with no 3D nominal: the patternmaker compares by template, caliper transfer and eye, judging how much wear, warp and shrink allowance to accept.

tasks.label: Correct patterns to compensate for defects in castings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: First-article casting measures oversize / heavy in section or carries excess machining stock. In the pattern shop the patternmaker compares casting to print (calipers, layout, or scan data), decides the correction, and removes material from the wood/tooling-board pattern - cutting back a boss, rib, or parting face - then re-checks and refinishes. Pattern is a machinable solid with an available 3D model.

Casting comes out undersize, warped, or distorted (shrink or distortion allowance wrong). Correction requires building the pattern up or re-cutting the whole geometry to a compensated shape: laminating on stock, or revising the model and cutting a new corrected pattern or section, then blending it in and refinishing.

Casting shows surface defects traceable to the pattern surface - rough or torn sand finish, sand sticking, hard draw, sharp or wrong-radius fillets, insufficient draft. Patternmaker sands and re-slicks pattern surfaces, adds draft, re-forms fillets, and re-seals/paints the pattern at the bench.

Casting shows misruns, cold shuts, or shrinkage porosity. Patternmaker reworks the gating and feeding on the pattern or match plate: fabricates and attaches new sprue/runner/ingate or riser pieces from wood, repositions them on the board, plugs old locations, and re-fillets joints.

Defects (flash, mismatch, broken detail, crushed core prints) trace to a worn, swollen, or damaged wooden pattern. Patternmaker repairs it by hand: gluing and clamping splits, fitting dutchman patches, re-fitting loose pieces and core prints, filling dings with putty, then sanding and refinishing.

Wood lathe turning: mounting a glued-up or solid blank and turning cylindrical, tapered or contoured pattern sections (bosses, hubs, cylindrical core prints, split turnings) to templates and calipered diameters, then sanding on the lathe.

tasks.label: Finish completed products or models with shellac, lacquer, wax, or paint.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Typical mid-size wooden pattern or core box (roughly shoebox- to suitcase-sized, moderate 3D geometry): seal with shellac/sanding sealer, scuff-sand, then spray two or three coats of lacquer or pattern paint in the shop's spray booth, with the part set on a bench or turntable; output must be a smooth, sealed, run-free surface that strips cleanly from molding sand.

Large or heavy sectional pattern, match plate, or cope/drag half (several feet across, moved by hoist or cart): sealing and spraying multiple coats over broad surfaces and deep draft faces in the booth or a curtained-off area of the shop.

Small, intricate patterns, loose pieces, thin sections and core boxes with deep pockets, narrow slots and undercut internal corners: shellac and lacquer worked in by brush and touched in by hand, hand-sanded between coats, with the piece repeatedly reoriented in the hand.

Applying the foundry color code and identification: masking off areas and painting core prints, loose-piece seats and machined-surface zones in contrasting colors, plus stenciling or hand-lettering pattern numbers on the finished pattern.
Waxing and rubbing out: applying paste wax or release/parting wax to a finished pattern and buffing the surfaces slick, including corners and fillets, so the pattern draws cleanly from the sand.
Refinishing a used or repaired pattern returned from the foundry: scuff-sanding off sand residue and worn coating, then re-sealing and re-spraying the whole pattern back to shop standard.

tasks.label: Repair broken or damaged patterns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the pattern shop, a small-to-medium wooden pattern returns from the foundry with a broken-off feature (fillet, core print, gate, chipped edge or a loose glued-up segment). The patternmaker inspects it, cleans sand and old glue off the irregular fracture surface, re-glues and clamps the fragment (or hand-fits a replacement bit), lets it cure, blends the joint by hand, re-seals/paints and checks the pattern still draws from the sand.

A pattern worn or dented from repeated ramming/rapping: gouges, crushed edges, rounded-over draft. The worker fills with epoxy/wood filler, re-shapes the 3D contour by rasp/sander to the original profile and draft, verifies critical dimensions against the drawing or template (pattern tolerances ~±0.005 in.), then re-finishes.

A large pattern or mounted match plate with a broken, split or rotted section: the damaged region is cut out, a new wood block is fabricated, fitted, glued and doweled/screwed, then re-machined or hand-carved to the original contour, re-rigged (gates, alignment pins) and refinished; dimensions verified before return to the foundry.

Core box repair: chipped or worn cavity corners and prints, split box halves, loose alignment dowels/hardware. The worker disassembles, re-glues joints, fills and recuts internal cavity detail and vents, and re-fits the halves so the box closes and produces cores to size.

Field repair on the foundry molding floor: pattern too large or too urgent to return to the shop, so the patternmaker works among molding stations in dusty, sand-strewn conditions with hand tools — tightening loose hardware, re-gluing a lifted section, patching with quick-set filler, and re-touching the surface between molding cycles.

Cosmetic re-surfacing of a pattern whose finish is scuffed, abraded or sand-blasted dull but whose geometry is intact: sand the surfaces smooth (without cutting into contour or draft), clean, and re-apply sealer/paint in the shop's finishing area.

tasks.label: Glue fillets along interior angles of patterns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench work in the pattern shop on a new medium-size wooden pattern (cope/drag halves, brackets, housings) whose interior angles are mostly straight runs and large-radius corners. The patternmaker cuts wax or wood fillet stock to length, applies glue, presses it into the angle, and wipes/tools it smooth so the corner will draw cleanly from the sand.

A contoured, one-off pattern in the shop whose interior angles curve in three dimensions and change radius along their length (blended bosses, ribs meeting curved walls). Wax fillet is pressed in with a heated fillet iron, or putty/Bondo fillet is formed with a ball tool and blended into adjacent surfaces before sanding.

A large pattern or match plate several feet across, sitting on a floor stand or trestles. Long runs of wood fillet stock (3/4 in.–1 1/2 in. radius) are glued and bradded or clamped along interior angles, including on vertical faces and undersides; joints are mitered where fillets meet.

Coreboxes and deep pockets: small fillets (1/8–1/4 in.) glued into narrow interior cavities and around bosses inside the box, with restricted access for hand and tool, where the fillet must be seated tight with no glue squeeze-out that would print in the core.

Rework of an existing legacy pattern brought back from the foundry: chipped, missing, or sand-eroded fillets are chiseled/scraped out and replaced, matching the radii and blend of the surrounding worn, painted surfaces with no CAD model available.

instances.label: Pattern shop, small-to-medium unit pattern: worker reads the cut list, goes to the shop lumber rack of kiln-dried stock (sugar pine, poplar, mahogany, cherry), sights each board for knots, checks, pitch pockets, warp and grain direction, pulls 2-5 acceptable boards and carries them to the bench/saw.

Selecting heavy, thick or long stock (8/4-16/4, wide or long boards) for a large or sectional pattern or a follow board/match plate, from racks or bulk storage in the shop, moved with a cart, roller table or hoist.

Culling and choosing boards from an incoming lumber delivery or at a supplier's yard/warehouse: inspecting a bundle or lift, rejecting defective or wet boards, and picking the pieces that will yield the required clear parts for upcoming pattern jobs.
Picking usable offcuts and shorts out of the shop's scrap rack or bin for small pattern parts, core box pieces, fillets and repairs - mixed sizes, mixed species, irregular pieces.

tasks.label: Collect and store patterns and lumber.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End of a job in a wood pattern shop: the patternmaker collects the finished/used loose pattern, match plate and coreboxes (roughly 5–80 lb, each a one-off irregular shape with delicate fillets, draft surfaces and shellac/paint finish) from the bench and floor, stencils or checks the pattern number, and places them on wooden shelving/racks in the shop's pattern storage area, recording the location.

Repeat order: the worker locates a specific stored pattern and its coreboxes by pattern number among hundreds of similar one-off wooden patterns stacked on shelves and racks, works it free from among neighbors without chipping fillets, inspects for damage/warp, and carries it to the bench or shipping area.

Incoming material receipt: banded bundles/pallets of kiln-dried pattern lumber (mahogany, sugar pine), MDF and plywood sheets arrive by truck at the shop dock; the worker unloads with a forklift or pallet jack and moves the unit loads into the shop's designated lumber storage area or rack.

Breaking down received stock: the worker hand-sorts loose boards by species, thickness and length, stickers them and stacks them into cantilever lumber racks in the shop, keeping shorts and premium stock segregated.

Post-job cleanup around machines: the worker collects offcuts, partly used boards and shorts scattered on a cluttered shop floor and around the table saw, band saw and lathe, returns usable stock to the racks or short-stock bin, and throws scrap in the waste bin.

Heavy items: large mounted patterns, match plates and skidded/palletized patterns (200–2,000 lb) are moved with a pallet jack or forklift between the shop and pallet racking in the pattern storage room or foundry pattern warehouse.

tasks.label: Inventory equipment and supplies, ordering parts and tools as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic walk-through of the pattern shop checking consumable supply levels (wood glue, sandpaper and abrasives, filler, sealer/lacquer, dowels, screws, brads, rapping plates and core-box hardware) against min/max levels and recording what is low.

Checking pattern-stock material on the lumber racks (sugar pine, mahogany, poplar, plywood, MDF, urethane board, plastic) for species, thickness, and board-footage on hand, and matching it to the stock needed for jobs already booked.

Reviewing tooling status — router and shaper cutters, saw blades, drill bits, hand-plane irons, chisels, measuring tools, sanding belts — noting worn, broken, or missing items that must be replaced or sent out for sharpening.

Placing the resulting orders: pulling part numbers from supplier catalogs, comparing prices and lead times, phoning/emailing suppliers or entering the order in an online portal or the shop's purchasing system, and following up on backorders and delivery dates.
Receiving an incoming shipment: verifying delivered items against the packing slip and purchase order, flagging shortages or wrong items for the supplier, and updating the shop's stock records.

tasks.label: Issue patterns to designated machine operators.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Newly finished one-off wooden loose pattern (roughly 5-60 lb, irregular geometry, fragile fillets, fresh sealer) is taken from the patternmaker's bench and handed across the pattern shop / foundry floor to the designated CNC router or molding-machine operator with the job ticket; the patternmaker points out loose pieces, draft and handling cautions and the operator accepts it.

An existing pattern is pulled from the pattern storage room: numbered wooden shelving and floor stacks, mixed sizes, dust and clutter. Worker matches the pattern number to the work order, checks for warping or broken corners, sets it on a cart, wheels it to the designated molding machine, and signs it out in the pattern log.

Large or heavy pattern / mounted match plate on a skid or pallet in heavy pattern racking. Worker uses a forklift or jib hoist to retrieve the skid, transports it across the plant to the molding line, and sets it down at the designated machine station for the operator.

A complete tooling set is issued: cope and drag pattern halves plus core boxes, loose pieces, follow boards and gating. Worker assembles the kit, inspects each piece for wear or damage (repairing minor chips), delivers it to the molding-machine operator and briefs them on assembly and core placement.

Repeat-production mounted pattern plate for an automatic (flaskless / vertical) molding line: worker pulls the plate from the pattern rack, stages/mounts it in the molding machine's pattern station or changer, and releases the machine to the operator for the run.

Palletized or crated pattern issued for transfer between buildings: moved from the pattern shop across the plant yard or to the shipping dock/staging lane for the foundry's molding department or an outside foundry, with the accompanying paperwork.

roles.title: Sawing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Wood
roles.description: Set up, operate, or tend wood sawing machines. May operate computer numerically controlled (CNC) equipment. Includes lead sawyers.

tasks.label: Inspect and measure workpieces to mark for cuts and to verify the accuracy of cuts, using rulers, squares, or caliper rules.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sawmill breakdown/trim line: a sawyer or lead sawyer sizes logs, cants and boards by eye and rule, decides where boards should be edged/trimmed, and periodically pulls sample boards to check thickness and width with a digital caliper or tape against target size, adjusting saws when the sizes drift.

Secondary/rough mill (moulding, flooring, furniture-component plant): operator inspects rough lumber for knots, wane and splits, marks defect cut lines with crayon or chalk before the crosscut/rip saw, then checks cut blanks against a length gauge or tape.

Custom cabinet or millwork shop: operator measures sheet goods and solid stock with tape, rule and framing square, pencils cut lines for one-off or short-run parts on a panel/table saw, and afterwards checks finished part length, width and squareness before the parts go to assembly.

Setup and first-piece verification on a CNC beam saw, gang rip or straight-line rip: after a setup or blade change, the operator measures the first cut piece with caliper, micrometer and square, corrects fence/blade position, re-cuts and re-measures, then makes periodic in-run checks.

High-volume pallet, crate or truss cut-up plant: operator makes quick repetitive length/width verifications of cut components with a tape, gauge block or go/no-go jig against spec, catching creep in stops and saw settings.

Portable sawmill or on-site timber cutting at a customer's property or yard: sawyer measures irregular logs, beams or timbers with a tape and square, marks cut lines by eye on rough or dirty stock, and verifies finished dimensions in the open air.

sources.title: Automate grade and trim solutions in your planer mill with USNR's Automated Lineal Grading System - International Forest Industries
sources.claim: USNR's AI-driven Automated Lineal Grading System grades lumber and produces grade and trim (cut) solutions automatically at mill speeds on planer-mill lineal conveyor lines; the article states over 70 units are installed in North America.
sources.transferJustification: The system performs the inspection/measurement and cut-location decision (trim solution) that the worker performs with rule and crayon, on the same lumber, and drives the trim saws directly.

sources.system: Microtec Goldeneye 300 Multi-Sensor Quality Scanner with GradeView
sources.title: Defect detection performance of automated hardwood lumber grading system - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed evaluation of the Microtec Goldeneye 300 multi-sensor scanner grading kiln-dried rough hardwood lumber found accuracy of 92.22% on grade and 99.50% ..., within industry standards, based on automatic detection and measurement of board defects.
sources.transferJustification: Automated defect detection and measurement on boards is the inspection half of the task; its output feeds the trim/chop decision the worker would mark by hand, at documented worker-comparable accuracy.

tasks.label: Adjust saw blades, using wrenches and rulers, or by turning handwheels or pressing pedals, levers, or panel buttons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sawmill breakdown/secondary line (edger, gang, trim saws): sawyer sets saw blade lateral positions, spacing and heights for a new cutting pattern or target size, working from a console with buttons/levers or hydraulic setworks, then verifies sizes on the first pieces.

Sawmill circular-saw blade change: dull or damaged circular blades on an edger/gang/trim arbor are pulled and replaced, arbor nuts and collars wrenched, spacing collars set, blade run-out checked before restart.

Bandmill/resaw blade change and alignment: a 20-40 ft band blade is pulled off the wheels, a sharp one mounted, strain/tension set, wheel tilt and tracking adjusted, guides set with wrenches and gauges, lead checked with a test cut.

Secondary wood plant (cabinet/furniture/millwork) CNC beam or panel saw: set main blade projection for the panel thickness, align and set the scoring blade laterally and in height, change main/scoring blades when dull, confirm with a test cut and rule.

Small custom/millwork shop stationary saws (sliding table saw, table saw, radial-arm, miter, band saw): change between rip and crosscut blades, set blade height and bevel, square blade to table/fence with a rule or square, cut and measure a test piece.

Portable band mill / pallet or tie mill working outdoors or in an open shed: swap band blades several times a shift, set tension and tracking, adjust guide rollers and blade height, in dust, weather and an as-found layout.

sources.system: Wood-Mizer EA3000 Optimizing Edger
sources.title: EA3000 Automated Edger | Wood-Mizer USA
sources.claim: Commercial optimizing edger installed in sawmills scans each board and positions its saw blades automatically with electric servo blade adjustment, replacing the operator's saw-setting decisions and console inputs.

sources.title: USNR - Self-setting saw guides
sources.claim: Sawmill band saws are delivered with saw guides that adjust their own height automatically to the log or cant, i.e. the blade-guide adjustment normally done by hand with wrenches is machine-controlled.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: setting saw guides is one of the wrench/handwheel blade adjustments named in the task; here the machine's own control system performs it on production band saws.

sources.system: WEINIG SOLID RIP V 310 (VarioRip 310) optimizing rip saw
sources.title: VarioRip 310 - Rip Saw Machine MICHAEL WEINIG (USA)
sources.claim: Multi-blade rip saws sold for solid-wood plants carry saw blades that the machine repositions itself on the arbor according to the measured board, in place of an operator sliding saws and spacers.

sources.title: Beam saw kappa automatic | Mayer

sources.system: VOLLMER ND 250 robot loading system for circular saw blades
sources.title: ND 250 robot system for sharpening circular saws
sources.claim: A CNC robot handling system mounts and dismounts carbide-tipped circular saw blades (100-630 mm) on machine clamping spindles automatically, running hundreds of blades from magazines without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic mounting/removal of circular saw blades onto a machine spindle and clamping them concentrically. sources.system: VOLLMER CHX 840 with HS automated loading station at Integrity Saw & Tool

sources.claim: A US saw shop runs a Vollmer sharpening machine with robotic blade loading unmanned, loading and processing batches of circular saw blades without an operator present.

sources.system: Altendorf F 30 sliding table saw (and F 45 / ELMO programmable versions)
sources.title: Altendorf F 30 – Altendorf Group
sources.claim: Shop-class sliding table saws are built with motorised, program-controlled saw blade height and tilt axes and CNC rip fence, so the blade setting itself is executed by machine axes rather than by hand.

tasks.label: Mount and bolt sawing blades or attachments to machine shafts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Millwork/cabinet/pallet shop: change a dull or wrong-kerf circular blade on a single-arbor wood saw (table saw, straight-line rip, cut-off/chop saw, trim saw). Lock out power, open guard/throat plate, break the arbor nut loose, lift off collar and 10-20 in. blade, seat a new blade on the arbor, retighten nut to spec, check runout and make a test cut.

Gang rip saw or edger: build a multi-blade arbor set — slide several blades alternating with spacer collars onto a long arbor in the pattern the rip solution calls for, index them, torque the arbor nut, verify blade spacing and that blades run true.

CNC beam saw / sliding table panel saw or CNC router: swap main and scoring blades on the saw carriage (Power-Loc or nut/flange), or mount a saw-blade aggregate/tool onto the machine spindle for grooving and sizing cuts; re-reference blade projection and scoring alignment.

Band sawmill, resaw or vertical bandsaw: take a dull band off the wheels, carry and uncoil a fresh 12-35 ft band, loop it over the wheels with teeth correctly oriented, apply and set tension, track the blade on the wheels, and reset guides/rollers.

Sawmill heavy circular saw work: change headrig, edger, trimmer or chipper saws — heavy (20-50 kg) blades, saw collars or whole saw boxes handled with a hoist in confined machine housings, high-torque arbor nuts, lockout/tagout, sawdust and pitch, then check for lead and runout.

Mount non-blade attachments to shafts: dado stacks, shaper/moulder cutterheads, sanding drums, feed rollers, hold-down wheels, chip breakers and guides — install on the machine shaft/spindle, key and bolt them, and set projection/height.

sources.system: DISCO Auto Blade Changer (ABC) on DFD6342/DFD6561/DFD6755 dicing saws
sources.title: An optional function that can automatically replace hubless blades: New ABC developed
sources.claim: DISCO's Auto Blade Changer, an option on production dicing saws, automatically removes and mounts the circular blade on the machine spindle (hub and hubless types) and has been sold commercially since 2005.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting a circular blade concentrically on a rotating machine spindle and securing it with a flange nut, then verifying it runs true. That is the same operation as mounting a wood saw blade on an arbor, at far tighter runout tolerance; wood blades are larger and heavier but well within industrial handling, and the demonstration occurs inside a purpose-built machine enclosure (E1).

sources.system: DISCO DFD6363 dicing saw with Automatic Blade Changer
sources.title: DFD6363 | Dicing Saws | Product Information | DISCO CORPORATION
sources.claim: On the DFD6363 dicing saw the blade change is a closed loop: the machine detects end of blade life and performs every step from blade replacement through resuming cutting in fully automatic operation.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (blade-to-spindle mounting); this source establishes that the whole change, not a sub-step, is done unattended and the machine returns to accepted-quality cutting.

sources.system: Futura Super log saw automatic blade change and sharpening system
sources.title: FUTURA SUPER 20 - Papnews
sources.claim: Futura's Super log saw for tissue converting lines includes an automatic blade change and sharpening ... that removes the manual blade-mounting operation on a large industrial circular blade.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: changing a large-diameter circular blade on the shaft of a high-speed production cutting machine. Object size, mass and mounting method (blade seated on shaft/flange, secured, then trued) match wood circular-saw blade changes; the work occurs inside a purpose-built, guarded machine.

sources.system: Saw blade aggregate holders for ATC-equipped woodworking CNC machining centres
sources.developer: CNC tooling suppliers (aggregate holders for Homag/Biesse/SCM-class machines)
sources.title: Saw blade Aggregate Holder - CNC Tool Holder Aggregates
sources.claim: Saw-blade aggregates — attachments carrying a saw blade — are made for woodworking CNC routers, machining centres and point-to-point machines that mount them via the machine's automatic tool changer onto the spindle.
sources.transferJustification: This is the task itself in wood machining: an attachment carrying a saw blade is mounted to the machine spindle (shaft) and clamped, under machine control, without an operator.

sources.system: ATC CNC router / machining centre with tool magazine
sources.developer: Multiple woodworking machine builders (as catalogued by STYLECNC)
sources.title: ATC CNC Routers with Automatic Tool Changer - STYLECNC
sources.claim: ATC CNC routers used for cabinet, door and furniture work carry a tool magazine and change tooling onto the spindle automatically without manual operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic mounting and clamping of tooling (including saw aggregates, per the aggregate suppliers) on a woodworking machine spindle — the mounting-to-shaft step of this task, performed to production quality in a guarded machine.

tasks.label: Set up, operate, or tend saws or machines that cut or trim wood to specified dimensions, such as circular saws, band saws, multiple-blade sawing machines, scroll saws, ripsaws, or crozer machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sawmill machine centers: tending/setting primary log breakdown (carriage, canter, band mill), gang saw, edger, resaw and trimmer in a dimension or hardwood sawmill. Logs and cants arrive on chains/conveyors; the sawyer sets cutting patterns and monitors from a booth; species, sweep and defects vary log to log.

Panel processing in a cabinet, casegoods, closet or millwork plant: loading sheet goods onto a beam saw or sliding-table panel saw, running a cut list/optimized cutting pattern, labeling and stacking parts, checking sizes and edge quality, changing blades and adjusting the scoring saw.

Rough mill / dimension cut-up line in a moulding, flooring, component or furniture plant: feeding packs of rough lumber to gang rip saws and optimizing chop saws, cutting out knots and defects to produce clear components to specified lengths and widths, sorting and stacking output.

Small custom shop or job-shop sawing: one-off or short-run parts on a table saw, radial-arm/miter saw, band saw or scroll saw. Stock varies (rough boards, plywood, hardwood blanks), layouts are hand-marked or from shop drawings, and the operator sets fences, blade height/angle and jigs for each job.

Pallet, crate and treated-timber mill: cut-up lines, gang rip saws, notchers, resaws and trim saws working low-grade, wet, dirty and sometimes nail-bearing stock (including recycled pallet dismantling and repair cutting) to standard sizes at high volume.

Portable or yard sawing taken as found: portable band sawmill on a woodlot or customer site, or a cut-off/log saw in an open log yard or retail lumberyard, cutting irregular logs and timbers outdoors in variable weather and footing.

sources.claim: HOMAG SAWTEQ B-300 flexTec robot saw installed at PAN + ARMBRUSTER (Oberkirch) since mid-2019 performs the whole cutting job — feeding panels from a storage/lift table, aligning to the cutting pattern, labeling, and destacking parts to pallets — including unmanned running after shift end.

sources.claim: Inotech CCS one-pass small-log breakdown system performs four-side facing and sawing of logs with 3D full optimization and automatic log rotation at production speeds, i.e., unattended execution of the primary sawing decision.

sources.system: WEINIG SOLID CUT TF 2000 / OptiCut 200 optimizing cross-cut saws
sources.title: OptiCut 200 series - Automated Crosscut Saw - MICHAEL WEINIG (USA)
sources.claim: WEINIG SOLID CUT TF 2000 series ... compute the best length combination from a cutting list, cut out defects, and can be run with fully automatic scanner-based defect detection integrated in the line.

tasks.label: Inspect stock for imperfections or to estimate grades or qualities of stock or workpieces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Softwood dimension-lumber sawmill or planer mill: the sawyer/grader stands at a grading station and inspects boards flowing past on the chain at high speed, looking for knots, wane, splits, skip, warp and stain, calling a grade and marking trim/defect decisions that drive the trimmer and sorter.

Hardwood sawmill or concentration yard: rough, random-width, kiln-dried or green boards of mixed commercial species (oak, maple, poplar, hickory) are inspected for clear-cutting yield under NHLA rules; the inspector judges both faces, estimates grade and value, and culls defective boards before resawing.

Log deck / carriage at a mill: the lead sawyer sizes up each log or cant before breakdown — sweep, taper, rot, ring shake, metal, knot clusters, surface indicators of internal defect — to estimate grade and pick the opening face and sawing pattern.

Secondary wood-products plant (millwork, cabinet/furniture components, moulding, truss or pallet plant): the operator at a rip or optimizing chop saw pulls boards from a bundle, inspects them for knots, pith, checks, resin pockets and discoloration, marks defects with crayon or keys them in, and also checks plywood/MDF panels for surface flaws before cutting.

Small custom shop, portable/bandsaw mill, or lumberyard job: the sawyer inspects customer-supplied, urban, reclaimed or air-dried stock and logs in a barn, driveway, open yard or cluttered shop — odd sizes, embedded nails, dirt, unfamiliar species, variable light — and judges what is usable and what grade it will yield.

tasks.label: Monitor sawing machines, adjusting speed and tension and clearing jams to ensure proper operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Primary breakdown line in a dimension lumber sawmill: sawyer/lead sawyer in a control booth watches the bandmill or canter-chipper and edger through cameras and optimizer displays, adjusts carriage/feed speed and saw strain (blade tension) for species, log size and cut quality, watches for saw deviation and heat, and when a cant or slab plugs the saw box or transfer, stops the line, locks out and pulls the piece free with a bar or pike pole before restarting. Guarded, conveyor-fed machine line; high noise, dust, high production rates.

Panel/beam saw in a cabinet, casework or furniture plant: operator loads sheet stock, runs cutting patterns, monitors cut quality and blade condition, adjusts feed and blade/scoring speeds, keeps dust extraction and waste-strip removal working, and clears offcuts or strips that wedge under the pressure beam or in the outfeed. Fixed shop floor with people moving nearby.

Gang ripsaw or optimizing crosscut/chop line in a moulding, flooring or truss/component plant: operator tends the saw as boards feed continuously, adjusts feed chain speed and blade/chain tension, watches for burning or blade wander, and clears strips, short blocks and slivers that jam the infeed, saw box or outfeed sorter. Structured plant floor, standard stock, institution-controlled.

Older or lighter-duty equipment at a pallet mill, crosstie mill, small circle/band mill or reman shop: operator manually cranks or hydraulically sets blade tension and checks tracking, changes feed speed by feel for hard knots and varying rough stock, and frequently clears jammed cants, off-spec boards and sawdust build-up from the machine. Fixed premises, but variable stock and older machines.

Portable band sawmill custom-sawing at a customer's property, log yard or job site: operator tensions and tracks the blade, adjusts feed speed through knots and tension wood, watches for blade dive, and frees the blade or board when the log pinches or a slab hangs up. Uneven ground, weather, no fixed layout.
