tasks.label: Sharpen blades, or replace defective or worn blades or bands, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cabinet/millwork/pallet shop or wood products plant: a 10–18 in. circular blade on a cut-off saw, straight-line rip saw, or sliding table saw has dulled or chipped. Operator locks out the machine, engages the arbor lock, breaks the arbor nut with a wrench, removes the outer flange and blade, cleans pitch off the flanges, mounts a sharpened blade with correct rotation, torques the nut, resets the guard/splitter and test-cuts.

Sawmill: band on a headrig, vertical/horizontal resaw, or band edger dulls or cracks mid-shift. Sawyer shuts down and locks out, opens the wheel guards, releases strain, lifts the heavy coiled band off the wheels (often 20–40 ft loop), hangs a fresh band, re-strains it, tracks it on the wheels, resets guides and lube, and sends the dull band to the filing room.

Filing/sharpening room: touch up or fully sharpen circular saw blades (carbide-tipped rip, cut-off, or trim saws) — grinding tooth face and top, checking gullets and runout — either by hand file/hand grinder or by mounting each blade on the sharpening machine, then returning blades to service.

Small mill or portable sawmill operation: sharpen dull bandsaw blades — mount the loop on the sharpener, grind every tooth to the correct hook/gullet profile, inspect for cracks, and return the band to the mill ready to cut.

Gang rip saw / multi-saw edger: pull the arbor or work in place to replace several worn or damaged saws along with spacers/collars, re-shim to the correct cut spacing, check saw runout and lead, and reassemble — heavier, multi-part work with dimensional set-up afterwards.

CNC panel-sizing beam saw or CNC router with saw aggregate in a furniture/panel plant: main saw blade and scoring blade have reached tool life. Operator opens the carriage access, releases the hub/quick-change fitting, swaps main and scoring blades, sets scoring projection, and restarts the cutting pattern.

tasks.label: Guide workpieces against saws, saw over workpieces by hand, or operate automatic feeding devices to guide cuts.

instances.label: Primary/secondary breakdown at a sawmill or planer mill: the operator runs the log carriage, gang saw, edger and trimmer from a console or control booth, using automatic feeding devices (feed chains, positioning fences, setworks) to present logs, cants and flitches to the saws; workpieces arrive on conveyors, the machine area is guarded and no one stands in it.

Freehand and irregular cutting: guiding a workpiece along a marked line on a band saw or scroll saw to make curved or contoured parts, resawing odd stock, and trimming out defects or crooked ends on a chop/radial-arm saw by eye; each piece differs and the cut path is judged by the operator at the machine in the shop.

Oversized or portable work: sawing over large workpieces by hand — cutting timbers, beams, log-home components or slabs with an over-arm/radial saw or hand-held circular saw, or running a portable band mill on logs staged in a yard or at ... customer's property; ground, weather, stock and layout are taken as found.

tasks.label: Clear machine jams, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Primary sawmill breakdown line (headrig, edger, resaw, trimmer, sorter/stacker): a cant, slab, board or bark wad wedges in the machine or on a chain deck. The sawyer/operator stops the line, locks out, climbs onto the deck or catwalk into the machine center, and frees the wedged material with cant hook, peavey, pinch/pry bar, sledge, or wedge, clears bark and sawdust, checks blade/guides, replaces guarding and restarts.

Secondary wood plant (millwork, cabinet, furniture, pallet, truss shop): stock jams in the feed rolls, against a fence, or in the outfeed of a gang rip saw, straight-line rip, chop saw or resaw. Operator shuts the machine down, removes a guard or hold-down with wrenches/hex keys, pries or mallets the bound board and offcuts free, checks for blade damage, reassembles and restarts.

Dust/scrap-path blockage or bound blade: packed sawdust, wet chips or slivers clog a dust hood, chute, blower or scrap conveyor under the saw, or an offcut binds the blade/kerf. Operator uses scraper, rod, hook, air lance, screwdriver and wrenches to open the hood and clear the pack, then restarts.

Enclosed automated line: CNC beam/panel saw or optimizing cut-to-length line where a strip or offcut jams under the pressure beam, in the pusher/gripper, or in the automated infeed. Operator acknowledges the fault, opens the interlocked enclosure, hooks or pries the piece out with a bar, clears debris, closes the guard and resets the machine.

Small custom or portable sawmill (band mill in an open shed, yard, or job site): the blade binds in a log or the log slips off the dogs and pinches the kerf. One operator uses wedges, hammer, wrenches and a bar to relieve the pinch, back the blade out, re-dog the log, and re-tension or change the band. Layout, footing and weather vary site to site.

sources.system: Flexxbotics FlexxCORE Intelligent Recovery (cobot machine tending at Ruland Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robot-Driven Manufacturing Enables "Lights-Out" Production | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Flexxbotics 'Intelligent Recovery' lets a machine-tending cobot in a fenced FANUC RoboDrill cell autonomously recover from non-safety work stops, repositioning and reseating an improperly seated workpiece without an operator. This is the closest deployed analogue to clearing a machine fault in a purpose-built cell, but it corrects a designed-for part-seating error with the robot's own gripper on precision metal parts; it does not open guards, use hand tools, or free wedged, splintered wood from a saw.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous error recovery from a work stoppage in an automated cell. Transfer fails for jam clearing: the fault class is a known part-seating error on fixtured metal parts, not variable wedged wood requiring guard removal, prying and hammering.

sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot with the Spot Arm is commercially deployed for industrial inspection and can autonomously open doors during Autowalk missions; other manipulation (turning valves, flipping levers) is semi-autonomous or teleoperated. sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation of plant hardware (doors, levers, valves) inside industrial facilities. tasks.label: Lubricate or clean machines, using wrenches, grease guns, or solvents.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift/periodic cleanout of a fixed production saw (edger, gang rip, resaw, cut-off saw) in a sawmill or millwork plant: machine locked out, guards and access doors opened, packed sawdust and chips brushed, scraped and vacuumed out of the saw box, guides, chip chutes and dust ports; dusty, noisy floor shared with forklifts and lumber flow.

Scheduled lubrication round on saw machinery: locating and wiping zerk fittings on arbor bearings, carriage rails, feed rolls, chains and conveyor bearings, pumping grease with a grease gun until grease shows, and checking/topping oil and way-lube reservoirs; some fittings in awkward, guarded positions.

Blade/tooling service: using wrenches to pull guards and remove a circular blade or band, soaking/scrubbing wood pitch and resin off with solvent or blade cleaner, wiping dry, then reinstalling and tensioning the blade on the machine.

Daily clean and lube of a CNC panel saw, beam saw or nesting machining centre in a cabinet/millwork shop: vacuuming dust from table and vacuum ports, wiping and oiling rails and ball screws, clearing the scoring unit and dust hood, greasing listed points.

Greasing a portable band mill or trailer-mounted saw rig at a yard, landing or job site: grease gun on wheel bearings, guide rollers and carriage tracks, oil/lube reservoir top-up, outdoors in weather with no fixed layout.

Cleaning a portable band mill or job-site saw rig in the field: scraping caked pitch and sawdust off band wheels, guides and belt covers with solvent and scraper, brushing debris out of the frame, conditions taken as found.

tasks.label: Adjust bolts, clamps, stops, guides, or table angles or heights, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Custom cabinet/millwork shop: setting up a sliding table saw or panel saw for a batch of parts — set the rip fence to width, set blade projection (height) and bevel angle, set crosscut fence stops and hold-down clamps, check with square/tape and tweak between parts. Indoor shop floor, standard machines, dusty but controlled.

Production plant (furniture/cabinet component, moulding, pallet): setting length stops and clamps on a crosscut/chop-saw line and blade/spacer positions on a gang rip saw at a run changeover — loosen wing nuts or bolts, slide stops to the cut list, retighten, run a test piece. Fixed line layout, repeat runs.

Sawmill breakdown line (headrig, edger, trimmer, gang): setting saw guides, edger fences and saw spacing, and feed roll/press roll heights for the log or cant mix — wrench and pry-bar work on heavy guides, stops and spacers, often during a scheduled downtime window with the line locked out. Noisy, wet, industrial mill floor.

Band resaw / bandmill after a blade change: setting the side guides and thrust/pressure guides to the new blade, setting strain (tension) and tracking, and setting table or roll height/tilt with hand tools, then test cutting and re-tweaking.

Corrective adjustment mid-shift: parts come off out-of-square or off-size, so the operator diagnoses the cause, loosens bolts, taps/shims a fence, table or guide back into alignment, re-torques, and re-checks with square, gauge or test cut.

Portable band mill set up on site (farm, logging landing, jobsite, small custom mill yard): level and set the bed and end stops, set the blade guide arm to log width, position log clamps and side supports, and set head height/thickness for each board. Outdoors, uneven ground, variable logs.

tasks.label: Examine logs or lumber to plan the best cuts.

instances.label: Primary breakdown at a softwood dimension sawmill: the sawyer/headrig operator sizes up each log arriving on the carriage or sharp-chain infeed (diameter, taper, sweep, crook, flare, surface defects) and decides rotation/opening face and the cutting pattern, at production speed of many logs per minute, from a control booth on the mill floor.

Hardwood grade sawmill: the sawyer examines each log face-by-face on the carriage, judging knots, stain, rot, shake and log geometry, and decides when to turn the log and where to open each face to maximize grade yield across mixed species and log quality.

Edger/trimmer/resaw station: the operator examines flitches, cants and rough boards for wane, taper, splits and defects and decides the edging lines, trim lengths, or resaw pattern that yields the highest-value piece; boards move by on chains or a table in a mill.

Secondary wood products plant or cabinet/millwork shop: worker examines rough kiln-dried boards from a cart or stack for knots, checks, wane, color and grain, and plans rip/crosscut layout against a cut list to hit yield and appearance requirements.

Portable/custom sawmill working outdoors at a farm, logging landing, or urban lot: operator sizes up each log by eye (embedded metal, rot, sweep, taper, butt flare), and decides opening face and cut pattern for the customer's specific order, one log at a time in variable weather and footing.

instances.label: Sawmill/planer mill green or dry end: boards leaving the trimmer are sorted by dimension and grade into bins, counted into packages, and stacked into stickered kiln loads or shipping units. Secondary wood products plant (RTA furniture, flooring, moulding, pallet or cabinet component plant): operator takes rectangular cut parts off the saw/bander outfeed, sorts by size and quality, counts to the order quantity, and stacks them on pallets or carts in set patterns. Small custom shop or job shop, repeat batches: operator running a straight-line rip, chop saw or panel saw sorts cut blanks by length/width and defect, counts pieces per bundle, and hand-stacks on carts in a crowded shop with frequent job changes but standard rectangular parts.

Small custom shop, one-off work: short runs of odd-shaped, profiled, curved or delicate finished pieces (mouldings, chair parts, veneered panels) with no part labels; the operator eyeballs quality, culls defects, hand-tallies pieces and hand-stacks them by job on whatever cart or bench is free.

Portable/small outdoor sawmilling: sawyer cutting on a customer's property or open yard stacks and stickers green boards on dunnage over uneven ground, sorts by width/grade, and tallies board footage by hand, in weather and with no fixed layout.

Heavy or oversize stock: timbers, glulam beams, large cants or slabs moved by hoist, crane or forklift onto a saw table, carriage or CNC joinery infeed, then squared with guides and secured with dogs, wedges or wrench-tightened clamps; low-volume custom work.

Portable/open-yard sawing: a portable band mill at a customer's property or an outdoor log yard; the operator loads a log onto the mill bed with loader arms or a cant hook, levels it with wedges and tightens the log dog/clamp. Uneven ground, weather, different setup each site.

instances.label: Rough mill / secondary wood products plant (furniture, molding, flooring components): operator inspects hardwood boards coming off a stack or conveyor, measures usable clear lengths, and marks defects and cut lines with a UV crayon or chalk so an optimizing cross-cut saw cuts around knots and splits. Boards up to ~8-12 ft, indoors, high volume.

Sawmill / planer mill: sawyer or grader working a moving line measures board length and width, judges trim and grade, and marks boards (crayon/paint/grade stamp) to designate trim cuts, downgrades or reman. Noisy, dusty, fast-moving lumber, standard dimension stock.

Custom cabinet / millwork shop: worker pulls lumber or sheet goods from a rack, lays it on a bench or horses, measures with tape and framing square, and pencils or chalks cut lines - including allowance for defects, grain match, and odd-size or one-off parts - before cutting on a panel saw, table saw or miter saw.

Structural wood plant (truss, pallet, timber-frame, panelized housing): worker measures framing lumber, timbers or sheathing panels and marks cut lines, joint locations and layout lines from a cut list or shop drawing before feeding component saws.

Portable sawmill, log yard or outdoor site: operator measures logs, cants or slabs (length, diameter, sweep, defect placement), and marks bucking points or cut lines with crayon, paint or chalk line. Irregular stock, mud, weather, layout differs at every job.

tasks.label: Operate panelboards of saw or conveyor systems to move stock through processes or to cut stock to specified dimensions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Primary breakdown at a softwood dimension sawmill: the sawyer sits in a control booth/cab over the log line and works a panelboard (joysticks, setworks keypad, optimizer display) to run the log deck, turner, carriage or sharp-chain infeed and headrig/canter, positioning each log and cutting cants and boards to target sizes at high speed. Setting is a fenced, guarded sawline with conveyors presenting logs one way.

Secondary breakdown station (edger, gang, trimmer): operator at a panelboard/console accepts or overrides scanner solutions, sets fences and skew, indexes saws to the ordered widths/lengths, runs the conveyors, kickers and unscramblers, and stops the line for jams. Guarded machine line inside the mill.

Green sorter / stacker / planer-mill conveyor panelboard: operator moves stock through the process — lug loaders, bin drops, transfer decks, stacker, dip tank — matching bins to sorts and keeping flow balanced. Purpose-built conveyor line with operator platform.

Cut-to-size at a cabinet, door, or millwork plant: operator at the control panel of a CNC beam saw / panel saw loads the day's cut list, feeds panel stacks (forklift or lifting table), runs the cutting patterns, labels parts and manages offcuts. Fixed-layout shop floor built around people, with the saw as one station.

Small hardwood, pallet, or specialty mill: sawyer at the panel controls of a carriage headrig, scragg or resaw handling irregular, defect-laden logs, making grade/value calls on each face, controlling live decks and edger/trimmer conveyors. Older, mixed equipment on a purpose-built but crowded saw line.

tasks.label: Cut grooves, bevels, or miters, saw curved or irregular designs, and sever or shape metals, according to specifications or work orders.

instances.label: Cabinet/closet/millwork shop: producing panel parts from sheet goods per a cut list — dados and grooves, curved and irregular part outlines, 45° bevel/mitre-fold edge cuts — on a panel saw or CNC nesting router. Worker loads sheets, sets/calls the program, offloads, labels and stacks parts.

Millwork/furniture/frame plant: cutting miters and bevels on solid stock (moulding, casing, frame and face-frame parts) on an upcut/chop/miter or table saw per work order; batches of varying lengths and species, cutting around knots and defects, angle and depth reset between jobs.

Truss, wall-panel or timber plant: bevel/angle cuts, birdsmouths, notches, scarfs and grooves in dimensional lumber and beams per a component cut list; sawyer sets stops/blade angles, feeds crooked or wet lumber, marks and stacks parts.

Furniture/specialty wood shop: sawing curved or irregular designs — chair legs, curved rails, brackets, patterns — on a band saw or scroll saw following a template or scribed line, plus occasional bevel resawing.

Occasional severing or shaping of metal in the wood plant: cutting steel/aluminum stock, banding, brackets, extrusions or blade/knife stock to length or angle on a cold saw, metal band saw or abrasive chop saw per spec.

Cutting done outside the plant building: beams/timbers or stock cut to miter, bevel or notch at a lumberyard cut area, a jobsite trailer or a portable mill setup — uneven ground, weather, non-standard stock and layout that varies site to site.

tasks.label: Unclamp and remove finished workpieces from tables.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cabinet/furniture plant, CNC pressure-beam (panel dividing) saw: after each cut cycle the operator releases the beam/clamps, pulls the cut melamine or plywood panels (up to ~4x8 ft) off the saw table, checks edges for chipping, and stacks them by part on carts/pallets amid sawdust and offcuts.

Nested-based CNC router in a cabinet, closet or door shop: vacuum hold-down releases at cycle end; the operator lifts cut parts and offcuts off the spoilboard, labels and stacks them, and clears scrap and dust from the table before the next sheet.

Small custom/architectural millwork shop: sliding-table saw, radial-arm or band saw with jigs held by toggle, cam or hand-screw clamps; the worker frees the clamps and lifts finished, often odd-shaped, long or delicate hardwood pieces off the table, stacking them on carts in a crowded shop.

Solid-wood rough mill / component plant: optimizing crosscut, gang rip or double-end saw; the tender clears cut blanks and components from the outfeed table, sorts them by length/grade, discards defect pieces, and stacks them in bundles or trays.

Sawmill or heavy timber resaw/band mill: releasing hydraulic dogs or clamps holding a cant/timber on the carriage or table and moving the heavy finished cant, slab or beam clear of the machine to rollers or a stack.

Portable band sawmill or outdoor cutting station in a lumber yard, farm or job site: unclamping logs/cants on the mill bed and pulling off freshly cut boards on uneven ground, in weather, with no fixed layout.

tasks.label: Dispose of waste material after completing work assignments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Millwork/cabinet/furniture plant, end of shift: clearing sawdust, chips and small debris from the open floor and aisles of the sawing department (smooth concrete, institution-controlled premises) and collecting it for disposal.

At-machine cleanup after a run in a cabinet or millwork shop: vacuuming/sweeping sawdust from under and around the saw table, fences, rails and fixtures, blowing the machine down with compressed air, and sweeping cutoffs and dust into a scrap barrel beside the saw.

Sawmill or pallet mill: after a run, removing accumulated slabs, edgings, trim ends, bark and sawdust piled around the headrig/edger/trim saw, moving them into the hog or waste conveyor and separating burnable wood from metal-contaminated scrap; occasionally freeing a plugged waste chute.
Moving the filled scrap cart, gaylord or waste bin from the saw station across the plant to the dumpster, compactor or grinder area and returning an empty container to the station.
Servicing the dust-collection system at shift end: emptying cyclone drums or barrels, changing and tying off filter bags of fines, and carrying the bags/drums out to the outdoor dumpster or silo.
Portable sawmill, yard or jobsite sawing: gathering slabs, cutoffs and sawdust from around the mill on uneven, unmaintained ground and loading them into a truck, trailer, burn pile or scrap heap.

roles.description: Set up, operate, or tend woodworking machines, such as drill presses, lathes, shapers, routers, sanders, planers, and wood nailing machines. May operate computer numerically controlled (CNC) equipment.

tasks.label: Set up, program, operate, or tend computerized or manual woodworking machines, such as drill presses, lathes, shapers, routers, sanders, planers, or wood-nailing machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nested-based CNC panel processing in a cabinet/furniture/millwork plant: pull the job, load 4x8 sheet goods onto the router table, verify the nest program and tooling, run the cycle, then unload, label and cart the cut parts, clear offcuts and dust between sheets.

Tending a planer/moulder or multi-head profiling machine in a millwork or lumber plant: feeding rough or ripped stock, watching feed and surface quality, culling defects, catching and stacking the profiled output, making minor running adjustments during the run.

Sanding operations in a plant: feeding panels or solid-wood parts through a wide-belt/throughfeed sander, loading and unloading stacks, checking thickness and surface, changing belts, some hand detail sanding of edges.

Small custom cabinet/millwork shop: set up and run manual or semi-automatic machines (drill press, shaper with a jig, router table, lathe) on one-off or short-run parts of varying size; lay out and clamp the work, cut a test part, check fit.

Wood-nailing/assembly machine in a pallet, crate or box plant: place stringers/blocks and deck boards into the jig, cycle the nailer, unload and stack finished units, clear nail jams, change format for a different pallet size.

Job changeover and programming on CNC equipment: load or edit the part program, install and measure tooling, position vacuum pods/fixtures for the new part, run a first article, measure it and set offsets before releasing the run.

tasks.label: Examine finished workpieces for smoothness, shape, angle, depth-of-cut, or conformity to specifications and verify dimensions, visually and using hands, rules, calipers, templates, or gauges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: CNC router / point-to-point boring machine operator in a cabinet or wood-component plant: after a nest or program runs, the operator pulls finished panel parts off the outfeed, checks length/width with a tape or calipers, verifies hole positions and depths and dado depth-of-cut against the cut list, and inspects routed edges for tear-out or burn before releasing the batch.

Planer, wide-belt sander, or moulder tender in a millwork/dimension plant: pulls sample pieces from the run, measures thickness/width with calipers or a dial gauge, runs a hand over the face to feel for chatter, snipe, scratches or fuzzy grain, and checks a moulding profile against the knife template or a profile card.

Boring, mortiser/tenoner, dowel-inserter, or lathe operator in a furniture/component plant: gauges hole depth and spacing with a depth gauge or jig, test-fits a tenon or dowel, checks turned diameters and shoulder positions with calipers and a go/no-go template, and confirms squareness of ends with a try square.

Small custom cabinet, architectural millwork, or stair shop: one-off or short-run parts made from shop drawings; the operator eyeballs and hand-feels the finished piece for smoothness and machine marks, checks angles with a bevel/square, test-fits the part to its mating assembly, and judges acceptance by craft standards rather than a CAD model.

High-volume commodity work (pallet/crate nailing lines, flooring, moulding, blanks): rapid visual and template/jig checks on pieces as they come off the machine, pulling out off-spec or damaged pieces and confirming that sizes hold to the setup gauge over a long run.

sources.system: Creaform (AMETEK/FARO) MetraSCAN 3D-R / CUBE-R automated measuring cell

sources.claim: Robot-mounted optical CMM scanners in enclosed measuring cells (CUBE-R, M2/M3/M4 models with the robot, part table and calibration artefact inside a safety enclosure) perform automated at-line dimensional inspection of manufactured parts to 0.025 mm accuracy, comparing scanned geometry against CAD.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional verification of machined parts against CAD in metal/composite manufacturing. It transfers to woodworking inspection because the checks are the same (overall size, shape, angle, feature position, depth of cut, conformity to spec), wood parts are rigid and matte-surfaced, and shop tolerances for machined wood (roughly 0.25–0.5 mm) are an order of magnitude looser than the cell's 0.025 mm accuracy. Transfer holds only where the part is fixtured and presented inside the cell.

tasks.label: Start machines, adjust controls, and make trial cuts to ensure that machinery is operating properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cabinet/millwork shop CNC machining center or nesting router: operator loads the program, homes and warms the machine, verifies tool lengths/offsets and vacuum-pod or console positions, runs a test cut in scrap or on the spoilboard, checks dimensions with tape/caliper and the cut surface for tear-out, then edits offsets, feeds and speeds before the production run.

Millwork plant or planer mill moulder/planer: after a tooling change the operator sets spindle axes, fences, feed rolls and pressure elements, starts the machine, feeds several trial pieces, measures thickness/width and profile fit against a template or caliper, checks for snipe and knife marks, and trims axis positions until pieces run on size.

Wide-belt sander or thickness planer tending in a furniture/panel plant: set table height, belt grits and feed speed, start the machine, run a sample board or panel, measure resulting thickness at several points and inspect the scratch pattern, then adjust table and pressure settings before running the batch.

Multi-spindle boring machine, dowel inserter or drill press in a cabinet/furniture shop: set stops, spindle spacing and depth from a drawing or program, drill a test piece, check hole spacing, depth and squareness with a gauge or a trial hardware fit, and correct stops/depth before running the parts.

Edgebander, shaper or router table in a cabinet/furniture production shop: warm the glue pot or set fence/collet and cutter height, start the machine, run a trial panel or piece, inspect glue line, trim and profile quality, and adjust trimming units, pressure or fence position until the sample is acceptable.

Small custom/artisan shop with older manual machines (lathe, shaper, router table, single-head planer): operator sets fences and cutter height by rule and eye on varied hardwood stock, starts the machine, takes a test cut on offcut material, judges dimension by caliper and surface by feel/appearance, and nudges the setting repeatedly.

Small custom/architectural millwork shop: operator runs shaper, router table, drill press or lathe on one-off parts in variable solid wood, judging by sight, sound and feel, adjusting fences, depth of cut and feed rate to compensate for grain direction, moisture and warp, hand-checking with calipers and templates.

tasks.label: Examine raw woodstock for defects and to ensure conformity to size and other specification standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Millwork/moulding/flooring plant: operator at the infeed of a moulder, planer, rip line or double-end tenoner examines rough or S4S lumber on a cart or bunk before feeding — sighting for knots, splits, wane, shake, crook/twist, checking thickness and width with tape or caliper against the run spec, and pulling or re-sorting off-spec pieces.

Cabinet/casegoods shop or panel plant: CNC router / point-to-point / panel-machine operator inspects sheet goods (plywood, MDF, particleboard, melamine) before nesting — surface blemishes, delamination, core voids, edge damage, bow/warp, thickness check with caliper, and color/grain acceptability; rejects or downgrades bad sheets.

Furniture or flooring component plant rough mill: operator examines kiln-dried hardwood boards for defects and for grain/color acceptability before feeding a shaper, router, lathe or optimizing line; marks or crayons defects to be cut around, verifies grade and nominal thickness.

Small custom/architectural millwork shop: worker pulls one-off boards from racks, sights down them for crook, bow and twist, checks moisture with a handheld meter, measures with tape/caliper, and picks best faces for the job; stock is varied and non-standard.

Receiving/yard check: operator or lead verifies an incoming lumber, veneer or panel shipment on the dock or in the yard — piece count against the packing slip, species and grade stamps, nominal dimensions, moisture, and transit damage or staining — before releasing the lot to production.

tasks.label: Adjust machine tables or cutting devices and set controls on machines to produce specified cuts or operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Panel shop / cabinet plant: setting up a CNC router or point-to-point machining centre for a new job — calling up the program, selecting and loading tools in the changer, setting tool-length and part-zero offsets, positioning consoles/rails/vacuum pods for the part outline, setting spindle speed and feed, running and checking a first part.

Millwork/moulding plant: setting up a throughfeed moulder or planer for a specified profile — positioning each spindle axially and radially to the tool dimensions, setting bed/table and fence height, pressure and guide elements, and feed speed, then running and measuring a first piece and correcting.

Furniture/cabinet plant: setting up a multi-spindle boring or dowel-inserting machine — selecting spindles for the hole pattern, setting drilling depths, and positioning the table, fences and stops for the specified pattern, then verifying on a sample.

Solid-wood shop: setting a wide-belt sander, planer or planer-sander — keying in or cranking the table/conveyor to the target thickness, setting head pressure and feed speed for the specified stock removal, checking the part with calipers and re-setting the table.

Small custom/job shop: setting a conventional shaper, router table, drill press, lathe or single-end tenoner for a one-off or short-run part — clamping fences and stops, setting cutter height and depth by rule or gauge, making test cuts in scrap, measuring and dialling in.

Any of the above machines mid-run: parts drift out of tolerance or show tear-out, snipe, burn or chatter as tooling dulls or stock varies; the operator inspects parts, diagnoses the cause and re-adjusts table height, fence, pressure, feed speed or tool offsets to bring output back to spec.

tasks.label: Remove and replace worn parts, bits, belts, sandpaper, or shaping tools.

instances.label: Cabinet/furniture plant or millwork shop: operator of a CNC router / point-to-point boring-routing machining center swaps dull compression router bits, spiral bits and boring bits — pulling the worn tool holder, cleaning the collet/HSK taper, mounting the fresh cutter, re-measuring tool length and returning it to the magazine position.

Wide-belt, stroke or edge sander in a panel or furniture plant: worn abrasive belt (e.g., 43" x 75" or 6" x 100") is released, pulled off the drums, a new grit belt is threaded around drums/platen, tensioned, tracking/oscillation checked and machine test-run.

Smaller sanding media changes: hook-and-loop discs and pads on orbital/random-orbit and profile sanding heads, sanding sleeves on spindle sanders, brush/pad inserts — several changes per shift as abrasive dulls or grit sequence changes.

Shaper, moulder or double-end tenoner: dull profile cutterhead / shaping tool taken off the spindle (spindle nut and spacer stack or HSK/PowerLock interface), replaced with a sharp identical head, height/fence reset and a trial piece run.

Bench work replacing the cutting edges inside a head: indexing or swapping planer/moulder knives and inserts in a cutterhead, cleaning gibs, seating knives to a set projection in a jig, torquing gib screws in sequence, balancing the head.

Worn mechanical machine parts on lathes, planers, drill presses, routers or nailing machines: drive/V-belts, feed roller tires, chain, bushings, bearings, guides, hold-downs, pressure shoes, dust hood parts — lock-out/tag-out, guard removal, disassembly with hand tools, reassembly and adjustment.

tasks.label: Inspect pulleys, drive belts, guards, or fences on machines to ensure that machines will operate safely.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-shift walk-up condition check on a stationary production machine in a large millwork/furniture/panel plant (moulder, wide-belt sander, CNC router, boring machine): confirm blade/cutterhead hoods and belt covers are present, closed and undamaged; look through guard mesh for frayed, glazed or slack drive belts; watch/listen for wobbling pulleys, squeal or slip; flag anything abnormal for maintenance. Fixed layout, good lighting, machines at known locations.

Setup-time check of the fence/guide and guard on the machine being set for a run (shaper, jointer/planer fence, router table, tenoner, borer): verify the fence is square/parallel to the cutter within tolerance, that lock levers and clamp bolts are tight, that hold-downs and the adjustable guard are positioned and secured for the workpiece being run. Requires a square/rule, hand pressure on the fence, and judgment about the specific setup.

Periodic (weekly/PM) drive-train inspection: shut down and lock out, unscrew or swing open the belt cover/access panel, inspect V-belts or timing belts for cracking, fraying and glazing, press the belt to judge deflection/tension, check sheave/pulley alignment and set-screw tightness, feel/check bearings and motor mount for heat and play, close and refasten the guard.

Small custom cabinet or millwork shop: mixed-vintage machines crowded into a dusty shop whose floor space and stock piles shift job to job; operator does a combined pre-use check on whichever machine is next — guard in place, fence locked and true, belt cover on, belt not slipping — often with obstructed access around the machine.

First-use check on a machine just relocated, newly installed, or a portable machine set up in a yard or at ... customer/jobsite: verify belts were re-tensioned and pulleys aligned after the move, guards reinstalled, fence re-squared, machine level and stable, before the first run. Surroundings are unstructured and vary site to site.

sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot, with Orbit/AIVI-Learning powered by Gemini Robotics, performs autonomous visual inspection missions in industrial facilities, including EHS safety checks and asset monitoring such as detecting conveyor belt damage and reading gauges.

Transfers to the walk-up part of this task (belt damage, guard/cover presence, visible anomalies) because the objects (belts, rotating equipment, covers) and the standoff visual judgment are comparable; it does not cover contact checks such as belt deflection or fence lock tightness.

sources.system: Force/torque-sensing collaborative robot test cells

tasks.label: Clean or maintain products, machines, or work areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-run cleanup at the machine in a millwork/furniture shop: blowing, brushing or vacuuming chips and dust off the machine table, fence, guards and vacuum pods, and clearing offcuts before the next part is set up.
End-of-shift housekeeping of open floor and aisles: sweeping or vacuuming accumulated sawdust and small scrap from the shop floor around and between machines.
Dust-collection upkeep: emptying collector bins/bags, checking and changing filters, clearing clogged hoods, ducts and chip chutes on planers, moulders and sanders.

Preventive machine maintenance: greasing bearings and ways, checking/tensioning belts and chains, wiping rails and sensors, removing pitch and resin buildup from blades, bits and pressure rolls, minor adjustments per the maintenance chart.
Changing worn tooling and abrasives: swapping router bits, sanding discs/belts, shaper cutters, and reloading tool magazines as part of keeping the machine in condition.
Cleaning the product: dedusting or wiping machined parts and panels before finishing, brushing sanding dust out of profiles, scraping glue squeeze-out off assembled or edgebanded panels.

tasks.label: Attach and adjust guides, stops, clamps, chucks, or feed mechanisms, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cabinet/joinery plant: reconfiguring the workholding on a pod-and-rail or console CNC machining center for the next job — moving pod bars, consoles, suction cups, side clamps and locating stops to the program's positions, locking them down and proving the part is held.

CNC shop: preparing and mounting cutting tooling — seating router bits/drills in ER collet chucks and ISO30/HSK toolholders and torquing the collet nut with spanners, setting projection, loading holders into the tool magazine and entering tool data; also mounting a chuck or faceplate on a wood lathe.

Millwork/moulding plant: setting up a moulder, planer, shaper or tenoner — mounting cutterheads/spacers on spindles and torquing spindle nuts with wrenches, setting fences, chipbreakers, pressure shoes and feed-roller heights, attaching a power stock feeder, running a test piece and fine-adjusting.

Case-goods plant: setting a CNC boring/dowel-insertion machine or throughfeed drill for a part — positioning clamps, tongs, counter-blocks, fences and end stops to the panel size, then verifying hole positions on a first piece.

Panel plant: setting the guides and feed system of throughfeed machines — edgebander infeed fence, pressure beam and unit positions for a new panel thickness/edge, or a wide-belt sander's conveyor table height, feed-belt tracking and hold-down rollers.

Small custom/one-off shop: rigging up shop-made jigs, stop blocks, featherboards, hold-downs or fixtures clamped onto a router table, shaper, drill press or nailing/assembly machine for a nonstandard part, adjusted by eye and by test cuts with hand tools.

tasks.label: Trim wood parts according to specifications, using planes, chisels, or wood files or sanders.

instances.label: Cabinet/millwork plant: after the CNC router or shaper run, the operator hand-sands flat and panel-type parts — cabinet doors, drawer fronts, MDF and veneered panels, tabletops — with an orbital sander and block to remove mill marks and machine ridges, break the arrises, and bring the face to grit spec before finishing. Parts arrive in batches on a cart; dusty, noisy shop floor.

Furniture plant: sanding and filing contoured, turned, or profiled parts — chair legs and back slats, curved rails, moldings, raised-panel profiles — following the shape with a file, profile block, or random-orbit sander, feeling for tearout and fuzz, on mixed product lines with several styles running the same day.

Bench work trimming excess stock off machined or glued panel assemblies: flushing edgeband overhang and glue squeeze-out with a file, scraper, or block plane, paring protruding dowel and tenon ends with a chisel, and easing sharp edges so the part meets the dimensional and edge-quality spec.

Chisel and file work in recesses and joints: squaring the round corners a router leaves in a hinge, lock, or hardware mortise, cleaning out joint shoulders and mortise walls, and paring a recess to depth so the hardware or mating member seats flush against the layout marks or template.

Fitting a part to its mating assembly by hand: planing or sanding a solid-wood door edge, drawer box, or tenon iteratively — test-fit, mark the tight spot, remove a shaving, test again — until the reveal or joint fit matches the spec on a specific, slightly out-of-square assembly.

tasks.label: Grease or oil woodworking machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily/weekly lubrication of a CNC router or point-to-point machining centre in a cabinet or panel shop: pump grease into the fittings on linear rails and ballscrews (or run the machine's grease/oil cycle), check and top off the lube reservoir, wipe excess grease and dust off rails. Shop floor, machine powered down or in maintenance mode.

Scheduled PM lube round on production machines in a millwork or furniture plant (moulder, wide-belt sander, edgebander, boring/dowel machine): grease-gun a list of zerk fittings on feed-roll and shaft bearings, oil drive chains and slides, in a dusty, locked-out machine with guards partly open.

Small custom shop with older, mixed machines (jointer, shaper, drill press, lathe, planer): oil can on ways, slides and spindle oil cups, occasional zerk fittings, wipe/oil bare cast-iron tables, done ad hoc by the operator around a cluttered machine.

Periodic lubrication of hard-to-reach or enclosed points: spindle-bearing grease points behind covers or guards, gearbox/reducer grease fittings inside the machine enclosure, checking sight glasses and topping off oil reservoirs and auto-oiler cups.

Lubricating a machine outside the fixed plant: a portable/temporary mill or moulder set up in a yard or shed, or a machine being serviced at an installation site, with variable footing, weather, dust and no standard layout.

tasks.label: Start machines and move levers to engage hydraulic lifts that press woodstocks into desired forms and disengage lifts after appropriate drying times.

instances.label: Structural panel mill (plywood/LVL): operator at a multi-opening hydraulic hot press takes glued, pre-pressed lay-up stacks, charges the press openings, starts the press and engages the hydraulic rams, holds for the programmed cure time at set pressure/temperature, then opens the press and discharges panels for stacking. High volume, standard sizes, fixed layout.

Cabinet / architectural panel shop or plant: flat veneer or laminate overlay pressing. Operator lays up glued panels with faces, loads the cold or short-cycle hot press, engages the hydraulic lift/platen, times the press cycle for the adhesive, disengages and unloads panels to a rack for further curing. Batch runs of doors, tops, panels.

Furniture component forming: glued veneer stacks or thin laminations placed in a shaped die/caul on a hydraulic form (bending) press \curcurved chair backs, seat shells, curved door fronts — press engaged to force the stock into the form, held for the glue's cure time (often RF/heat assisted), then released and the part removed. Frequent mold changeovers.

Glulam / mass-timber plant: glue-spread lamellas laid up in a hydraulic beam press (straight, cambered or curved bed), hydraulic clamping engaged to press the stock to the beam contour, held for the required clamping/cure time, then released and the beam removed. Large, heavy stock; mixed straight and curved orders.

Small custom / job shop (millwork, boat, instrument, stair work): one-off bent laminations and glue-ups in shop-built forms and cauls on a small hydraulic press, clamp carrier or press frame; stock and form differ job to job, operator judges cure time by glue type and shop temperature and fits pressing around other machine duties.

Small shop one-off glue-ups of irregular assemblies: gluing curved or mitered subassemblies, odd-shaped furniture parts, patch/repair veneer work, hand-fitted cauls and clamps chosen for the part, glue squeeze-out cleaned by feel.

tasks.label: Set up, program, or control computer-aided design (CAD) or computer numerical control (CNC) machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Panel/cabinet plant, nested-based production on a 3-axis CNC router: destack and load 4x8 melamine/ply sheets onto the vacuum table, index against pop-up pins to set part zero, confirm the tool list in the ATC, call the nest program from the day's worklist, run, label and off-load parts, clear offcuts and keep the spoilboard flat. Repeated dozens of sheets per shift.

Point-to-point CNC machining center (pod-and-rail) or CNC boring/dowel machine in a millwork or furniture shop: set the worktable for the job (position support bars, pods, suction cups or clamps), load the solid-wood or panel workpiece, call the program, run drilling/routing/mortising, unload and spot-check dimensions before the next batch.

Routine job programming/changeover on standard parts: pull the part or cabinet from the CAD/CAM library (Cabinet Vision, Microvellum, Aspire, Maestro, Weinig CAM), generate/nest toolpaths and post to the machine, load the program at the control, run the first sheet/part and check key dimensions before releasing the run.

New or custom part: build the geometry in CAD/CAM from a shop drawing or customer file, choose tooling, cut order, feeds/speeds and a workholding strategy, simulate, then prove out on the machine 	rwith trial cuts, measure with tape/calipers, adjust offsets, tabs, depths and hold-down, and re-cut until the part is accepted.

Tooling and consumable set-up: assemble router bits/aggregates into collets and HSK/ISO holders, torque them, load the magazine positions, enter or verify tool data, replace or resurface the spoilboard, swap worn vacuum gaskets and pods, and check machine squareness/calibration after a crash or at shift start.

Small custom/one-off shop with a 4x8 or benchtop CNC router (ShopBot, Laguna, Avid): irregular solid-wood stock, slabs or offcuts held with clamps, screws or tape-and-glue, operator jogs to an XY zero on a corner, touches off Z with a plate, runs a bespoke program while watching for hold-down failure, then frees parts from tabs.

tasks.label: Operate nuclear power reactors in accordance with policies and procedures to protect workers from radiation and to ensure environmental safety.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steady-state at-power shift operation at the main control boards of a commercial LWR: monitoring reactor power, temperature, pressure and level; making reactivity and plant adjustments (rod motion, boration/dilution, feedwater/turbine) to hold the unit within Technical Specification, dose and effluent limits; acknowledging annunciators; peer checks and shift logs.

Planned reactor evolutions executed step-by-step from approved procedures: startup and approach to criticality, power ascension/descension or load change, shutdown and cooldown; reactivity management plan, key-operated switches, independent verification, continuous coordination with the shift supervisor and field operators.

Abnormal or emergency response from the control room: alarm/annunciator response, degraded or failed equipment, unexpected reactivity or coolant transients; diagnosing the cause, entering abnormal/emergency operating procedures, manually tripping the reactor or actuating safety systems if warranted, taking actions that limit any release.

Radiological and environmental compliance actions inherent in operating the unit: lining up and authorizing liquid and gaseous radwaste discharges under release permits and monitor setpoints, controlling containment purge/venting, adjusting plant conditions (cleanup, cooldown rate, shielding) to limit worker dose for planned maintenance, verifying effluents stay within license limits.

Local plant operations supporting an operating evolution inside the radiologically controlled area: locating tagged components, performing or verifying local valve/breaker manipulations and system lineups per procedure, taking local readings and samples in congested reactor/auxiliary building spaces under dose, contamination and heat constraints.

tasks.label: Adjust controls to position rod and to regulate flux level, reactor period, coolant temperature, or rate of power flow, following standard procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: PWR at steady full power: RO keeps Tavg on the temperature program and axial flux difference in the target band, making small control-bank/boron adjustments (or supervising rod control in automatic) as xenon burns in and grid load drifts, per plant operating procedures, from the main control room console.

Reactor startup / approach to criticality and low-power ascension: withdrawing control rods in prescribed increments toward the estimated critical position, watching source-range count rate and startup rate (reactor period) limits, taking the reactor critical and heating up / raising power into the power range under a startup procedure.

Planned power maneuver at a large LWR: coordinated down-power and return to full power for turbine valve testing, rod exercise surveillance, grid dispatch or end-of-cycle coastdown, holding prescribed ramp rates over hours while adjusting rods, boron and turbine load from the control boards.

BWR power control: adjusting recirculation flow (master flow / pump speed) for fine power control and moving control rods in the prescribed rod pattern/sequence during power changes and rod-pattern adjustments, staying inside thermal limits and the power/flow map.

Design-basis plant/grid load transient: turbine runback, large load rejection, grid frequency excursion or feed pump trip, requiring rapid reactivity and power adjustment (rod insertion plus steam dump/flow reduction) to hold parameters and avoid a reactor trip.

Degraded or abnormal condition requiring diagnosis and non-routine manual control: dropped or misaligned control rod, rod control system malfunction, instrument failure, or a xenon oscillation/AFD excursion after an unplanned transient, handled by abnormal operating procedures with rod control taken out of automatic.

instances.label: Steady-state watchstanding in the main control room: monitoring turbine-generator, feedwater/condensate, steam and auxiliary equipment indications and alarms, and making routine control adjustments (feed pump speed, level/pressure controllers, small load changes) at the benchboard, logging readings each shift.

Major control-room evolution on the secondary/BOP side: turbine rollup and warm-up, generator synchronization to the grid, load ramping, or plant startup/shutdown sequences performed step-by-step from written procedures with field-operator coordination.

Field rounds through the turbine hall, auxiliary and diesel buildings: taking local gauge, level, oil-sight-glass and temperature readings, checking pumps and motors for leaks, heat, noise and vibration, and recording the data on round sheets/logs.

Local operation of auxiliary equipment in the plant: manual valve lineups and throttling on handwheels/reach rods, swapping running and standby pumps, starting the auxiliary boiler, air compressors or diesel generator locally, adding oil, resetting/racking breakers.

Response to an anticipated equipment upset with a designed automatic/procedural response: feed pump or heater drain pump trip, turbine load runback, auto-start of standby equipment, controlled shutdown of a boiler or turbine to protect equipment.

Response to a novel or degraded abnormality: conflicting or failed instrumentation, an unexplained vibration/leak/temperature trend, determining the cause and improvising corrective actions or workarounds on equipment not covered cleanly by procedure.

instances.label: Refueling-outage restart at a US commercial reactor: the licensed crew in the main control room executes the general operating procedure from cold shutdown through fill/vent, heatup, control-rod withdrawal to criticality, condenser vacuum, turbine roll, generator synchronization and power ascension to 100% over 2-4 days, with tech-spec mode changes, peer checks, and coordination with non-licensed field operators doing local lineups.

Planned or grid-directed power reduction and reactor shutdown to hot standby: from the control-room panels the reactor operator lowers turbine load and reactor power (control rods/boron in a PWR, recirculation flow and rods in a BWR), removes the generator from the grid, and inserts rods to shut the reactor down, following the shutdown procedure with continuous parameter monitoring.

Post-shutdown cooldown and mode changes to cold shutdown for an outage: cooling down and depressurizing at controlled rates, placing residual heat removal/shutdown cooling in service, securing reactor coolant pumps and steam plant, establishing outage lineups and completing mode-change checklists, with field operators manipulating local valves and breakers under control-room direction.

At-power procedure implementation during a fuel cycle: holding reactor power, coolant temperature, pressure and levels within limits, executing procedure-directed power changes (coastdown, dispatcher-directed load changes, grid frequency response, rod-pattern or boron adjustments), and correcting small deviations and alarms from the control-room controls.

Routine control-room evolutions and surveillance tests per written procedure: starting, stopping and swapping pumps and trains, stroking valves, running periodic pump/valve/ESF surveillance tests with data recording against acceptance criteria, authorizing clearances/tagouts, and coordinating local steps with non-licensed operators.

Abnormal or emergency procedure implementation: reactor trip, loss of feedwater, load rejection or leak; diagnosing the condition, entering and executing the applicable abnormal/emergency operating procedure, stabilizing the plant, controlling inventory and heat removal under time pressure with degraded or unavailable equipment.

instances.label: Refueling outage core offload/shuffle/reload at a US PWR or BWR: working from the manipulator crane / refuel bridge over the flooded reactor cavity in containment, grappling fuel assemblies at indexed core grid coordinates, hoisting into the mast, traversing to the fuel transfer system upender, and executing hundreds of moves in the exact sequence of the approved core loading plan with per-move identity/position verification.

Spent fuel pool / fuel handling building moves: operating the spent fuel handling machine (pool bridge) to take assemblies off the transfer-system conveyor car, place them in indexed storage rack cells, perform in-pool shuffles, and bring new fuel from the new fuel elevator/storage rack into the pool and onto the transfer car for the core.

New fuel receipt and preparation: receiving shipping containers on trucks at the receiving bay, unloading with the overhead crane, unbolting/opening containers and removing wrapping, visual inspection and dimensional checks of each assembly, uprighting/upending, and moving assemblies into the new fuel storage vault or racks.

Handling of control components, inserts and tooling on the refuel floor: transferring RCCAs/control blades, thimble plugs and burnable poison inserts with the change fixture, changing grapples/masts/long-handled tools, rigging and setting up handling equipment, and other non-routine handling around the cavity and pool.

Dry cask loading campaign support: selecting and moving qualified spent assemblies from rack cells into the MPC/canister basket in the cask pit, verifying assembly IDs and heat load limits, and supporting cask rigging, lid placement and removal of the loaded cask from the pool.

Fuel inspection and special handling: underwater visual inspection or sipping of suspect assemblies, handling of leaking/damaged fuel into cans, fuel reconstitution or rod replacement work, and associated fixture setup in the pool.

instances.label: Routine shift rounds inside the turbine and auxiliary buildings: walking a fixed multi-floor route past pumps, motors, heat exchangers and tanks; reading local pressure/level/flow gauges, checking oil sight glasses, feeling/listening for abnormal vibration or noise, looking for leaks and hot spots, and logging the readings for the control room.

Local operation of equipment per procedure: throttling or cycling manual handwheel/lever valves, racking and closing breakers, starting or stopping pumps and fans at local panels, resetting relays and dampers, hanging and removing clearance/danger tags, and taking directed manual actions during an abnormal event or transient.

System lineup and independent verification walkdowns before startup or after maintenance: visually confirming each valve handwheel/lever position, breaker position, switch position and indicator light against a written checklist and signing off the lineup.

Dispatched field verification of a suspect indication: control room sends the operator to a named component to read the local gauge against the control room indication, look for leakage or overheating, confirm a level or a running/stopped state, and report back promptly by radio.

Inspection inside radiologically controlled areas: containment entry with the unit at power, high-dose or contaminated cubicles, spent fuel pool and dry-cask storage areas — visual inspection plus radiation/temperature survey, normally requiring PPE, dosimetry and dose-limited stay times.

Outdoor plant walkdowns in weather, day or night: switchyard and main transformers, diesel generator building, condensate/fuel-oil tank farm, circulating-water intake structure — visual and thermal checks, level readings, ice/debris checks.

instances.label: Substation/switchyard walkdown by a substation operator or dispatcher assigned to the station: visual check of power transformers, breakers, disconnects, bushings and arresters for oil leaks, corrosion, cracked porcelain; reading oil-level, gas-pressure and temperature gauges; thermal check for hot connections; logging anything off-spec. Energized outdoor yard, fenced and utility-controlled, fixed layout, any weather.

Check of dispatch/control-center and control-building equipment: SCADA consoles and servers, annunciator/alarm panels, communications and telemetry racks, UPS and station battery bank (cell voltages, electrolyte, terminal heat), standby generator fuel/coolant levels and leaks. Indoor, climate-controlled, utility-controlled premises.

Inspection of indoor switchgear rooms, relay houses and cable vaults at substations: metal-clad switchgear and relay panels for indicator flags, discoloration/overheating, arcing sounds, moisture ingress, blown fuses; verifying equipment ratings and settings match specification before or after switching.

Steam distribution variant: operator rounds through a boiler house / district-steam plant or distribution tunnel checking boilers, feed pumps, valves, steam traps, pressure-reducing stations and expansion joints for leaks, vibration, abnormal pressure/temperature gauge readings and insulation damage. Indoor industrial plant, hot and noisy, utility-controlled.

Field patrol of overhead distribution equipment along streets and rights-of-way: pole-mounted reclosers, sectionalizers, capacitor banks, cutouts, insulators, conductors and crossarms checked for damage, leaks, burned contacts and vegetation contact; findings logged as defects for work orders. Public roadside, layout varies feeder to feeder, traffic and bystanders present.

Post-fault / post-storm verification in the field: after a breaker lockout or severe weather, inspect the affected equipment and line section for damage (downed conductor, failed transformer, damaged switch) to confirm it is safe to re-energize. Off-hours, adverse weather, debris, unpredictable conditions.

instances.label: Control-room/console tending of station auxiliary systems: from a utility control center or plant control board, the dispatcher watches status and alarms for station batteries and chargers, transformer cooling banks, station-service supply, air compressors for breakers, HVAC and standby generators, starts/stops or transfers them via SCADA, acknowledges alarms and logs readings.

Routine walkdown round of a substation or switching station yard and control house: confirm cooling fans/oil pumps running, read charger and compressor gauges, check battery bank and oil/SF6 levels, take thermal readings, record values on the round sheet and report anomalies. Fenced, utility-controlled site, day or night, all weather.

Steam/district-heating or campus utility plant: tend auxiliary equipment supporting distribution - circulating and condensate pumps, feedwater and makeup pumps, air compressors, heat exchangers and motor-operated valves - monitoring pressures/temperatures, rotating lead-lag pumps, throttling flow and starting standby units to hold header setpoints.

Hands-on corrective/servicing tending in a station: reset a tripped charger or fan breaker, restart a stalled cooling pump, top off oil or coolant, replace a filter or desiccant, add water to battery cells, clean a strainer or panel, and test-run the standby generator.

Auxiliary distribution equipment away from the station: pole-mounted capacitor banks and voltage regulators on public streets, network protectors and transformers in sidewalk vaults, padmount reclosers - inspect condition, verify controller status, and operate/reset the device. Layout and access vary site to site; traffic, weather and confined space.

tasks.label: Take regulatory action, based on readings from charts, meters and gauges, at established intervals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control-room log round on a fossil or combined-cycle unit: at each established interval the operator reads MW output, throttle/drum pressure, drum level, steam temperatures, O2/CO, condenser vacuum, bearing temps on the DCS displays and recording charts, then makes regulating adjustments from the console — biasing fuel and air, trimming attemperator sprays, adjusting feedwater, changing load in response to dispatch — to hold every parameter inside its band and log the result.

Field/auxiliary operator round: at set intervals the operator walks the boiler house, turbine deck, pump and compressor rooms and fuel-handling areas of the plant, reads local gauges, sight glasses and panel meters, and takes the corresponding local action by hand — throttling a manual valve, adjusting a damper or gland seal, draining a sight glass, adding lube oil, shifting to a standby pump or swapping a strainer — then records readings on the round sheet.

Environmental/emissions compliance action at interval: operator reads CEMS NOx/SO2/CO/opacity, ammonia flow, scrubber pH and slurry density on meters and strip charts and adjusts SCR/SNCR reagent injection, scrubber reagent feed, or precipitator/baghouse settings to keep the unit inside permit limits at the current load.

Water chemistry / chemical feed regulation: at scheduled intervals the operator reads conductivity, pH, dissolved oxygen, phosphate and silica from online analyzers and panel meters on the boiler feedwater, condensate and cooling-water loops and adjusts chemical feed pump rates and blowdown to bring chemistry back to spec.

Hydro or small peaking plant: operator checks headwater/tailwater levels, unit MW, wicket gate position, bearing and winding temperatures at intervals and regulates gate opening, unit loading, or starts/stops a unit to hold pond level and meet the generation schedule.

Off-normal reading found on a scheduled check: a parameter is drifting outside its band or two indications disagree; the operator must judge whether the instrument or the process is at fault, then take the corrective regulating action (reduce load, shift equipment, isolate, call maintenance) and document it.

tasks.label: Start or stop generators, auxiliary pumping equipment, turbines, or other power plant equipment as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control-room start-up or shutdown of a major generating unit (combined-cycle/gas turbine or steam turbine-generator) on a dispatch or market schedule: the operator arms and initiates the unit start sequence at the DCS, watches purge, ignition, roll-up, warm-up, synchronization and loading, intervenes on hold points and alarms, and later unloads, opens the generator breaker and puts the unit on turning gear.

Start/stop of frequently cycled, remotely dispatched generation: simple-cycle peakers, reciprocating-engine plants and hydro units at unattended or centrally supervised stations, started and stopped on dispatch/AGC signals, sometimes several times a day, with synchronization and loading handled through SCADA/unit control.

Starting and stopping auxiliary equipment from the control room during normal operation: swapping boiler feed, condensate or circulating-water pumps, starting/stopping fans, air compressors, lube-oil pumps and cooling-water pumps as load changes or as equipment is rotated or removed for maintenance.

Local field start/stop of auxiliary equipment: the operator walks the plant to the pump, fan or compressor, checks lube-oil level, cooling and coupling, lines up manual suction/discharge and vent valves, racks in or closes a local breaker or presses the local start pushbutton, then verifies flow, pressure, temperature and vibration before reporting the machine in service (or secures and tags it out).

Emergency and abnormal starts and stops: tripping a unit or isolating failing equipment on a serious alarm (high vibration, loss of lube oil, tube leak), responding to a load rejection or grid disturbance, starting standby or emergency generators and standby pumps on loss of power or loss of the running machine, and coordinating the stop/restart with the dispatcher.

tasks.label: Monitor power plant equipment and indicators to detect evidence of operating problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control-room board watch at a fossil, combined-cycle or hydro plant: the operator scans DCS/SCADA screens, trend displays, annunciator alarms and mimic panels for deviations (rising bearing temperature, drifting drum level, falling vacuum, exhaust spread), cross-checking instruments against each other over a 8-12 hour shift.

Routine indoor field round through the operating plant (turbine hall, boiler house, pump and auxiliary rooms, water treatment): walking a fixed route up stairs and across gratings, reading local analog gauges, sight glasses and oil levels, looking for steam/water/oil leaks and puddles, listening for abnormal bearing or valve noise, checking for hot spots, and logging readings.

Outdoor/yard round in the plant's controlled premises: switchyard and transformers, cooling towers, fuel handling and conveyors, tank farm and chemical storage; visual and thermal checks of energized equipment, level and leak checks, in rain, heat or cold.

Alarm or abnormal indication prompts a check at a specific, known asset (e.g., 'go verify the local pressure gauge on B feed pump', 'check whether the transformer cooler is hot' ), confirming or dismissing the indication and reporting the local condition back to the control room.

Open-ended field troubleshooting: tracking down an unfamiliar noise, vibration, odor or leak whose source is unknown, following piping and systems off any fixed route, opening cabinets or local panels, using portable instruments (IR gun, vibration pen, ultrasonic probe) and judging severity and cause.

Heightened local surveillance during a transient: unit startup or shutdown, turbine roll-up, pump or mill start, or return to service after maintenance — standing watch at the machine, watching for vibration, leaks, smoke or abnormal behavior in real time and coordinating by radio with the control room.

instances.label: Routine operator round on an on-site distributed generation installation (fuel cell array on a pad, or microturbine/CHP skid in an equipment room) at a manufacturing plant, hospital, data center or campus: walk the unit line, read local gauges, panel displays and flow/pressure indicators, thermal-check inverters and switchgear, look for gas/water/oil leaks, listen for abnormal noise or vibration, check inlet filter differential pressure, log readings and flag anomalies.

Operating the units themselves: starting and stopping the fuel cell modules or microturbines, synchronizing to the grid and transferring to island mode, raising/lowering output to follow facility electrical and thermal demand, acknowledging and clearing alarms, restarting after a trip, and keeping the units dispatched through the unit control system, HMI and local switches.

Corrective maintenance and troubleshooting: diagnosing a fault or derate, isolating and locking out the unit, replacing sensors, injectors, fuel valves, inverter boards or a fuel cell power module, repairing a leaking fitting or coolant loop, then restoring, purging and test-running the unit, often alongside vendor field service.

Balance-of-plant and consumables work: fuel gas conditioning and booster-compressor checks, water treatment sampling and chemical dosing, condensate and waste handling, verifying fuel/hydrogen or DI-water deliveries, heat-recovery loop and cooling checks, housekeeping around the enclosures.

tasks.label: Open and close valves and switches in sequence to start or shut down auxiliary units.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control room of a gas/combined-cycle or coal unit: operator steps a start or stop sequence for an auxiliary unit (condensate pump, circulating water pump, instrument air compressor, fuel gas skid) using DCS soft controls and hardwired panel switches, checking permissives, opening/closing motor-operated valves in order and watching pressures, flows and amps until the auxiliary is in service or safely off.

Auxiliary equipment operator walks the plant to line up an auxiliary unit locally: opens and closes manual handwheel gate/globe valves on suction, discharge, seal water and cooling water lines (some stiff, chained, overhead or in tight pipe runs), vents and primes the casing, checks oil level, starts the pump at the local starter, then confirms discharge pressure and no leaks.

Field shutdown and isolation of an auxiliary unit (pump, fan, mill, heater, air compressor) for standby or maintenance: sequenced stop, closing local isolation valves, cracking vents and drains, lining up cooling water, and opening/racking the local breaker or disconnect, verifying the equipment is de-pressurized and stopped.

Nuclear plant auxiliary system valve and switch lineup under a formal written procedure with independent verification and radiological controls: heavy manual and motor-operated valves, sign-off of each step, position verification and documentation in radiologically controlled areas.

Hydro station or small/remote plant: starting or stopping unit auxiliaries (governor oil pumps, cooling water valves, air compressors, brake and seal air, station service) at a facility that is often unattended between visits, from the local control panel and by hand at the valves.

Off-normal case: an auxiliary fails to auto-start or must be placed in service fast after a trip or during an emergency; operator goes to the equipment under degraded conditions (alarms, steam or oil leak, hot or noisy space), troubleshoots, resets or jogs local devices, forces a stiff or partially seized valve, and gets the unit running against time pressure.

sources.system: Siemens Energy plant automation / remote operating center (Leipheim peaking plant; Volkswagen Autonomy72 plant)
sources.title: Autonomous Power Generation – The Future is Now (POWER Magazine, sponsored by Siemens Energy)
sources.claim: Gas turbine power plants run with no onsite operating staff: the Leipheim 300 MW peaker (operating since 2023) is controlled from a remote center 150 km away and ramps from idle to full load in under 30 minutes, and a Siemens Energy SGT-800 plant at Volkswagen runs fully autonomously for up to 72 hours including controlled and emergency shutdowns, so unit and auxiliary start/stop sequences are executed by machine-actuated valves, dampers and switchgear rather than by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Starting and stopping the unit necessarily sequences its auxiliary systems (lube oil, fuel, cooling, air); with no operator on site those valve and switch sequences are performed by installed actuators under the control system, which is the task in question.

tasks.label: Control or maintain auxiliary equipment, such as pumps, fans, compressors, condensers, feedwater heaters, filters, or chlorinators, to supply water, fuel, lubricants, air, or auxiliary power.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control-room control of auxiliary systems on a fossil/combined-cycle or hydro unit: starting, stopping and swapping condensate, feedwater, circulating-water, lube-oil and service-air machines from the DCS/HMI; adjusting feedwater-heater levels and drains, condenser vacuum/air-removal, deaerator level, fan dampers and compressor loading; placing auxiliaries in auto and acknowledging alarms during load changes and unit startup/shutdown.

Field rounds and local operation inside the plant (turbine hall, pump bays, compressor rooms, water-treatment building): walking the aux equipment, checking oil levels/sight glasses, bearing temperatures, seal leakage, vibration and discharge pressures; operating manual valves and handwheels, venting/priming pumps, shifting running/standby pumps and fans locally, resetting MCC breakers, and logging readings — over stairs, gratings and around hot piping.

Routine minor maintenance to keep auxiliaries in service: cleaning or swapping suction strainers, basket strainers and cartridge filters; backwashing/cleaning traveling screens and condenser waterbox debris; greasing bearings and topping up lube-oil reservoirs on pumps, fans and compressors; draining compressor moisture traps and cleaning air-intake filters.

Chemical/water-treatment auxiliary duty: operating chlorinators and biocide dosing on circulating/service water, adjusting dosing rates to residual-chlorine targets, sampling and testing water, changing out hypochlorite totes/chlorine cylinders and refilling chemical day tanks, checking dosing pumps and analyzers.

Abnormal-condition response and troubleshooting on auxiliaries: a pump cavitating on a clogged suction strainer, an air compressor tripping on high discharge temperature, a fan bearing running hot, a feedwater heater level control hunting, loss of condenser vacuum — diagnosing in field and control room, isolating and shifting to standby, clearing the fault or making a minor repair, and restoring the equipment to service.
