tasks.label: Clean, lubricate, or maintain equipment, such as generators, turbines, pumps, or compressors, to prevent failure or deterioration.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine lubrication round in a gas, coal, nuclear or hydro plant: operator walks the turbine hall, pump rooms and outdoor auxiliaries with grease gun and oil can, checks bearing sight glasses and lube-oil reservoir levels, tops off oil, greases motor/pump/fan bearings at grease fittings, wipes fittings and notes leaks. Points are at varied heights, in tight spaces, hot and noisy, on installed equipment that cannot be moved.

Cleaning equipment and its immediate surroundings: wiping oil, grease, coal or ash dust off pump casings, motors, turbine deck and control cabinets; blowing/vacuuming dust from cooling fins, air coolers and switchgear; hosing or sweeping washdown of the deck plate and grating around the equipment; cleaning up small oil spills.

Servicing filters, strainers and screens: swapping duplex strainer baskets on lube-oil, fuel-oil and service-water lines, replacing lube-oil and hydraulic filter elements (unbolting covers, draining, handling gaskets, re-torquing), changing gas-turbine inlet air filter cartridges, and clearing debris from cooling-water intake screens and trash racks.

Minor mechanical upkeep on generators, pumps and compressors: adjusting or repacking valve packing, tightening leaking flanges and fittings, replacing sight glasses and small gaskets, resetting couplings/guards, draining condensate pots and sumps, and assisting the maintenance crew on pump or compressor servicing during outages.

Scheduled cleaning of major heat-transfer and combustion equipment: initiating/monitoring soot blowing and ash removal on the boiler, condenser and heat-exchanger tube cleaning, air-cooled condenser fin cleaning, and gas-turbine compressor water washing, all inside the operating plant.

Renewable/hybrid generating site: operator-technician cleans PV modules or heliostat mirrors and clears dust from inverter, transformer and battery-container cooling surfaces and filters across a fenced, fixed-layout utility-scale plant.

tasks.label: Make adjustments or minor repairs, such as tightening leaking gland or pipe joints.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inside the plant (turbine hall, pump room, boiler feed area): a packing gland on a feedwater pump, valve stem or turbine seal is dripping. The operator brings a wrench, snugs the gland-follower nuts a fraction of a turn at a time, watches leak-off rate and gland temperature, and stops when leakage is acceptable without overtightening.

A flanged or threaded joint on a lube-oil, service-water, instrument-air or condensate line is weeping. The operator retorques flange bolts in a cross pattern or snugs a tube/compression fitting with two wrenches, then wipes it down and rechecks for leakage after a period of operation.

Routine minor servicing/adjustment of auxiliary equipment on rounds: snugging loose fasteners on covers and guards, filling/adjusting a packing lubricator, greasing fittings on a fan or pump bearing, swapping a plugged strainer basket, filter element or a failed local gauge.

Local operating adjustments at the equipment rather than the control room: throttling a manual valve or handwheel to trim flow/level, resetting a tripped local breaker or overload, tweaking a local controller/regulator setpoint, freeing or adjusting a damper linkage or limit switch.

Same kinds of minor tightening/adjustment but in outdoor or awkward plant locations: cooling-tower riser fittings, fuel/ash handling, boiler catwalks and elevated platforms, congested pipe galleries — done in weather, at height, or with restricted access around insulation and hot surfaces.

Urgent or more involved minor repair on a hot/pressurized system: isolate and tag the component, pull lagging or a cover, cut out and replace packing rings or a gasket on a valve or pump, reassemble and restore to service under time pressure with degraded, corroded or unknown-condition parts.

The physical act (engaging a nut/bolt with a socket and driving it to a target torque, with vision correction and thrust control) is the same act an operator performs when tightening a gland follower or flange bolts; torque range up to 500 N·m covers plant small-bore and gland hardware.

Startup, shutdown and abnormal-event work: bringing the capture train and CO2 compressor online or offline, responding to a compressor trip/surge, absorber foaming, solvent carryover or a CO2 leak, isolating and tagging equipment out for maintenance and returning it to service.

tasks.label: Operate, control, or monitor gasifiers or related equipment, such as coolers, water quenches, water gas shifts reactors, or sulfur recovery units, to produce syngas or electricity from coal.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine control-room shift work on a steady-running gasification train: watching DCS graphics and trends for the gasifier (coal/slurry feed, oxygen-to-coal ratio, temperature, pressure), syngas coolers/quench, water-gas-shift reactor, acid gas removal and sulfur recovery unit; making setpoint and ratio adjustments to hold syngas quality, sulfur removal and plant load within limits; recording logs. No upsets.

Control-room response to abnormal conditions and alarms on the gasification island: gasifier temperature/pressure excursion or slagging, plugged quench line, burner or feed-pump trip, SRU/tail-gas upset, high H2S in treated syngas. Operator diagnoses from instruments, takes corrective action or trips the unit, coordinates with field operators and maintenance, and returns the train to normal.

Startup, shutdown, load ramps and gasifier-train switchovers: purging and inerting, warming refractory, burner light-off, introducing coal slurry and oxygen, bringing quench/shift/AGR/SRU online, routing syngas from flare to the combustion turbine, then reversing the sequence — coordinated between the control room and field operators over many hours.

Field operator rounds through the gasification island: walking multi-level outdoor/indoor structures and hazardous (classified) areas, reading local gauges and sight glasses, checking pumps, compressors, coolers and the SRU for leaks, vibration, abnormal noise or temperature, checking levels and valve positions, and reporting/logging findings back to the control room.

Hands-on field operating actions on the gasification equipment: manual valve line-ups and block/bleed operations, swapping pumps, strainers and filters, draining condensate legs, pulling process samples (syngas condensate, sour water, molten sulfur, slag), rodding or steaming out plugged lines, washing down slag handling, and locally starting/resetting equipment.

instances.label: Routine water/steam cycle chemistry grab samples at an indoor sample panel/sample sink in the turbine building: operator opens a cooled sample valve, flushes the line, rinses and fills labeled bottles (condensate, feedwater, boiler water, cooling water), caps, logs, and walks them to the plant chemistry lab.

Lubricating/hydraulic/seal oil samples taken at the machine in turbine hall, pump rooms and diesel-generator rooms: operator reaches a sampling port or bearing drain on a running unit (hot, oily, cramped access, ladders/gratings), purges dead oil, fills and caps a sample bottle, labels it and sends it for oil analysis.

Insulating oil samples from main/auxiliary transformers, LTCs and oil circuit breakers in the outdoor switchyard: operator connects a syringe or bottle to the drain valve on energized oil-filled equipment, purges, draws an air-free sample for DGA/dielectric testing, in outdoor weather under clearance rules.

Station battery room: operator draws electrolyte from individual lead-acid cells with a hydrometer/syringe for specific-gravity checks and occasional lab analysis, working over open cells in acid PPE and returning residual electrolyte to the cell.

Sampling at a hazard-controlled sampling station (nuclear-plant secondary/primary chemistry sample room, or high-temperature/high-pressure and chemically hazardous sample sink): sample drawn under procedure into a shielded or sealed container, surveyed/labeled, chain-of-custody paperwork, delivered to the counting/chemistry lab.

Outdoor environmental/effluent grab samples on plant grounds: discharge outfall, cooling-tower basin, intake canal, ash/settling pond or oily-water separator; operator walks or drives to the point, dips a bottle or pole sampler from a bank or platform in the weather, preserves and labels the sample for the lab.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shift rounds through the plant's indoor electrical areas — 4160/480 V switchgear lineups, motor control centers, bus duct, station service transformers, DC/battery panels: visual check of indicators, breaker/relay flags, oil/liquid levels, temperature and load gauges, thermal-camera or IR-thermometer scans through viewing windows, listening for arcing or abnormal hum; readings logged and anomalies written up.

Walkdown of the outdoor switchyard / generator step-up and station transformers: transformer oil level and temperature gauges, cooling fans, bushings, SF6 breaker pressures, disconnect positions, corrosion and leaks, IR scan of bus and cable terminations; readings logged in the round sheet and abnormalities reported. All weather, energized high-voltage yard, fenced and access-controlled.

Handheld instrument measurements on distribution equipment during rounds or pre-maintenance checks: clamp-meter load currents on feeders, DC bus and battery cell voltages with a multimeter, ground-detector and control-power checks — requires opening panel doors or cubicle covers, wearing arc-flash PPE, and placing probes/clamps on terminals, then comparing to acceptance limits.

De-energized functional and diagnostic testing of a specific device before return to service: insulation resistance (megger) on a motor feeder or cable, breaker trip/close and contact-resistance test, protective relay injection with a test set — requires isolation/LOTO, racking out, connecting test leads to studs and terminal blocks, running the test and judging the result against limits.

Response to an electrical alarm or abnormality (ground alarm, tripped breaker, lost control power, hot spot found earlier): troubleshoot with a meter across several points to localize the faulty component (blown fuse, failed contactor, loose lug, failed relay), decide whether to isolate and switch load, and notify maintenance with findings.

tasks.label: Place standby emergency electrical generators on line in emergencies and monitor the temperature, output, and lubrication of the system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Unplanned emergency at a generating station: loss of offsite/station power or a bus undervoltage. The standby/emergency diesel generator must start within seconds, be brought onto the emergency bus with loads sequenced on, and its voltage, frequency, kW output, jacket-water temperature and lube-oil pressure watched from the control room while the event is handled.

Deliberate placing of a standby unit on line during degraded or anticipated-loss conditions: operator brings the unit up to speed and voltage, matches frequency/phase (sync scope or auto-synchronizer), closes the generator breaker, adjusts governor and excitation to pick up and share load, then monitors output, temperatures and lube-oil pressure from the control room / switchgear room.

Scheduled exercise or on-load test of a standby emergency generator (weekly/monthly per NFPA 110 or plant tech specs): start the unit, parallel it or transfer load to it, run 30-60 minutes, log temperatures, output and lube-oil pressure at intervals, verify no alarms, then unload and secure the unit.

Extended run during a prolonged outage: hourly field rounds at the running emergency generator — read local gauges (jacket water and lube-oil temperature/pressure, exhaust temperature, day-tank level), infrared/temperature checks on bearings, cables and breaker connections, look and listen for leaks and abnormal noise, log the readings and flag deviations.

Hands-on field intervention: the generator fails to auto-start or trips, so the operator goes to the generator room, lines up fuel valves, cranks the unit at the local panel, checks lube oil level with a dipstick, tops off oil or coolant during a long run, resets local devices and wipes/traces leaks before returning the unit to service.

tasks.label: Diagnose or troubleshoot problems with gas collection systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Landfill/biogas gas-to-energy plant: inlet methane/BTU is falling and oxygen is up. Operator goes into the wellfield, takes wellhead readings (CH4/O2/CO2, vacuum, temperature) across the affected area with a portable gas analyzer, identifies the wells pulling air or over-drawn, rebalances valves and re-reads to confirm the diagnosis. Uneven refuse slopes, mud, weather.

Odor complaint or surface-emission exceedance: operator must find where gas is escaping across a several-hundred-acre site — cover cracks, penetrations, wellhead seals, above-ground header joints — using a hand-held FID/TDLAS detector on a walking grid, and attribute the escape to the responsible collection-system deficiency.

A leg of the collection field loses vacuum or flow: operator traces the lateral and header, checks condensate sumps, traps and pneumatic pumps, opens access points, dewaters a liquid-loaded well, finds a crushed/settled or frozen pipe or a plugged orifice, and verifies restoration of flow. Hands-on work outdoors on the fill.

Blower/flare/gas-conditioning skid in the fenced plant compound: fault that is identifiable by inspection and sensing — a leaking flange or shaft seal, a hot bearing or motor, an off-normal gauge/transmitter, a combustible-gas alarm — operator walks the skid, reads gauges, sniffs/scans for leaks and identifies the offending component.

Same plant compound, fault requiring hands-on isolation to diagnose: drain the knockout pot to check for moisture carryover, swap or open a coalescing filter to confirm high differential pressure, cycle valves to isolate a section, reset and re-light a flare pilot, clear a plugged drain.

Control building / analyzer shelter: operator uses SCADA and historian trends plus alarm history to decide whether a gas-collection indication is a real process problem or an instrument fault, verifies the on-line gas analyzer with calibration gas, checks transmitter loops, and directs field checks.

tasks.label: Monitor well fields periodically to ensure proper functioning and performance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Geothermal plant: operator makes a periodic round of production wellpads on company-controlled land reached by graded gravel roads — reads wellhead pressure/temperature gauges and flow meters, checks valve positions, looks and listens for steam/brine leaks, scaling, corrosion and abnormal noise in H2S atmosphere, logs readings against expected performance.

Landfill-gas-to-energy plant: operator/technician walks the gas extraction well field on the landfill cover, connects a portable gas analyzer at each wellhead sample port to read methane, oxygen, CO2, vacuum and temperature, throttles the well valve to tune it, notes damaged wellheads, liquid levels and settlement, and reports field-wide performance.

Thermal/geothermal plant water supply or reinjection well field: operator checks small pump houses and wellheads across plant property — pump amps and discharge pressure, water level, seal/packing leaks, strainer condition, flow totalizers — and confirms the wells are meeting the plant's makeup or injection duty.

Periodic patrol of outlying wells and the gathering/injection pipeline right-of-way over rough, steep, partly wildland terrain (often after storms, snow or heavy rain): checking for steam plumes, insulation damage, slumped ground, washed-out access, vegetation and animal damage, with no fixed layout between pads.

Abnormal-condition trip: monitoring shows a well off-spec (pressure/flow/temperature deviation, oxygen intrusion, or declining output); the operator goes to the wellhead, investigates the cause (scale, liquid loading, plugged lateral, leaking or failed valve, pump trouble), makes the corrective valve adjustment or isolates the well, and reports findings.

tasks.label: Operate landfill gas, methane, or natural gas fueled electrical generation systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility or merchant natural-gas station control room: on a dispatch order, start a combustion turbine or combined-cycle unit, bring it through purge/ignition/acceleration, synchronize the generator to the grid, ramp and hold MW/MVAr on AGC, watch temperatures, pressures, vibration and emissions, and shut the unit down at the end of ....

Landfill-gas or digester-gas engine plant: keep several reciprocating gensets online on gas whose methane content, moisture and pressure swing through the day; trim load and air-fuel, start and stop engines as gas availability changes, coordinate with the blower/flare, and hold emissions in compliance.

Field/auxiliary operator work supporting the running units: rounds through the engine hall and turbine deck reading local gauges and oil levels and checking for leaks, heat and vibration, plus the hands-on part — manual valve lineups and permissive/purge checks before a cold start, draining condensate knockouts, swapping gas filters and coalescers, topping up lube oil, locally starting pumps and fans.

Abnormal condition inside the unit's control envelope: exhaust temperature spread, high vibration, engine knock, fuel-gas pressure excursion or a grid disturbance — unload, take protective action, execute a controlled or emergency shutdown, then restart the unit per procedure once conditions clear.

Trip that requires physical field diagnosis and restoration: gas train lockout, plugged filter, tripped local device or failed sensor — walk to the equipment, find the cause, isolate or reset locally, and get the unit back on line.

Unmanned peaker, CHP or distributed natural-gas genset site overseen from a central location: the unit must start on a dispatch or outage signal, pick up load, run through the event and shut down, with one operator covering several such sites.

tasks.label: Repair or replace gas piping.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-bore fuel-gas work inside the plant: operator finds a weeping 1/2"–2" threaded fitting, gauge line, drip leg, strainer or instrument tubing on a gas turbine fuel-gas skid or burner front. Isolate and lock out, bleed/purge, break the corroded threaded joint with wrenches in congested piping, re-thread/replace nipple or fitting with sealant, re-pressurize and soap/sniffer leak-check.

Flanged component or short spool replacement on the fuel-gas header: isolate and nitrogen-purge, unbolt seized flange studs (sometimes overhead or on a pipe rack), rig out the old valve/strainer/spool, set new gasket, align flanges, torque bolts in star pattern, pressure test and return to service during an outage.

Welded carbon-steel fuel-gas pipe section replacement during a scheduled outage: cut out a corroded/cracked section of 2"–12" gas pipe in place, bevel and fit up a new spool piece, weld (or have welded) root and fill passes to code, NDE the welds, purge and leak/pressure test the line before return to service.

Outdoor gas yard / metering-and-regulating station within the plant fence: repair or replace piping, regulators, filter/separator connections or buried-to-aboveground transitions; weather exposure, mud or gravel, sometimes shallow excavation, mix of threaded, flanged and welded joints.

Unplanned in-service leak response: combustible-gas alarm or odor during operation; operator locates the leak (often elevated on scaffolding/ladder, behind insulation or in a tight equipment enclosure), isolates the affected leg, applies a temporary clamp or replaces the leaking fitting/section under time pressure, then re-tests and restores fuel supply.

It does not transfer to work on installed piping.

tasks.label: Trace electrical circuitry to ensure compliance of electrical systems with applicable codes or laws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine in-plant configuration walkdown of the station electrical distribution: the operator traces feeders and control circuits through MCCs, switchgear line-ups, distribution and DC panels against controlled one-line diagrams and panel schedules, opening cabinet doors, comparing tags and breaker ratings, and flagging mislabeled, abandoned or unauthorized circuits. Indoor plant electrical rooms, energized gear, arc-flash PPE.

Tracing one specific circuit through the plant during troubleshooting or pre-job verification: following a conductor from its breaker through conduit, junction boxes, cable trays and terminal cabinets to the load, using a tone tracer/clamp meter to positively identify it, and confirming isolation and grounding per NFPA 70E before work is authorized.

Compliance inspection and sign-off of newly installed or modified wiring in the plant (contractor instrument loop, temporary power, added receptacle circuit, replaced cable): verifying conductor size/ampacity, conduit fill and support, bonding and grounding, terminations, labeling and arc-flash marking against NEC/NFPA 70E and station standards, then documenting acceptance.

Shop bench check-out before energization: point-to-point verification of a newly fabricated or rewired control/relay panel or a multiconductor cable at the plant electrical shop bench \ontinuity against the schematic, megger/hipot insulation checks, confirming no crossed or mislanded conductors \documented for turnover.

Outdoor switchyard and yard tracing: following control and power cables in the switchyard, cable trenches and outdoor enclosures, verifying ground-grid connections, cable identification and physical condition against drawings and code, in weather and around energized high-voltage equipment.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operator rounds/inspection in a power plant (E2). It establishes that mobile robots work in this setting, but the demonstrated capability is camera/thermal data capture on fixed routes, not opening panels, probing conductors, or judging code compliance, so it does not substantiate this task.

tasks.label: Operate biomass fuel-burning boiler or biomass fuel gasification system equipment in accordance with specifications or instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steady-state operation of a wood-fired/multifuel boiler (fluidized-bed or grate/stoker) at a utility, district-heating or mill CHP plant: from the control room, holding steam pressure/temperature, bed and furnace temperature, fuel feed rate, combustion air and O2/CO within the operating specification while following load and staying inside permit limits.

Startup and shutdown of the boiler or gasifier per written procedure: furnace purge, support-fuel light-off, bringing feeders, fans and pumps on line, warming and ramping to specified pressure/temperature, then controlled shutdown or hot standby.

Local/field operation during a shift in the boiler house: rounds to read local gauges and levels, operate manual valves and dampers, locally start/stop feeders, fans, pumps and ash conveyors, verify lineups, and take fuel/ash samples, over stairs, grating and hot piping.

Control-side upset handling: wet or variable-quality fuel, fuel-feeding disturbances, bed/furnace temperature excursions, high CO or opacity, load rejection and alarm/trip conditions, corrected by adjusting fuel, air and load per the operating specification.

Physical intervention upsets: rodding a bridged fuel chute or plugged feed screw, removing tramp material, breaking clinker/slag, unplugging ash removal, so the boiler can be returned to specified operation.

Operating a biomass gasification system (containerized wood-gas CHP unit through to a larger gasifier island): holding gasifier bed temperature and fuel level, managing producer-gas quality and cleanup, char/ash discharge, and the coupled engine/boiler or flare, per manufacturer instructions.

tasks.label: Perform tests of water chemistry in boilers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily routine boiler-water check at a small biomass plant: technician walks to the boiler blowdown/drum sample cooler on the plant floor, opens the sample valve, purges and cools the line, rinses and fills a sample bottle, carries it to the small plant lab bench, and runs pH, conductivity, P/M alkalinity titration, hardness drop test and sulfite/phosphate colorimetric tests; logs results in the chemistry log and adjusts chemical feed or blowdown.

Multi-point water/steam cycle round: samples drawn at several panels around the plant (softened makeup/demineralized water, condensate, deaerator/feedwater, boiler drum, sometimes economizer), each purged and cooled, tested for the relevant parameter set (conductivity, hardness, pH, silica, sulfite/oxygen scavenger, phosphate), and results trended against control limits.

Bench-only analysis in the plant chemistry lab: sample bottles already collected are lined up on the bench; technician performs the standardized analytical procedures (titrations with burettes/digital titrators, photometer/colorimeter tests, conductivity and pH meters), rinses glassware, verifies meter calibration, and records results to the log or LIMS.

Verification and calibration of the continuous online instruments at the steam-and-water analysis (SWAS) panel: running standard solutions through pH/cation-conductivity/sodium/silica analyzers, comparing analyzer readings to a fresh grab-sample bench result, replenishing reagents and standards, adjusting calibration and documenting the check.

Off-normal or non-routine testing episode: an alarm or odd result (rising conductivity, silica breakthrough, suspected hardness leak, carryover, oil or condensate contamination) triggers repeat and expanded testing on streams that may not be instrumented, ad-hoc methods (e.g., iron/corrosion-product or chloride tests), judging whether results are valid, resampling, and recommending corrective action.

sources.claim: Hach NA5600sc online sodium analyzer for power-cycle water performs continuous measurement with built-in automatic calibration and electrode reactivation, needing reagent replenishment only every 90 ...; available in multi-channel versions for several sample streams.
sources.transferJustification: Sodium/cation-conductivity monitoring of boiler feedwater and condensate is one of the water-chemistry tests biomass/steam plant technicians perform; the analyzer draws the piped sample, doses reagents, measures and self-calibrates, producing the same accepted output (a logged in-spec/out-of-spec chemistry value).

tasks.label: Operate high-pressure steam boiler or water chiller equipment for electrical cogeneration operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steady-state control-room operation of the biomass-fired high-pressure boiler and turbine-generator through a shift: holding drum level, steam header pressure and temperature, bed/grate temperatures and O2 by trimming fuel feed and combustion air, following the host's electric and steam load, logging readings.

Startup, shutdown and major load transitions: furnace purge and light-off of start-up burners, raising pressure on a warm or cold boiler, rolling and synchronizing the turbine-generator, ramping to load, and executing controlled shutdowns after a run.

Field operating rounds and local operation in the boiler house and fuel yard: reading local gauges and gauge glasses, checking feedwater pumps, ID/FD fans and feeders for leaks, heat and vibration, cracking drains and manual valves, taking bottom blowdown, pulling boiler-water grab samples and trimming chemical feed.

Operating the chilled-water/absorption chiller equipment served by the cogeneration plant (campus or district cooling, process cooling): starting, staging and stopping chillers with their pumps and cooling towers, setting chilled-water supply temperature, matching tonnage to load, watching condenser approach and purge.

Handling upsets and abnormal conditions: high bed temperature or slagging, bridged fuel in the silo or a plugged chute/feeder jam, ash-system plug, boiler trip and restart, suspected tube leak - requiring both control-room action and hands-on intervention out in the plant.

sources.system: Siemens Energy Omnivise T3000 / BosB72 autonomous operation, VW Wolfsburg CHP plant
sources.title: Volkswagen Power Plant, Germany: 72 hours of plant autonomy

tasks.label: Operate equipment to heat biomass, using knowledge of controls, combustion, and firing mechanisms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steady-state firing control from the plant control room of a wood-fired power/CHP boiler (stoker-grate or fluidized bed): watching steam pressure/temperature, furnace or bed temperature, O2/CO, opacity, and trimming fuel feed rate, grate speed/bed level, and primary/secondary air to hold load as fuel moisture and species vary over a shift.

Starting up or shutting down the firing system: purging the furnace, lighting oil/gas start-up burners, warming the boiler on a controlled ramp, cutting over to solid biomass firing and bringing feeders and air fans into service (or the reverse for a planned shutdown), inside the boiler house and control room.

Keeping fuel moving to the fire during firing: running the reclaim/silo/crane and conveyor-feeder train that fills the surge bin and furnace chutes, setting feeder and metering speeds, and blending wet and dry fuel to match the boiler's demand in a covered fuel storage building.

Field monitoring rounds while the unit fires: walking the boiler house and fuel handling floors on standard routes, viewing the fire bed through sight ports, reading local gauges and temperatures, checking feeders, drives, fans and ash conveyors for heat, noise, vibration and leaks, and reporting back to the control room.

Hands-on field intervention on the firing equipment during operation: rodding out bridged fuel in a chute or hopper, breaking clinker or slag off the grate/refractory, clearing an ash conveyor, cleaning a sight glass or igniter, stroking a stuck damper and operating local manual valves at the boiler.

Responding to combustion upsets and trips: high CO or opacity excursion, bed defluidization or low bed temperature, feeder trip, furnace pressure excursion, or a fuel-handling fire — diagnosing quickly from panel and field indications, taking manual control of firing, and recovering or safely tripping the unit.

instances.label: Control-room start-up and shutdown sequencing of the biomass boiler and turbine-generator: checking permissives, initiating start-up burners/purge/light-off, bringing fans, feedwater and fuel feeders into service, rolling and synchronizing the generator, or taking the unit off line on schedule. Work is done at the DCS console in the plant control room.

Regulating the unit during normal operation: trimming solid-fuel feed rate, primary/secondary air, bed or grate temperature, furnace draft, drum level, steam pressure and temperature, and generator MW output to follow dispatch or host steam demand, while keeping emissions in limits. Done from the DCS console.

Field/local operation and system line-ups inside the plant: walking the boiler house and turbine hall to open and close manual valves, start and stop pumps, blowers and hydraulic packs at local starters and panels, position dampers and drains, swap running/standby equipment, and place equipment in or out of service with tagging/LOTO. Layout is fixed but devices are hand-operated and scattered over multiple levels.

Operating fuel- and ash-handling auxiliaries: running the fuel yard/bunker grab crane or loader feed, conveyors, screws, metering bins and stokers to keep the boiler fed with wood chips/hog fuel, and running ash conveyors, drag chains and silo unloading. Dusty, noisy, institution-controlled indoor/outdoor plant areas.

Protective or emergency shutdown when a fault is detected: tripping the fuel feed and burners, tripping the turbine-generator, and placing the unit in a safe state on loss of flame, drum level, or other critical parameter.

Abnormal-condition response and recovery: diagnosing an upset or trip, clearing plugged chutes, bridged fuel in bins or jammed feeders and conveyors, dealing with clinker, tube leaks or tripped auxiliaries, then re-lining up and restarting the affected system. Requires field troubleshooting with hand tools on non-standard blockages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine operating rounds inside the plant (boiler house, turbine/generator hall, pump and fan rooms): walk the fixed route, read local gauges and sight glasses, look and listen for steam/water/oil leaks, hot bearings, abnormal noise or vibration, log readings on the rounds sheet and report anomalies to the control room.

Fuel-handling walkdown: belt conveyors, transfer chutes, hoppers, screens, drag chains and hammermills in dusty covered galleries — check belt tracking, spillage, plugged chutes, overheated idlers/bearings, worn liners, and report what is found.

Outdoor/yard and external structure inspection: fuel storage yard and silos, outdoor conveyor galleries, ash silos, stack and ductwork exterior, cooling equipment, transformers/switchyard — walked in all weather, documenting leaks, corrosion, hot spots and physical damage.

Targeted condition check of one suspect asset after an alarm or operator report: go to the pump/fan/motor, take a temperature reading, listen for bearing or seal noise, look at the seal and oil sight glass, then write the deficiency up as a work order.

Hands-on mechanical inspection: remove a guard or inspection cover, check oil level and condition, feel belt/chain tension and check sprocket and knife wear, check for loose fasteners, rotate a coupling by hand, then record findings.

Outage/shutdown internal inspection: enter the cooled, ash-covered, scaffolded boiler, grate and ash-handling interior; inspect waterwall tubes, refractory, grate bars and superheater for erosion, cracks and wear; measure and document damage to scope the repair.

Bringing a unit on or off line: light-off and warm-up, rolling the steam turbine, synchronizing the generator to the grid and ramping load, or a controlled shutdown - control-room sequencing plus field valve line-ups, drain/vent operation and local walkdown checks.

Anaerobic digester or landfill-gas site: operating the gas train and reciprocating engine-gensets - starting and stopping engines, adjusting gas flow/blend and flare changeover valves, setting load, and holding output as biogas quantity and quality vary.

Ethanol or biodiesel plant: setting pump rates and control valves for feed and slurry, fermenter fills and transfers, distillation column steam and reflux, and methanol/catalyst dosing to hold production rate and product spec.

tasks.label: Calculate, measure, load, or mix biomass feedstock for power generation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Enclosed-store plant: keep the boiler's fuel hopper continuously charged from a covered fuel hall or bunker of wood chips/waste wood. Technician runs the grab crane or reclaim conveyors, watches hopper level and bunker inventory, and repositions fuel tipped into the reception pocket so feed never starves.

Open fuel yard: reclaim hog fuel, bark, chips or ag residue from outdoor piles with a front-end loader, push up and shape piles, and charge the reclaim hopper/truck dumper. Work in rain, snow, mud and dust, amid arriving delivery trucks, with fuel varying in size and wetness.

Blend to spec: proportion wet green chips with dry pellets/sawdust, or wood with bark, peat, RDF or ag residue, to hit target moisture, ash and heating value for stable combustion - layering the pile, mixing in the bunker with the grab, or setting dosing/feeder ratios.

Measure and calculate: take representative samples from incoming truck/rail loads and the pile, determine moisture (and ash/size/contaminants), compute energy content and tonnage for fuel payment and inventory, and calculate the feed rate needed to hold the required steam/MW output.

Hands-on interventions in the feed system: break a bridge or rathole in a day bin or silo, rod out a plugged chute or screw feeder, shovel spillage back onto the belt, pull tramp metal/oversize out of a jam, and hand-charge small quantities (bales, startup fuel, additive bags).

tasks.label: Perform routine maintenance or make minor repairs to mechanical, electrical, or electronic equipment in biomass plants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled lubrication round through the plant: pumping grease into fittings on conveyor drive and idler bearings, ID/FD fan bearings, feedwater and ash pumps; topping up gearbox and bearing housing oil to sight-glass level. Fittings are in place on installed machinery, often overhead, on catwalks, or in dusty fuel-handling galleries.

Fluid and filter service on running plant equipment: draining and refilling lube-oil reservoirs and hydraulic power units, changing spin-on and cartridge oil/hydraulic/air filters on compressors, hydraulic packs and gearboxes, cleaning Y-strainers and duplex filters, wiping up spills and checking for leaks after restart.

Minor mechanical repairs in the fuel- and ash-handling system: replacing worn conveyor idlers and return rollers, adjusting belt tracking and scrapers, replacing drag-chain flights, screen panels and hogger/grinder wear parts, clearing plugged chutes and ash conveyors. Cramped, dusty, wet-ash conditions, lockout/tagout, work at height.

Minor repairs to rotating equipment and drives: replacing pump mechanical seals or repacking a gland, replacing V-belts, sheaves and flexible couplings, swapping bearings on small fans/pumps, re-torquing flanges and replacing gaskets, checking shaft alignment after the repair.

Minor electrical repairs: replacing failed motor contactors, overload relays, fuses and control-circuit components in the MCC, re-terminating loose or burnt wiring in junction boxes, replacing area lighting and receptacles, meggering a motor and reconnecting leads after a change-out.

Instrumentation and electronics work: calibrating or replacing pressure, level, flow and draft transmitters, replacing thermocouples/RTDs, cleaning flame scanners and level probes, servicing control-valve positioners and limit switches, then loop-checking against the DCS.

tasks.label: Calibrate liquid flow devices or meters, including fuel, chemical, and water meters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-situ calibration check of a process flow transmitter in the running biomass plant (DP transmitter across an orifice on boiler feedwater, or a magnetic flowmeter on cooling/service water): technician isolates the instrument with block-and-bleed valves, connects a portable documenting calibrator and HART communicator at the test ports, runs a 5-point as-found up/down check, trims zero and span, returns the loop to service and records as-found/as-left data in the CMMS. Work is done on pipe racks, in tight or elevated locations, with plant online.

Bench/shop calibration: a flowmeter or flow transmitter is removed from service and brought to the plant instrument shop, connected to reference standards (master meter, pressure controller, decade box), calibrated over its range, adjusted, stickered and certificated, and staged for reinstallation.

Chemical feed metering pump calibration in the chemical dosing area (ammonia/urea for SCR, boiler-water treatment, biocide): technician valves the pump suction to a graduated calibration column, times a drawdown, computes mL/min, adjusts stroke length/speed or controller setpoint, repeats to confirm, logs result. Involves hazardous chemicals, PPE, and cramped skid piping.

Fuel oil / liquid fuel flow meter verification at the tank farm or truck-unloading station: compare meter totalizer against a master meter, prover, or calibrated tank gauge over a transfer, compute the meter factor and update the K-factor in the flow computer/DCS, and file the record for fuel accounting. Often outdoors, in weather.

Water meter/totalizer verification for permit, water-balance or make-up accounting (raw water intake, demin makeup, cooling tower blowdown/discharge): field check against a portable clamp-on ultrasonic reference or removal of the meter for bench testing, adjust or replace, and document for regulatory reporting.

tasks.label: Assess quality of biomass feedstock.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Incoming truck delivery of wood chips/hog fuel at the plant scale house: before unloading, take a probe or grab sample of the load, determine moisture and estimated energy content for payment and blending, and log the result per load.

Screening a delivered load on the tipping floor/fuel yard for unacceptable material — rocks, soil, tramp metal, plastics, painted/treated wood, oversize pieces, ice — and deciding to accept, downgrade, divert or reject it.

Determining moisture content of received fuel: forming a composite sample per standard, running an oven-dry test or rapid meter in the plant sampling station/fuel lab, and reporting the value to the control room and fuel purchasing.

Routine quality checks of fuel on the handling line: pulling samples from conveyors/chutes feeding the day silo or boiler, checking particle size, fines, foreign matter and wetness, and passing findings to the control room to adjust the fuel blend.

Periodic full analysis of composite samples in the plant lab (or prep-and-ship to an outside lab): ash content, calorific value, particle-size distribution, occasionally chlorine/alkali, reported for contract compliance and boiler tuning.

Assessing feedstock held in storage: walking the outdoor chip pile or checking the bunker/silo for mold and spoilage, self-heating, frozen or waterlogged material and contamination, and taking probe samples from the pile.

Pile management: dozer (or loader) work in the outdoor storage yard building, pushing up, shaping and compacting fuel piles, blending fuel types/moisture, pushing reserve fuel toward the reclaim area, and keeping the yard pad clear so piles shed water and do not self-heat.

Residue removal: loader with bucket removing bottom ash/grate siftings or boiler residue from the ash pad or bunker and loading it into dump trucks or roll-off containers; also scooping spilled fuel and ash from under conveyors and transfer points.

tasks.label: Preprocess feedstock to prepare for biochemical or thermochemical production processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-size biomass power/CHP or pellet plant: technician runs the feedstock preparation train from the control room and local panels — sequencing walking-floor/push-floor bunkers, disc screens, hogs/hammer mills, dryers and conveyors; adjusting feed rate, screen splits and dryer setpoints to hold chip size and moisture on spec for the boiler/gasifier.

Fuel yard/bunker: reclaiming feedstock from the receiving floor or storage pile, stacking, blending wet and dry fuel types (bark, chips, hog fuel, waste wood), and keeping the process hopper continuously fed, using a grab crane or wheel loader inside the plant's fuel building/yard.

Contaminant removal from the feedstock stream: picking tramp metal, wire, rock, dirt clods, plastics and oversize pieces off the picking belt or reject conveyor ahead of the mill/reactor, and clearing rejects from magnets and screens, on a plant conveyor line.

Restoring flow when preprocessing equipment plugs: bridged material in a bunker or surge bin, wrapped rags/wire in an auger, a jammed chipper/hammer mill or plugged transfer chute — lockout/tagout, opening access doors, breaking the plug out by hand with bars/hooks/saws in dusty confined space, then restart and cleanup of spillage.

Feedstock quality verification and blend adjustment: pulling representative samples from incoming trucks, piles or the belt, running moisture (oven or handheld) and checking size/ash/contaminant level, then changing blend ratios or dryer/screen settings so the prepared feedstock meets the process spec.

Biochemical-route feedstock prep (anaerobic digestion / cellulosic conversion plant): packaged and mixed organics or slurry feedstock run through a depackager/separator and dosed into the digester feed system; contaminated reject stream managed and organics adjusted to target solids content.

instances.label: Pull a specific spare part for a maintenance job: locate it among bins, shelves and drawers in the plant parts crib (bearings, seals, belts, filters, conveyor chain links, electrical spares), verify part number, record the withdrawal in the CMMS, and carry it to the technician at the boiler, fuel handling or turbine area.

Receive a palletized or bulk delivery at the plant dock (drums of lube oil, totes of boiler/water-treatment chemicals, pallets of filters or bagged consumables): unload from the trailer, check against the packing slip/PO, and move the pallets into warehouse rack or floor storage, updating stock records.

Receive small-parcel and mixed LTL deliveries: open cartons, verify contents against packing slip and PO, tag/label items, and shelve loose small parts and consumables in the correct bin locations in the crib, updating stock records and closing out the receipt.

Perform cycle counts or a periodic physical inventory of the parts store: count and scan items at each bin/rack location, reconcile against CMMS/inventory records, investigate discrepancies, and flag items below min levels for reorder.

Walk the operating plant to check point-of-use supply and consumable levels (lube oil tanks and drums, hydraulic reservoirs, chemical totes, urea/ammonia, welding gas, filter and PPE stocks at stations), note what is running low, and initiate replenishment/reorder requests.

tasks.label: Monitor hydroelectric power plant equipment operation and performance, adjusting to performance specifications, as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control-room/SCADA watch at an attended hydro plant or a fleet operations center: trending unit MW, frequency, voltage, bearing and winding temperatures, vibration and headwater/tailwater; adjusting load and gate setpoints, voltage regulator setpoints and unit start/stop to hold the plant to dispatch and equipment specifications.

Routine round through the powerhouse (generator floor, turbine pit, galleries, oil and cooling-water rooms): reading local gauges and level glasses, checking bearing oil levels and temperatures, listening/feeling for abnormal noise and vibration, spotting leaks and hot spots, logging readings and flagging anything out of spec.

Making the hands-on field adjustment that the round or an alarm calls for: throttling a cooling-water or governor oil valve, resetting air/oil pressure setpoints on a compressor or sump, switching to a standby pump or filter, adjusting brush rigging or a shaft-seal packing gland, and confirming the parameter returns to spec.

Responding to an off-normal alarm or upset (high bearing temperature, high vibration, low oil pressure, unit trip): investigating at the machine, diagnosing the cause, adjusting or derating the unit or removing it from service, then restoring it to specified operation.

Monitoring and adjusting the water-side structures at the dam/intake in outdoor conditions: reservoir and tailwater levels, intake and spillway gate positions and hoists, trash-rack differential; changing gate openings to hold specified pond level and flow.

tasks.label: Identify or address malfunctions of hydroelectric plant operational equipment, such as generators, transformers, or turbines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field investigation of an abnormal indication on a running unit (control-room alarm, rising guide-bearing temperature, vibration, unusual noise, oil seepage): technician walks to the unit in the powerhouse, takes local gauge readings, thermal and acoustic checks, sight-glass/oil levels, localizes and identifies the malfunction, logs and reports it for correction.

Post-trip electrical/control fault diagnosis and restoration: reading protection relay targets and drawings, testing exciter/AVR, governor control cards, transducers, wiring and terminal boxes with multimeter/megger inside the powerhouse and relay room, then resetting or swapping a device and returning the unit to service.

Corrective mechanical repair on turbine/generator auxiliaries: repacking a shaft seal, chasing a bearing-oil or hydraulic leak, rebuilding a cooling-water pump or valve, servicing governor hydraulics or wicket-gate linkage and bushings, using hand tools, rigging and the powerhouse crane, often in confined, wet, oily spaces.

Corrective electrical repair/replacement on generators and transformers: changing carbon brushes and cleaning slip rings/collector, replacing space heaters, contactors, relays, breakers, cooling fans/pumps and terminations, in the powerhouse or the outdoor transformer yard under clearance/lockout.

Scheduled-outage internal defect investigation on a generator or turbine: air-gap or borescope inspection with rotor in place, stator wedge tap test, insulation resistance/PD testing, runner and draft-tube crack inspection and NDT, to pin down the cause of an observed malfunction.

Turbine runner cavitation/erosion damage repair during a dewatered outage: mapping the damaged area inside the turbine, grinding out pitted metal, weld build-up between blades, blending back to profile and peening, in the confined space around the runner.

It transfers to a hydro powerhouse because the objects (motors, pumps, bearings, gauges, piping), the sensing modalities (thermal, acoustic, visual gauge reading, leak detection) and the structured plant environment are the same class as investigating an abnormal indication on a hydro generating unit.

tasks.label: Start, adjust, or stop generating units, operating valves, gates, or auxiliary equipment in hydroelectric power generating plants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine start or stop of a generating unit on dispatch or schedule at a modern plant with digital controls: technician initiates the start from the control-room HMI or a remote operations center, and the unit runs through its lineup (aux systems, brake release, wicket gate opening, field flashing, synchronizing, breaker close, loading) with the technician monitoring permissives and alarms.

Adjusting a running unit: changing MW/MVAR setpoints on dispatch or AGC signal, trimming wicket gate/blade position, regulating forebay or pond level, shifting a unit between generate, condense or standby modes over a shift.

Operating water-passage gates and main valves at the dam or in the gate gallery: raising/lowering intake or spillway gates for flow and flood passage, stroking penstock shutoff or spherical/butterfly valves, closing draft-tube gates, using hoist controls at the deck or the plant control panel.

Local field operation of auxiliary equipment during unit prep, switching, or rounds in the powerhouse galleries: hand-turning manual valves and lineups, starting/stopping sump, drainage, cooling-water and oil pumps and compressors locally, racking or resetting breakers and local control switches, verifying mechanical indications — common at older plants with local unit control switchboards.

Abnormal or emergency operation: emergency shutdown of a unit on alarm or trip, tripping and isolating on overspeed, bearing or vibration alarms, and restart after a grid disturbance under safe conditions.

Return to service after maintenance or an outage: confirming clearances and tags removed, restoring field lineups and blocks, staged startup with local mechanical checks at the machine, and troubleshooting a start that fails on a permissive.

tasks.label: Perform preventive or corrective containment or cleanup measures in hydroelectric plants to prevent environmental contamination.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine preventive containment around leaking equipment inside the powerhouse: checking and emptying drip pans and oil-collection trays under turbine guide bearings, governor/hydraulic power units and gate cylinders; replacing saturated absorbent pads and socks; wiping oil film off machinery, grating and floor plates; bagging and labeling used absorbents as waste. Cluttered multi-level machine spaces with piping, cables, gratings and stairs.

Unit drainage sump and oily-water separator work: opening and inspecting station/unit dewatering sumps, skimming or vacuuming accumulated oil and sludge, cleaning coalescing media and strainers, checking float switches and high-oil alarms, sampling the discharge before it reaches the tailrace and logging the result.

Outdoor oil-handling areas: inspecting transformer containment vaults/berms and their normally-closed drain valves, draining accumulated rainwater after checking for sheen, clearing leaves and debris from containment, inspecting secondary containment of the used-oil drum and lube storage area, wiping up small seeps at valves and fittings.

Corrective response to an actual release: several gallons of turbine oil, hydraulic fluid, grease or coolant on the powerhouse floor, or a sheen appearing on the forebay/tailrace. Plug or dam floor drains, deploy spill-kit pads and containment boom, stop the source, recover product, drum and manifest the waste, decontaminate the area and complete incident reporting.

Scheduled housekeeping washdown/scrubbing of open machine-hall and gallery floors and access ways to keep oil, grease and dirt residues from accumulating and reaching floor drains and the river; large flat concrete/epoxy floor areas inside the powerhouse.

Removing and disposing of floating debris and trash accumulated at the intake trash racks, log boom and forebay so it is not passed downstream or left to foul the plant; raking debris off the screens and dropping it into a skip or trailer for disposal.

tasks.label: Inspect water-powered electric generators or auxiliary equipment in hydroelectric plants to verify proper operation or to determine maintenance or repair needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shift/periodic operating round through the powerhouse on running units: walk the unit floor and galleries, read local gauges (bearing oil level and temperature, cooling-water pressure/flow, governor oil pressure, generator air temperature), look and listen for abnormal noise, vibration, oil or water leaks, check indicator lamps, log readings and flag anomalies for follow-up. Plant is climate-controlled, fixed layout, access-controlled, often remotely operated with periodic technician visits.

Routine inspection of auxiliary systems and equipment rooms: station-service switchgear and MCCs, battery bank and chargers, air compressors and receivers, sump/unwatering and drainage pumps, cooling-water strainers, HVAC, and the adjacent transformer/switchyard walkdown; visual checks, gauge and level readings, infrared/thermal checks of panels and connections, leak checks.

Scheduled outage or overhaul inspection of an opened/disassembled unit: turbine runner and wicket gates checked for cavitation pitting, cracks and wear; draft tube and headcover; bearing babbitt and clearances; generator stator windings, wedges and rotor poles; brakes and couplings. Involves scaffolding, confined space, hands-on measurement, borescope and NDT, and a written determination of repair scope.

Alarm- or symptom-driven troubleshooting inspection: unit trip, high bearing or winding temperature, abnormal vibration or noise, low oil pressure, seal water or hydraulic leak. Technician goes to the machine, opens cabinets and covers, takes portable instrument readings (vibration analyzer, multimeter, thermometer), traces the cause and determines the repair needed.

Dewatered water-passage and gate inspection during an outage: interior of penstock/pressure steel pipe, scroll case, draft tube and concrete flow passages, intake and draft-tube gates, seals and hoists; confined-space entry, poor lighting, wet and slippery surfaces, checking for corrosion, cracks, erosion and lining damage and sizing the defects found.

Submerged inspection of the intake and tailrace side: trash racks and rakes, submerged gate seals and guides, penstock entrance, debris and sediment accumulation, in a reservoir or tailwater with current, limited visibility, and site-specific geometry; performed from a boat/deck with divers or a tethered camera system.

tasks.label: Operate high voltage switches or related devices in hydropower stations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine unit switching from the powerhouse control room (or a remote dispatch desk): bringing a hydro unit up on a schedule/dispatch order and closing the generator (and line) breaker after matching speed, voltage and phase, then opening it on shutdown. Indoor control room, standard plant SCADA/HMI and unit control panels, several times a day.

Operating the powerhouse medium- and low-voltage switchgear: opening/closing station-service main, tie and feeder breakers, transferring station service between sources, resetting after a trip. Indoor, clean, standard drawout switchgear lineups with local and remote control panels.

Switchyard configuration switching on motorized/electrically operated apparatus: opening or closing HV circuit breakers, circuit switchers and motor-operated disconnects to isolate a bus, transformer or line, with position confirmation. Fenced plant switchyard, executed from SCADA or the yard control cabinet.

Field operation of hand-operated apparatus in the switchyard: cranking a gang-operated air-break disconnect open/closed at its manual operator, hookstick work, and walking the yard to visually verify blade position, in rain, wind, heat or snow on equipment of varying age.

Isolation and clearance for maintenance: executing a switching order to de-energize equipment - trip and rack out a drawout breaker, open disconnects, close integral ground switches or apply portable safety grounds, test dead, install locks and clearance tags - partly indoors, partly in the yard.

Abnormal or emergency switching: after a unit trip, bus fault or line relay operation, isolating the faulted device, inspecting apparatus for damage, and reconfiguring or restoring the plant/line under time pressure while coordinating with the transmission dispatcher.

tasks.label: Operate hydroelectric plant equipment, such as turbines, pumps, valves, gates, fans, electric control boards, or battery banks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control-room/board operation of generating units at a conventional powerhouse: start, synchronize, load, unload and stop units; adjust wicket-gate/blade position, MW and MVAR setpoints in response to dispatch or market schedules; switch control modes and acknowledge alarms on the unit control board and HMI.

Operating water-passage equipment at the dam: raising and lowering intake gates, headgates, sluice and spillway gates and bypass/synchronous-bypass valves to hold forebay level, pass required flows and ramp releases, including during high-water events and in weather.

Operating motor-driven auxiliaries and unit support systems as part of unit line-ups: cooling-water and lube/governor oil pumps, drainage and unwatering sump pumps, air compressors, ventilation fans, brakes and greasing systems, started/stopped from the control system, MCC or local start stations.

Hands-on local operation of non-actuated equipment during rounds and line-ups: hand-wheel and lever valves on cooling water, air, oil and drainage headers, local hand switches and local unit control panels operated while standing at the machine in the powerhouse galleries.

Electrical operation: opening and closing generator, station-service and feeder breakers and disconnects, synchronizing to the bus, transferring station service, operating the exciter/AVR, and operating the station DC system and battery bank/charger (float/equalize, transfers).

Abnormal, emergency and outage-related operation: local emergency shutdown at the machine, hand or backup-power operation of gates on loss of power, restoring units after trips and alarms, black-start/islanded operation, and operating the plant with automation, sections of the bus or equipment out of service or tagged.

tasks.label: Maintain or repair hydroelectric plant electrical, mechanical, or electronic equipment, such as motors, transformers, voltage regulators, generators, relays, battery systems, air compressors, sump pumps, gates, or valves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Powerhouse mechanical auxiliaries: overhaul/repair of sump pumps, cooling-water pumps, air compressors and fans. Technician isolates the unit, disassembles it with hand and power tools (often corroded fasteners), replaces mechanical seals, bearings, impellers, couplings, belts and filters, aligns and reassembles to torque spec, then test-runs. Work in wet, cramped pits or the plant shop.

Rotating electrical machinery and transformers: generator/exciter/motor brush and slip-ring service, collector and stator cleaning, insulation-resistance and PI testing, re-torquing bus and terminal connections, voltage-regulator servicing, transformer oil sampling and gasket/bushing leak repair. Requires lockout/tagout, grounding, confined access inside machine housings.

Protection, control and electronic equipment: troubleshooting protective relays and annunciators, replacing failed relays, PLC/governor I-O cards and transducers, calibrating instruments, pulling and terminating small wiring in panels, verifying with test sets before return to service. Work at live-adjacent switchboards and relay panels.

Station battery bank and DC system: reading cell voltages and specific gravity, cleaning and greasing terminals, re-torquing inter-cell connectors, adding water, replacing failed cells, repairing/adjusting chargers, performing capacity/load tests in the battery room with PPE.

Gates, valves and actuators, routine mechanical service: greasing wicket-gate bushings, hoist gearboxes and stem threads, replacing valve packing and seals, adjusting linkages, shear pins and limit switches, servicing hydraulic power units and servomotors. Often outdoors on the dam deck or in gate slots, wet and awkward positions.

Scheduled-outage in-situ metal repair of large wetted steel components: weld build-up, gouging, grinding and machining of gate wheel tracks/guide slots, spherical (main inlet) valve sealing surfaces and cavitation or crack damage, restoring the surface to tight tolerance inside the powerhouse or a dewatered gate slot.

tasks.label: Implement load or switching orders in hydroelectric plants, in accordance with specifications or instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine load order from the dispatcher/balancing authority at an attended plant: raise or lower plant/unit MW to the hourly schedule or follow an AGC signal, allocate the load among available units, keep off rough zones and within head/tailwater limits, and confirm the plant is at the ordered output. Executed from the control-room console/control board on units equipped with governors and excitation control.

Order to place a unit on or off line: run up auxiliaries (oil, cooling water, brakes), open the intake/wicket gates, bring the unit to speed, apply excitation, synchronize and close the generator breaker, ramp to the ordered load; or the reverse for a shutdown order. Standard powerhouse equipment, normal conditions.

Switching order carried out on remotely operable station equipment: change bus configuration, isolate or return a generator step-up transformer, line or station-service supply, place equipment in hot or cold standby per the operating ticket, with each device position verified before the next step. Motor-operated breakers and disconnects controlled from the plant SCADA/control board.

Local/manual portion of a switching order or clearance in an older powerhouse and switchyard: walk down the equipment, rack breakers in or out, operate manual disconnect handles or hookstick switches, close local isolation valves/gate dogs, test for absence of voltage, install personal protective grounds, hang tags, and physically verify blade positions before reporting the order complete.

Non-routine order under abnormal conditions: unit trip or load rejection recovery, emergency generation change during a system disturbance, an order that conflicts with plant limits or an out-of-service unit, high-water/spill constraints — requiring verification of plant condition, ad hoc field checks, and coordination back with the dispatcher before and while implementing.

Install or set up equipment outdoors at the dam, intake, spillway or flood channel - gate actuators, flow/level instruments, trash-rack and screen gear - on found ground, in weather, mud and moving water.

tasks.label: Change oil, hydraulic fluid, or other lubricants to maintain condition of hydroelectric plant equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled grease round inside the powerhouse: technician walks the unit floor and galleries with a grease gun/pail pump, hitting fittings on wicket gate linkage pins, operating ring, servomotor pins, generator/exciter and motor bearings, fan and pump bearings, valve stems; wipes zerks, counts strokes, checks for purge, logs completion.

Unit-outage oil change on a turbine guide bearing or thrust bearing oil bath: unit locked out and drained, several hundred gallons of used oil pumped to drums or a waste tank, covers removed and pit entered, sump wiped of sludge and inspected, gaskets replaced, refill with new turbine oil through a filter cart, level set and an oil sample pulled.

Governor / hydraulic power unit fluid service: drain the HPU sump, replace pressure and return filter elements, flush lines, refill with clean hydraulic fluid through a filter cart, bleed air, reset accumulator charge, verify levels and check for leaks; includes hydraulic top-ups on gate servomotors.

Small auxiliary equipment oil change/top-up: gearboxes on powerhouse cranes and gate hoists, air compressors, sump and cooling-water pumps, station-service diesel engine - pull a drain plug or open a drain valve, drain into a pan, change the spin-on filter where fitted, refill a measured volume of new oil, check the sight glass, log it.

Outdoor and remote lubrication work at dam structures and small unattended plants: greasing intake gate hoists, trashrack rake, spillway gate trunnions, and changing gearbox oil on gate operators - done in weather, on catwalks and ladders, with site-to-site variation in access and equipment.

tasks.label: Lift and move loads, using cranes, hoists, and rigging, to install or repair hydroelectric system equipment or infrastructure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine maintenance lift inside the powerhouse: technician rigs a pump, motor, exciter part, valve or governor component (0.5–20 tons) with slings, shackles and eyebolts, signals/operates the overhead bridge crane, lifts it clear of the unit, travels it down the erection bay, and lands it on cribbing or a work stand; tag lines and a spotter are used, clearances are tight around handrails, piping and live equipment.

Major unit overhaul heavy lift: generator rotor, turbine runner, head cover or thrust bearing (50–500+ tons) rigged with a lifting frame/spreader beam and bolted lifting lugs, lifted with the main powerhouse crane (often twin hoists), rotated/staged on the erection floor, then lowered into the stator bore or turbine pit with millimetre air-gap clearance while several riggers guide, measure and adjust.

Small-scale rigging away from the main crane: chain falls, come-alongs, jib cranes, portable gantries and snatch blocks anchored to overhead beams or padeyes to pull, hold and position parts in confined or awkward spaces (draft tube, scroll case, wicket-gate linkage, valve gallery, cable vault, battery room), often on scaffolding or in wet, low-headroom conditions.

Outdoor deck work at the dam/intake: operating the gantry crane or gate hoist to set and pull stoplogs, bulkheads, trash racks or intake gates with a lifting beam, and to lift gate-hoist motors, sheaves and cables for repair; wind, rain, ice, submerged guide slots, silt and debris are part of the conditions.

Receiving and site transport: offloading a transformer, spare runner, switchgear cubicle or pallets of parts from a delivery truck in the plant yard with a mobile/boom-truck crane or forklift, rigging the load, moving it to the powerhouse roof hatch, and lowering it through the hatch to the crane bay for the plant crane to take.

Ground-level checks at remote field assets reached by truck, boat or on foot: remote intakes, small diversion dams, gauging stations and gate houses - reading staff gauges and local instruments, opening the structure, verifying screens and gate positions, checking for vandalism.

Inspection of submerged features - intake trashracks and screens, gate seals and slots, upstream dam face, draft tube and tailrace - in silty, low-visibility water, currently done by divers or piloted ROVs.

tasks.label: Splice or terminate cables or electrical wiring in hydroelectric plants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Terminating small-gauge control, protection and instrumentation wiring inside plant panels: relay/RTU cabinets, governor and excitation control panels, MCC control sections. Technician cuts wire to length, strips, crimps ferrules or ring lugs, lands conductors on DIN-rail terminal blocks, contactors and breakers, torques screws, labels wires and point-to-point checks against the schematic. Indoor powerhouse control room or electrical room, clean, lit, utility-controlled.

Terminating field-device wiring in situ: multi-conductor shielded cable pulled to a limit switch on a wicket gate, an RTD/level transmitter head, a gate-position sensor or a local junction box on the intake deck or spillway. Strip the cable jacket, land conductors and shield drains on terminal blocks inside the box, gland and seal it. Cramped, sometimes damp or outdoor but on utility-controlled dam premises.

Terminating low-voltage power cable at motors, MCC buckets, breakers and battery banks (roughly 6 AWG to 500 kcmil): jacket stripping, hydraulic lug crimping, bolting lugs to studs or terminal boards, torquing, insulating with tape or heat shrink, then meggering. Powerhouse gallery, pump room or switchgear room.

Terminating or splicing medium-voltage cable (4.16-13.8 kV generator leads, station service feeders): removing jacket, shield tape and semicon layers to tolerance, installing cold-shrink or heat-shrink stress-cone terminations or splice kits, grounding shields, hipot testing. Switchgear room or cable vault, high consequence of workmanship error.

Repair splicing of damaged or aged cable in place: a chafed submersible sump-pump cord, a crushed control cable in a cable tray or conduit run, a lighting/heater circuit in a wet draft-tube gallery or penstock tunnel. Access is awkward, cable positions are as found, splice must be sealed and moisture-proof.

Terminating and splicing communication media for SCADA and protection: fiber-optic fusion splices in a splice tray, connectorizing patch cords, coax and shielded twisted-pair terminations at communication racks and remote structures.

tasks.label: Test and repair or replace electrical equipment, such as circuit breakers, station batteries, cable trays, conduits, or control devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic testing and servicing of powerhouse switchgear circuit breakers (LV and MV): de-energize and lock out, rack the breaker out of its cubicle, clean/inspect/lubricate the mechanism, run insulation-resistance, contact-resistance and timing/trip tests with a breaker analyzer, re-rack and functionally verify. Done in the plant's switchgear room to a maintenance schedule.

Station battery bank work in the plant battery room: measure cell voltages, specific gravity and inter-cell connection resistance, torque/clean terminals, run an annual capacity (load-bank) discharge test, and replace weak cells or an entire lead-acid/NiCd string, including handling heavy cells and re-making bolted bus connections.

Test, repair or replace control devices in control panels and cabinets: protective relays, auxiliary relays, timers, contactors, control switches, transducers and terminal blocks. Bench or in-panel testing with a relay test set/meter, removing the failed device from its DIN rail or panel cutout, mounting the replacement, re-terminating and landing wires per drawings, and functionally proving the circuit.

Raceway work in the powerhouse and galleries: install, extend or repair cable trays and conduit runs, drill and set overhead/wall anchors, bend and fit conduit around existing structure, pull and dress cables into the tray, terminate at both ends. Cramped, wet, sometimes confined or elevated locations that vary from run to run.

Corrective troubleshooting after an alarm or trip: e.g., DC ground fault on the station battery system, a breaker that fails to close, an intermittent control circuit or burned contactor. Interpret alarms and elementary drawings, probe circuits live or de-energized, isolate the failed component, repair or swap it and restore the unit to service under time pressure.

tasks.label: Take readings and record data, such as water levels, temperatures, or flow rates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine operating round inside the powerhouse of a hydro station: walk a fixed route past units, governors, exciters, transformers and auxiliary systems; read local analog and digital gauges (bearing and winding temperatures, oil levels and pressures, cooling-water flow and pressure, air-system pressures), note annunciators, and log values in the shift log/CMMS. Standard indoor layout, utility controls access.

Control-room / instrument-panel readings and recording: at set intervals read headwater and tailwater elevations, unit MW and discharge, temperatures and vibration values off SCADA HMI screens, meters and chart recorders, and enter them into shift logs, spreadsheets and regulatory compliance reports.

Outdoor readings on dam/plant premises: read headwater and tailwater staff gauges, forebay level and trash-rack differential, spillway and intake gate position indicators, penstock pressure gauges and precipitation/weather instruments; performed in rain, snow, ice and darkness on utility-owned, fenced dam grounds.

Readings that require contact or manipulation: pulling a dipstick or wiping a sight glass, opening a cabinet or hatch to read an internal meter, pressing an accelerometer/IR probe against a specific bearing housing point for a route vibration or temperature reading, or tape-down measurement in a piezometer well, then logging the value.

Readings inside dam interior galleries, draft-tube decks and other confined, wet, poorly lit spaces: seepage weir and drain flow readings, piezometer and uplift-pressure gauges, sump levels, scroll-case and draft-tube gauges, reached via long galleries, stairs and hatches.

Field readings away from the plant premises: staff gauges and flow measurements at a remote diversion dam, canal or flume, streamflow/stage checks at a river gaging point, water temperature or fish-passage readings, reached by truck or on foot over unimproved terrain in all weather.
