tasks.label: Erect scaffolds, platforms, or hoisting frames to access hydroelectric plant machinery or infrastructure for repair or replacement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Unit overhaul in the powerhouse machine hall: technicians erect a multi-lift tube-and-clamp or system scaffold around a generator/turbine pit — landing steel standards, ledgers, braces and planks (15–25 kg each) delivered by the bridge crane, leveling base plates on the deck, tying into structural steel, fitting guardrails and toeboards, and having the finished scaffold inspected/tagged before crews use it.

Small-scale access on the plant floor or galleries: assembling or rolling a tower/baker's scaffold or portable work platform into position to reach a governor cabinet, exciter, cable tray, lighting, crane rail or overhead valve — setting outriggers, leveling on a sloped or cluttered floor, locking casters, installing platform deck and rails.

Staging inside dewatered water passages: building scaffold or work platforms in a draft tube, spiral/scroll case, penstock or intake — confined-space entry through a manhole, wet and silty curved steel/concrete surfaces, sloped invert requiring custom-cut base cribbing, limited lighting and ventilation, all components hand-passed through a small opening.

Outdoor work on dam and waterway structures: erecting scaffold, needle beams or suspended/swing stages on the dam face, spillway or intake gates, trashracks, penstock exterior or tailrace deck — uneven ground or gate slots, weather and spray, rigging anchor points on existing embeds, exposure to falling into water.

Rigging temporary lifting structures in the powerhouse: assembling a portable gantry, A-frame, monorail beam, trolley or temporary jib over a wicket-gate servomotor, valve, exciter or pump — bolting to floor inserts or beams, verifying load ratings and anchor capacity, hanging chain falls, before the component is pulled for repair or replacement.

roles.description: Operate or maintain stationary engines, boilers, or other mechanical equipment to provide utilities for buildings or industrial processes. Operate equipment such as steam engines, generators, motors, turbines, and steam boilers.

tasks.label: Operate or tend stationary engines, boilers, and auxiliary equipment, such as pumps, compressors, or air-conditioning equipment, to supply and maintain steam or heat for buildings, marine vessels, or pneumatic tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional heating plant (hospital, school, campus, office tower): keeping hot-water or low-pressure steam boilers, circulating and condensate pumps and air-handling equipment supplying heat over a shift — watching pressure, temperature and water level, adjusting firing rate and setpoints to match building load, in a locked mechanical room.

Industrial process steam plant (food plant, laundry, paper/refinery utility area): tending packaged firetube or watertube boilers with deaerator, feedwater pumps, chemical feed and blowdown, holding steam-header pressure against a swinging process load, from a plant control panel plus field rounds.

Cooling and compressed-air side of the same utility duties: starting, stopping and sequencing centrifugal/screw chillers, cooling towers, condenser and chilled-water pumps, and air compressors/dryers to hold chilled-water temperature and plant air pressure for pneumatic tools.

Marine vessel: tending auxiliary boiler, steam plant, air compressors, purifiers and pumps in a ship's engine room at sea — watchkeeping, load changes and standby-machinery changeover under vibration, heat and vessel motion.

Discrete operating events handled through the plant control system: seasonal or daily boiler start-up and shutdown, lead/lag rotation between boilers, bringing a standby pump or additional chiller online, re-matching output after a step change in demand.

Hands-on field work in older or partly manual plants and during upsets: manual valve line-ups, opening bottom-blowdown valves, priming and venting pumps, cracking steam valves during warm-up, local resets after a flame-failure or low-water trip, in cluttered mechanical rooms full of handwheels and local panels.

tasks.label: Activate valves to maintain required amounts of water in boilers, to adjust supplies of combustion air, and to control the flow of fuel into burners.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steady-state shift operation of automatically controlled packaged firetube/watertube boilers in a commercial or institutional plant (hospital, university, hotel, office). The engineer watches gauge glass/drum level, steam pressure and stack O2, and adjusts feedwater, combustion-air and fuel-valve settings to hold level and firing rate as building load swings. Valves are factory-mounted modulating control valves and dampers in a boiler room.

Large industrial or utility steam plant run from a DCS/control room: the operator trims the drum-level (feedwater valve), air-flow/damper and fuel-flow loops to follow load, places loops in manual and strokes control valves as needed, coordinated with a field operator on the boiler deck.

Bringing a boiler on or off line: lining up feedwater, vent and drain valves, filling to normal water level, purge and burner light-off, then progressively opening the fuel valve and combustion-air damper while holding water level, and cutting the boiler in on the steam header (or the reverse for shutdown).

Scheduled manual field valve work at the boiler front to hold correct water inventory and water quality: bottom blowdown (quick-opening then slow-opening valve in sequence), surface/TDS blowdown, and restoring level with the feedwater valve, all while watching the gauge glass.

Older or semi-manual small plants (aging school/municipal/small industrial boilers, jackshaft-linkage burners, manual feedwater bypass valves on field-erected units): the engineer physically turns handwheels and adjusts damper/linkage settings through the shift to hold water level and fuel-air balance in an as-found boiler room.

Abnormal or upset conditions: swinging or hunting drum level, carryover, low-water alarm, flame instability, a sticking or failed control valve, fuel changeover trouble. The engineer takes the loops to manual, diagnoses the cause, and works the feedwater, air and fuel valves by hand and judgment to stabilize or safely secure the boiler.

tasks.label: Monitor boiler water, chemical, and fuel levels, and make adjustments to maintain required levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large industrial/utility steam plant: operator watches drum level, feedwater flow, fuel flow and chemical feed on the DCS/HMI from a control room, trims setpoints and makes occasional local field adjustments (feed pump, chemical pump, fuel valve) during load swings and startup.

Institutional plant (hospital, university, large commercial building): walking rounds through the boiler room each shift — read sight glass and gauges, check deaerator/condensate receiver and chemical tank levels, verify chemical pump operation, log readings, adjust chemical feed pump stroke or feedwater valve.

Boiler water chemistry check: draw a cooled sample at the sample valve, run test-kit titrations (sulfite, phosphate, alkalinity, hardness, conductivity), and adjust chemical feed rate/blowdown to bring the water back into spec.

Chemical replenishment: physically move, mix and refill treatment chemical from drums/pails/totes into the day tank or feed tank in a cramped mechanical room, prime the metering pump, and verify draw-down.

Fuel level management: check fuel oil day tank and bulk/outdoor storage tank levels (gauge, ATG or dipstick), start/verify transfer to keep the day tank full, switch fuel supply, or check coal/wood-chip bin level and adjust the feed rate; order fuel as needed.

Abnormal conditions: low-water alarm, fouled or misreading gauge glass, sticking feedwater regulator or failed level control — blow down the water column/gauge glass, manually feed water, isolate/bypass and restore correct level before the boiler trips or is damaged.

tasks.label: Analyze problems and take appropriate action to ensure continuous and reliable operation of equipment and systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional building plant (hospital, university, office tower): a BAS alarm or occupant complaint (a wing losing heat, chilled-water supply temperature drifting). The operator trends points at the workstation, then walks the mechanical room, checks pumps, control valves, actuators, VFDs and filters, finds the fault (e.g., a seized valve actuator, a tripped drive, an airbound coil), corrects or replaces it, restores service and verifies recovery.

Boiler trip or burner fault in an institutional/industrial boiler room: low-water cutoff trip, flame failure, or pressure/fuel-train lockout. The operator blows down the water column, tests the LWCO, inspects and cleans the flame scanner/ignition electrode, checks the gas train and combustion air, resets the burner management system, relights, tunes and monitors while a standby boiler carries load.

Rotating equipment problem in the plant: a feedwater or condenser-water pump, fan, or air compressor showing noise, vibration, overheated bearing or a leaking mechanical seal. The operator diagnoses on the spot, valves over to the standby unit, locks out the failed unit, repacks/greases or tags it for repair, and restores the loop without interrupting service.

Chiller/cooling-tower fault: chiller trips on high condenser pressure or low evaporator flow. The operator checks strainers and condenser-water flow, cleans a plugged basket strainer or tower basin screen, checks refrigerant/oil and purge, checks water chemistry, resets the chiller controller, restarts and verifies stable operation during a hot afternoon.

Distribution-side troubleshooting across an occupied campus or building: failed steam traps, a leaking flanged joint or valve packing in a utility tunnel, an air handler with a broken damper linkage or belt, unbalanced zones. The operator walks the route, isolates the section, repairs or replaces the component, and returns the system to service while occupants are present.

Large coal/biomass/waste-fired industrial or utility boiler: heat-transfer surfaces slag and foul, flue-gas temperatures climb and output derates. The operator determines which superheater/reheater/economizer surfaces need cleaning and when, sequences the installed sootblowers accordingly (avoiding over- or under-cleaning), and verifies that cleanliness and heat rate recover.

tasks.label: Observe and interpret readings on gauges, meters, and charts registering various aspects of boiler operation to ensure that boilers are operating properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine round of a building/institutional central boiler plant (hospital, university, hotel, office): operator walks the boiler room and mechanical levels, reads local steam-pressure and temperature gauges, water-level sight glasses, feedwater and stack-temperature indicators, records values on a log sheet and flags anything out of range. Fixed layout, tight aisles, stairs/ladders, hot surfaces.

Control-room/panel monitoring at a central plant: operator reads panel-mounted gauges, meters, annunciators and digital displays for boiler pressure, drum level, feedwater flow, O2/flue-gas readings; logs values each hour and notes deviations from setpoints.

Field round in a large industrial or utility steam plant: local gauges, level meters, fuel and steam-flow meters read on grated catwalks around large boilers; hot, noisy, multi-level, PPE required; readings logged and out-of-limit values reported.
Interpreting circular chart recorders and strip-chart traces (pen recordings of pressure, temperature, flow) plus shift trend logs, to spot slow drift, cycling, or fouling over hours or days.

Abnormal or upset condition: readings conflict or alarm (falling drum level, pressure swing, rising stack temperature, erratic gauge). Operator cross-checks redundant gauges, blows down/verifies the gauge glass, judges whether the instrument or the process is at fault, and decides urgency within minutes.

tasks.label: Test boiler water quality or arrange for testing and take necessary corrective action, such as adding chemicals to prevent corrosion and harmful deposits.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shift/daily water testing at a commercial or institutional steam plant (hospital, campus, office tower, district heating): draw cooled grab samples from the boiler, feedwater and condensate sample coolers; run pH, conductivity/TDS, P & M alkalinity, sulfite and hardness with a test kit or bench titrator; log results and compare against ASME/vendor limits.

Water testing at an industrial or utility plant with higher-pressure boilers (power plant, refinery, food/paper mill): phosphate, silica, dissolved oxygen, cation conductivity, iron; verify installed on-line analyzer readings against grab samples and record chemistry trends for the shift log.

Corrective action when a result is out of spec: change the chemical feed pump setpoint or stroke, slug-dose oxygen scavenger/phosphate/amine into the feedwater or drum, increase surface blowdown or perform a bottom blowdown, then re-test to confirm the boiler is back inside limits.

Keeping treatment chemicals supplied: receive 5-gallon pails, 55-gallon drums or totes of scavenger/polymer/amine, move them into the boiler room, transfer product into day tanks or set a suction lance in a fresh drum, dilute/mix a batch tank.

Fixing the feed and sampling hardware as part of taking corrective action: replace cracked peristaltic tubing or a diaphragm, clear a plugged injection quill or blocked sample cooler/strainer, calibrate the metering pump against a draw-down column, stop a chemical leak.

Arranging outside testing: draw grab samples into bottles at the sample coolers, label them, hand them to the water-treatment service rep or ship to the contract lab, then read the returned report and implement the recommended dosage or blowdown changes.

tasks.label: Monitor and inspect equipment, computer terminals, switches, valves, gauges, alarms, safety devices, and meters to detect leaks or malfunctions and to ensure that equipment is operating efficiently and safely.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled operating rounds through a large central/industrial plant (power station, refinery/chemical plant, large district-energy or campus central plant): walking a fixed multi-level route past boilers, turbines, compressors and pumps; reading local gauges, meters and panels; thermal/feel checks on bearings, motors and steam lines; listening for steam, air or gas leaks; checking seals and oil levels; logging readings and flagging anomalies. Heat, noise, catwalks, stairs.

Close-up boiler/steam-side checks in the boiler room: water level in the gauge glass, burner flame and fuel pressure, stack and feedwater temperatures, condition of feedwater pumps, steam traps and safety-valve piping, looking and listening for steam/water/fuel leaks and abnormal combustion, then recording readings on the log sheet.

Control-room/BAS console watch: sitting at computer terminals and DDC/SCADA screens and annunciator panels for a shift, watching trends and alarm banners, cross-checking suspicious values, and deciding which indications signal a real malfunction requiring field verification.

Rounds through mechanical and electrical rooms of a commercial high-rise, hospital, data center or campus reachable on foot (corridors, doors, stairs): chillers, boilers, air handlers, pumps, switchgear; checking for water/refrigerant leaks, unusual vibration or noise, hot components, trip and alarm lights, and reading local gauges.

Checks in hard-access spaces: pipe tunnels and crawl spaces, penthouse and cramped equipment closets crowded with piping, and equipment reached by vertical ladders or roof hatches; confined-space or fall-protection precautions, poor lighting, clutter that varies building to building.

Outdoor equipment checks on plant premises in weather: cooling towers and condenser fans, fuel-oil and chemical tanks, yard pumps and rooftop units; rain, snow, heat, darkness on night rounds; checking levels, leaks, vibration and icing.

tasks.label: Switch from automatic to manual controls and isolate equipment mechanically and electrically to allow for safe inspection and repair work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Building/campus mechanical room: take a pump, fan or motor-driven auxiliary out of service for maintenance — move the starter or BAS point from AUTO to HAND/OFF at the local panel, close the suction and discharge handwheel/lever valves, open the local disconnect or breaker, apply a personal padlock and tag to each energy-isolating device, then verify zero energy by attempted restart and by draining/venting the casing.

Boiler room: remove a fire-tube or water-tube boiler from service for internal inspection or tube/refractory repair — shift burner management from automatic to manual, ramp down and shut off, close and lock main and pilot fuel gas cocks, close the main steam stop, open drains and vents, open the burner control panel breaker, tag multiple isolation points, and confirm the unit is cool, depressurized and at zero energy before the inspector or repair crew enters.

Central plant: isolate a chiller, air compressor, cooling tower or large air-handling unit — local HOA switch to OFF, close chilled/condenser water or refrigerant service valves, pump down or drain as required, open the unit disconnect at the MCC, lock and tag, and prove de-energization before belts, filters, tubes or seals are worked on.

Power plant / district energy plant: isolate a turbine-generator or a section of high-pressure steam header — place the governor/control loop in manual, trip the unit, rack out or open the generator/feeder breaker in the switchgear room, close and chain-lock steam and drain valves, install blind flanges or blanks at flanged connections, drain and vent, and hang a group lockout with multiple workers' locks and permit tags.

Abnormal or urgent conditions: a leak, tube failure, bearing failure, alarm or smoke condition requires deciding on the spot which equipment and energy sources must be isolated, then bypassing automatic controls, closing valves under heat/steam/noise (steam tunnels, rooftops, cramped equipment spaces), and locking and tagging the affected apparatus so repairs can begin immediately.

sources.system: Tactile active-inference peg-in-hole insertion policy on UR5 e-series

sources.claim: A UR5 arm with vision-based tactile sensors autonomously inserts pegs into holes with sub-0.1 mm clearance at a 90% success rate in real-world experiments, generalizing across five objects without pre-training on real data.

tasks.label: Perform or arrange for repairs, such as complete overhauls, replacement of defective valves, gaskets, or bearings, or fabrication of new parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Replace a defective valve in a building/industrial plant room: isolate and drain a steam, condensate, or chilled-water line, cut out or unbolt a leaking gate/globe/control valve (often hot, insulated, overhead, in cramped piping), install the replacement with new gaskets/packing, restore service and leak-check.

Replace gaskets, packing, or seals: heat-exchanger head or boiler manway/handhole gaskets during an annual inspection, or repack a pump gland / change a mechanical seal on a circulating pump — break out corroded bolting, scrape and clean sealing faces, fit and center the new gasket, torque in sequence, pressure-test.

Replace bearings and couplings on rotating equipment (fan, pump, motor, air compressor): uncouple and disassemble, pull a seized bearing, clean and inspect the shaft journal, press or heat-fit the new bearing, reassemble, laser-align the coupling, lubricate, run and check vibration/temperature.

Perform or assist a complete overhaul: reciprocating air-compressor top end, chiller or refrigeration compressor, burner/refractory work on a boiler, or turbine element — multi-day teardown in the plant, measuring clearances and wear, replacing wear parts, reassembling to spec, then commissioning and tuning.

Fabricate a replacement part in the plant shop: turn a shaft sleeve or bushing on a lathe, mill a bracket, cut a gasket from sheet stock, or cut/thread/weld a pipe spool or equipment support to a measured sketch, to fit the existing machine.

Arrange for repairs: diagnose the failure, write the scope, obtain parts/quotes, schedule the outage, isolate and lock out the equipment for the contractor, escort and monitor the work, then verify, restart and commission the repaired equipment.

It transfers to the 'fabrication of new parts' instance because the objects (steel plate/pipe/brackets), joining process (arc welding to a drawing) and required precision are the same work a stationary engineer does in the plant shop; the difference is only that the cell is purpose-built and the part is fixtured.

It transfers to 'fabrication of new parts' because a replacement sleeve, bushing or bracket is exactly a one-off machined metal part at similar or looser tolerance; the cell supplies fixturing and presentation, matching the E1 counterfactual.

sources.developer: Multiple (academic and industry survey; Robotics & Automation News)

sources.claim: Trade and academic sources report that robotic disassembly of used equipment — the core of overhauls and of valve/bearing/gasket replacement — remains largely unautomated because of corrosion, wear and part-to-part variation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown/rebuild of used machinery (remanufacturing). Directly informative for overhauls and for valve/bearing/gasket replacement, which are teardown-and-rebuild jobs on worn, corroded, in-service assemblies.

sources.system: Object-centric autonomous robotic disassembly research system
sources.developer: University research (published in Journal of Manufacturing Systems / ScienceDirect)
sources.title: Disassembly from scratch: An object-centric approach for robotic autonomous disassembly with zero contact/interference information — ScienceDirect

Upset, alarm and failure response: a control valve sticks or fails, a pump trips, a leak appears; the operator diagnoses, manually throttles or isolates with hand valves, swaps to standby equipment and restores service under time pressure.

Periodic (outage or seasonal) cleaning of heat-transfer surfaces: removing soot, ash and scale from firetubes or watertube/waterwall surfaces, brushing and vacuuming tubes, cleaning the breeching, smokebox and air heater, and cleaning condenser/heat-exchanger tubes so rated heat transfer is restored.

Minor adjustments discovered on rounds, made with hand tools: snugging or repacking a leaking pump packing gland, adjusting belt tension on a fan drive, tightening a weeping flange or fitting, adjusting a burner linkage or air damper stop, changing a gauge-glass gasket, resetting a limit switch - each requiring the operator to diagnose what is off and choose the adjustment.

Small commercial/institutional boiler room (school or apartment basement, small hotel, retail plant): cramped ad-hoc space with low headroom and packed piping; a combined visit in which the operator oils circulator pumps and burner motor, vacuums and wipes the burner and boiler front, cleans the low-water cutoff float chamber, and makes small hand-tool adjustments.

tasks.label: Test electrical systems to determine voltages, using voltage meters.

instances.label: Live supply-voltage check at a 480 V motor control center or distribution panel in a boiler/mechanical room: don arc-flash PPE, open the enclosure, apply DMM leads to phase lugs, breaker terminals and neutral/ground, read and log L-L and L-N values. Cramped, energized, other equipment running.

Troubleshooting a control circuit on a burner management panel, pump starter or VFD control section: probing 24 V/120 V control terminals, fuses, relay coils, interlock and limit-switch contacts point by point against a schematic to find the open or failed device while the plant is running.

Absence-of-voltage verification during lockout/tagout: prove the meter on a known live source, test each phase-to-phase and phase-to-ground on the isolated feeder of a motor, heater or pump, re-prove the meter, then release the equipment for maintenance.

DC/battery system checks during rounds in a generator or electrical room: measuring string and individual jar/cell voltages on emergency generator starting batteries and UPS banks, plus charger float/output voltage, and logging results.

Voltage check on outdoor/rooftop plant equipment: rooftop unit or condenser disconnect, cooling tower fan motor, outdoor pump-house panel — reached by ladder or roof hatch, in weather, with awkward access.
Bench testing of a removed component in the maintenance shop: motor leads, transformer secondary, control board or transducer placed on the bench and checked with a meter and test supply.

tasks.label: Check the air quality of ventilation systems and make adjustments to ensure compliance with mandated safety codes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine monitoring of ventilation air quality in a large commercial or institutional building (office tower, campus, hospital): tracking CO2, temperature/humidity, outdoor-air fraction and damper/economizer position across air handlers, and adjusting outdoor-air damper positions, fan speeds and minimum-OA setpoints so ventilation rates stay at the code minimum (ASHRAE 62.1 / IMC / Title 24).

Boiler and mechanical room: taking flue-gas O2/CO readings with a combustion analyzer and checking boiler-room CO and combustion-air supply, then adjusting the burner air-fuel ratio (air damper/trim) and room ventilation so combustion products and room atmosphere meet safety and emissions codes.

Hazardous-gas ventilation zones such as an underground parking garage, loading dock or refrigeration machinery room: monitoring CO/NO2 or refrigerant levels and adjusting/verifying staged exhaust-fan operation to satisfy IMC 404 / ASHRAE 15 ventilation requirements.

Field airflow verification and physical adjustment: taking hood/anemometer readings at diffusers, grilles, lab hoods and outdoor-air intakes; then physically resetting balancing dampers above ceilings and in shafts, correcting damper linkages and fan belts/sheaves, replacing loaded filters, clearing obstructed intakes, and logging the results for the compliance file.

Complaint- or incident-driven indoor air quality investigation in occupied space: an odor, dust, vehicle-exhaust re-entrainment or humidity/mold complaint; walking the affected area with handheld CO/CO2/PM meters, tracing the source, adjusting the serving ventilation equipment, and re-verifying and documenting the fix.

Confined or non-standard spaces (tanks, pits, steam tunnels, boiler mud drums, crawl spaces): pre-entry atmospheric testing for O2/LEL/CO/H2S, rigging portable blowers and ducting to purge the space, and retesting until readings meet permit-required entry limits.

Assisting with waste/sewer line work inside the facility: snaking or jetting a clogged drain or grease-laden waste line, pulling and cleaning traps, strainers and floor drains, cutting out and replacing a section of cast-iron or PVC waste pipe with no-hub couplings, servicing sump/sewage ejector pits, then cleaning and disinfecting the area. On-site material handling and support for the plumber: carrying pipe lengths, fittings, a threading machine, torches and hand tools from the shop to the work area, staging materials, setting barricades and drop cloths in occupied corridors, hauling out old pipe and debris, and mopping up water at the end of ... job.

Assisting on an outdoor/underground water or sewer line repair on the grounds — locating the line, supporting excavation, dewatering the hole, handling repair clamps or couplings in mud, and backfilling. Site taken as found, weather and buried-utility surprises.

Daily maintenance round alongside the plumber in a large plant or campus building: walking the piping, pumps, valves and sump pits checking for leaks, drips and abnormal noise, reading gauges, logging readings and tagging problems for follow-up.

tasks.label: Fire coal furnaces by hand or with stokers and gas- or oil-fed boilers, using automatic gas feeds or oil pumps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gas-fired firetube or watertube boiler in an institutional/commercial building plant (hospital, university, office tower, food plant): line up the gas train, initiate light-off, confirm purge, pilot and main flame, set and modulate firing rate to load, watch combustion/stack and water level through the shift.

Dual-fuel or oil-fired boiler in an industrial plant: start fuel oil pumps and heaters (No. 2 or heavy oil), set atomizing air/steam, light off the oil burner, change over between gas and oil, and trim fuel-air ratio while firing.

Solid-fuel plant (industrial stoker-fired coal/biomass boiler or utility pulverized-coal unit): run fuel feeders/pulverizers or stoker, set grate speed and undergrate air, keep the fire bed and combustion within limits, manage continuous ash discharge and soot blowing.

Hand-firing a small legacy coal furnace with a shovel (old small heating plant, historic property, museum/heritage steam plant): build and light the fire, shovel and level coal on the grate, slice the fire, break and pull clinkers, bank the fire.

Firing upsets requiring hands-on burner work: flame-failure lockout with code-required manual reset, fouled oil nozzle or electrodes, plugged duplex strainer, failed igniter needing a hand torch light-off, fuel-supply problems found and cleared at the burner front.

Temporary/rental boiler brought in for an outage, emergency or renovation: trailer-mounted packaged gas/oil boiler parked in a yard, alley or jobsite, lit off and tended in place, sometimes outdoors in weather.

tasks.label: Operate mechanical hoppers and provide assistance in their adjustment and repair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine operation of a fuel/charging hopper at a coal-, biomass-, refuse- or stoker-fired boiler plant: watching hopper and bunker levels, starting/stopping feeders and conveyors, adjusting feed rate to match steam demand, keeping the boiler continuously supplied over a shift.

Keeping hopper material flowing: knocking down bridging/buildup on hopper walls, rapping or hammering, running vibrators, poking or air-lancing sticky wet coal, ash or lime in the hopper throat so the feeder does not starve.

Severe plug or clean-out: a fully plugged wet coal bunker, ash hopper or chemical hopper with ratholed/caked material needing lances, whips, hydro-blasting or confined-space entry, done during an outage in a hot, dusty, awkward space.

Charging hoppers with consumables: cutting and dumping 50-lb bags or totes of lime, soda ash, salt, sorbent or pellets into a feed hopper, clearing dust, verifying the screw/rotary feeder picks up the material.

Assisting a millwright/mechanic in adjustment and repair of hoppers and their feeders: lockout/tagout and isolation, removing access covers, holding and aligning slide gates, rotary valves, liners or actuator linkages, torquing bolts, replacing packing, then test-running the hopper.

tasks.label: Ignite fuel in burners, using torches or flames.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Light-off of a large industrial/central-plant watertube boiler: after purge, the operator inserts or fires an ignition torch/igniter at the burner front, cracks the pilot fuel valve, confirms pilot flame, then admits main fuel and verifies flame appearance. Hot, noisy powerhouse; institution-controlled premises.

Seasonal or routine startup of institutional heating boilers (hospital, campus, office complex) in a building mechanical room: operator lights gas pilots on one or more packaged boilers with a torch/lighter or spark igniter, holds the pilot valve, confirms flame, then places boilers in service.

Oil-fired burner light-off on older plant equipment: operator lights an oil-soaked lighting torch or gas lighting lance, positions it at the atomizer/burner throat, opens oil valve at low fire, confirms ignition and adjusts atomizing steam/air; soot, oil mist and higher hazard.

Relight after a nuisance flame-failure trip or off-hours emergency restart: operator resets the flame safeguard, re-purges, and relights the burner with a torch in a cramped, hot boiler room, sometimes at night with steam load waiting.

Igniting auxiliary combustion equipment with torch or portable igniter: flare or waste-gas burner pilot, incinerator/afterburner, deaerator or small package burner, often at an outdoor stack or in a service yard on the plant site.
